Prerequisites The Maya plug-in edition, with several objects selected in the viewport. Marquee selecting collapses parent and child objects of the same level to the topmost root, and one root object counts as one variant. The asset is a .zasset . Steps Select the objects to export in the viewport. Right-click the target asset → 「更新资产」 (Update asset) → 「批量添加变体…（每个选中物体一个）」 (Batch add variants…, one per selected object) . Choose a geometry format (at least one) and the thumbnail source in the export configuration, then confirm. Watch the progress dialog (cancellable): each row shows the current variant name, and with a playblast / render source the text notes that an image is being produced. Naming rules The variant name is the node's short name (namespace and hierarchy prefixes removed). Duplicate names get a number appended automatically: name , name_2 , name_3 … Thumbnails and selection sets Thumbnail source Behavior in batch mode Maya playblast / render Automatic images after each variant export (no per-item confirmation) Screenshot Not run automatically (needs manual framing); fill in later with 「更新变体」 (Update variant) When the batch finishes your previous selection set is restored, so nothing on screen is lost. If you cancel midway, finished variants are kept and unprocessed ones are skipped. Verify the result The closing message reads 「批量添加变体完成：成功 N 个，失败 M 个」 (batch add variants finished: N succeeded, M failed) . variants/ gains N <variant name>.<ext> files, plus matching .sicon files when images were produced automatically. All new variant entries appear under 「导入变体 / 版本」 (Import variant / version) in the context menu.

items.title: Overwrite a variant and append a LOD
path: Overwrite a variant and append a LOD
items.summary: When an existing variant needs a new shape or another detail level, do it in 「更新变体」 (Update variant) instead of deleting and recreating it; the shared textures
items.text: When an existing variant needs a new shape or another detail level, do it in 「更新变体」 (Update variant) instead of deleting and recreating it; the shared textures and materials never change. Entry point Right-click the asset → 「更新资产」 (Update asset) → 「更新变体 ▶」 (Update variant ▶) → choose a variant. The submenu contains: Menu item Effect Capture / import / Maya playblast / render / add / capture and add Redo that variant's thumbnail only, with the same entries as 「更新缩略图」 (Update thumbnail) 「覆盖（用当前选中）」 (Overwrite from current selection) Overwrite the variant with the geometry currently selected in the viewport 「追加 LOD…」 (Append LOD…) Add a detail level to that variant 「删除变体」 (Delete variant) Delete the variant (see "Variant management and deletion") Overwriting a variant Select the new geometry in the viewport (marquee selecting collapses to root objects). Right-click the asset → 「更新资产」 (Update asset) → 「更新变体 ▶」 (Update variant ▶) → target variant → 「覆盖（用当前选中）」 (Overwrite from current selection) . Confirm the prompt to finish overwriting. Only the geometry of variants/<id>.<ext> is replaced; textures and materials are untouched. After overwriting, regenerate the image in 「更新变体」 (Update variant) so the thumbnail matches the geometry. Appending a LOD Select the low- or high-poly object to use for that level. 「更新变体 ▶」 (Update variant ▶) → target variant → 「追加 LOD…」 (Append LOD…) and enter a level number from 1 to 9. The file is written as variants/<id>_lodN.<ext> and registered in that variant's lods in variants.json . LOD0 is the variant's own geometry ( variants/<id>.<ext> ) and needs no extra append. Afterwards 「导入变体 / 版本」 (Import variant / version) shows one more level menu for that variant (its own geometry plus LOD1 , LOD2 …). Verify the result Overwrite: the Script Editor reports 「变体「…」已用当前选中覆盖」 (variant "…" overwritten from the current selection) , and reimporting the variant in the scene gives the new shape. Append LOD: it reports 「变体「…」已追加 LODn」 (variant "…" got LODn appended) and variants/ gains <id>_lodN.<ext> . 注意 Variants do not offer the background (headless) render entry: that path renders a whole asset package, and a variant has no package of its own.

items.title: Variant management and deletion
synonyms: add a variant from a model file
items.summary: The variant management window lists every variant of the asset in one table with thumbnails, face counts and formats, and lets you import, add from files or del
items.text: The variant management window lists every variant of the asset in one table with thumbnails, face counts and formats, and lets you import, add from files or delete them. How to open it Right-click the asset → 「更新资产」 (Update asset) → 「变体管理…」 (Variant management…) . Interface Area Contents List Each variant shows its thumbnail, variant name (id) , face count, formats and LOD ×N ; Ctrl / Shift multi-selection is supported 「导入选中变体」 (Import selected variants) Imports the selected variants into the current scene one by one (double-clicking a row imports only that one) 「从文件添加…」 (Add from files…) Pick model files from disk, one file = one variant 「删除选中变体」 (Delete selected variants) Deletes the selected variants (with confirmation; the dialog shows the count for a multi-selection) Footer note All variants share the textures and materials in the asset root; the variant directory stores geometry only Multi-selection With the first row selected, hold Ctrl and click other rows to add or remove single rows; hold Shift and click to take a range. 「导入选中变体」 (Import selected variants) and 「删除选中变体」 (Delete selected variants) act on the current selection; both buttons are disabled when nothing is selected. Double-clicking one row imports only that row, regardless of other selections. Adding variants from files Click 「从文件添加…」 (Add from files…) and select one or more model files: *.ma , *.mb , *.fbx , *.obj , *.usd , *.usda , *.usdc , *.glb , *.gltf . Each file becomes one variant named after the file (without extension); duplicates get _2 , _3 appended. The progress dialog can be cancelled; afterwards it reports successes / failures and the list refreshes. This path only copies geometry and does not generate thumbnails; add images through the thumbnail entries in 「更新变体」 (Update variant) . Deleting variants Select one or more variants ( Ctrl / Shift ), then click 「删除选中变体」 (Delete selected variants) . The confirmation says 「只删除这些变体的几何体与缩略图，资产共享的贴图 / 材质不受影响」 (only the geometry and thumbnails of these variants are deleted; the asset's shared textures / materials are unaffected) ; a multi-selection shows the count, and the actual number deleted is reported afterwards. Verify the result The list refreshes immediately after adding or deleting, and the library in the main window refreshes too. The matching <id>.<ext> , <id>_lodN.<ext> and <id>.sicon files under variants/ are removed while the asset root's textures and materials stay. The version browser (double-click the preview on the right) also lists variant entries and offers 「导入此变体」 (Import this variant) and 「删除此变体」 (Delete this variant) .

synonyms: where to look up a menu
items.summary: One-line summary: this chapter is a dictionary that finds features by where they sit in the interface — even if you do not know a button's name, you can reach i
items.text: One-line summary: this chapter is a dictionary that finds features by where they sit in the interface — even if you do not know a button's name, you can reach it from its position in the window. How the chapter is divided Part Pages Covers When to open it How to use this dictionary 8.1.1, 8.1.2 How to read the dictionary, common interface conventions The first time you use the help Top toolbar 8.2.1 ~ 8.2.7 Search bar, refresh, quick tools, AI tools, panels and layout, Maya target, settings, help Before clicking that row of icons at the top Left navigation 8.3.1 ~ 8.3.6 The Category / Project / Favorites tabs, the library dropdown, the category tree and its context menu To switch libraries or categories, or change a category Asset area toolbar 8.4.1 ~ 8.4.8 Import from outside, create asset, breadcrumb, tag filter, view, sort, thumbnail size To import, export, change the view or sort Asset context menu 8.5.1 ~ 8.5.21 The menu on asset cards, detailed per sub-library such as materials, models and lights To import into the scene, update, delete or favorite Right panels and status bar 8.6.1 ~ 8.8.3 Properties panel, preview panel, status bar, AI area, recycle bin To edit fields, view the preview, find the recycle bin Windows and dialogs 8.9.1 ~ 8.15.3 Settings window, export dialog, batch windows, AI windows, quick tool windows A menu opened a window Index 8.16.1, 8.16.2 Find menus by task, pinyin index of menu items You do not know which page to start from Two ways to look things up By position (recommended) : find the area on the window first (top / left / center / right), go to the matching page from the table above, then find the row in that page's menu table. By wording : search in plain language in the help center search box (for example "import model", "button is gray", "what is in the right-click menu"). Each page's keywords / synonyms are written the way people speak, so you never need to memorize the official UI names. By task : when you only know what you want to do, use the "I want to…" list in 8.16.1 to work back to the menu location. What every page looks like Menu pages follow the same sections, and reading them in order matches the order of operations: Section What it answers One-line summary Where this menu or button appears and what it governs How to open it Which steps lead to it from the window (including prerequisites) Menu screenshot What the menu looks like (provided when a screenshot exists) Item-by-item table One row per item: effect / prerequisite / what happens on click / notes Submenu section Items with ▶ get their next level listed item by item too Beginner pitfalls What to check when nothing happens, when something cannot be found, or when you fear breaking things Related Other pages on the same topic Read the four table columns like this: Effect : what the item actually does, in one sentence. Prerequisite : the state it needs to be meaningful (for example a category is selected, Maya is online, objects are selected). What happens on click : what you see change immediately in the UI (dialog / progress / new node / new card). Notes : whether it overwrites, whether it can be undone, and which settings it interacts with. How to read numbered screenshots Numbers on the image run left to right, top to bottom ; the numbers below the image or in the table correspond one to one. Screenshots without numbers are photos of the whole menu; table rows follow the menu from top to bottom , so match them in order. Names in this dictionary always use the official UI text (for example "Import from outside", "Panels and layout") rather than invented labels. items.title: Common conventions for menus, buttons and dialogs
path: Common conventions for menus, buttons and dialogs
synonyms: what does a check mark mean
items.summary: One-line summary: every page that follows uses these symbols and states, so learn them once here and no other page has to explain them again. Grayed-out item =
items.text: One-line summary: every page that follows uses these symbols and states, so learn them once here and no other page has to explain them again. Grayed-out item = not available now A grayed-out (unclickable) menu item or button is not broken; it means the current state does not meet its prerequisite . Common causes: Symptom Cause What to do "Create asset" and "Import from outside" are gray You are on the All assets page or in the recycle bin, so there is no definite target category Select a specific category in the left tree first; leave the recycle bin "Create asset" is missing entirely You are in the Images or Audio category — those assets are files themselves, so "create from scene" does not apply Switch to materials / models / lights and similar categories A few items are missing from the context menu The current asset's sub-library does not support them, or they are hidden in settings Check the page for that sub-library; add or remove items in 8.9.5 The whole menu is one gray line The feature is not ready yet (for example "Initializing..." in the AI tools menu) Wait for the interface to finish loading A general rule: hovering over a grayed item usually shows what it needs ; if clicking does nothing, suspect an unmet prerequisite before blaming the plug-in. Checked (✓) = currently in effect In the view menu , only one of "Icons / List" can apply; the menu does not show a check, so read the toolbar button text for the current view. In the sort menu , "Name / Type / Category / Time" is the current sort key (see the toolbar button text); the direction comes from the blue arrow on the button, and "Ascending / Descending" in the menu carry no check mark. Lock items in the Panels and layout menu: checked = the layout is locked , and the item then reads "Unlock layout". In the Maya target menu the check sits on the currently selected Maya instance row; with the default "Auto select (prefer newest)" the instance the plug-in picked carries the check. ▶ = there is another level An item with ▶ does not run immediately but opens another submenu . In this dictionary such items get their own section on the page, listing every item of the next level in a table. For example "Panels and layout → New panel ▶". An ellipsis after the name = clicking opens a dialog Clicking opens a dialog or window where you fill in content, choose a path and confirm. Items without an ellipsis usually take effect immediately (for example switching the view or the sort). Separators = groups by type of action Horizontal lines inside one menu usually group like this: common actions → dangerous actions → view / layout settings. A separator cannot be clicked; it only says "the things above and below are not the same kind". Menus with a dashed line at the top can be "torn off" The AI tools , Quick tools and Panels and layout dropdowns have a dashed line at the top: drag down from the dashed line and the menu becomes a floating window you can keep on screen and click repeatedly. Closing the floating window does not affect the main window, and its contents are exactly the same as the dropdown. Fixed mouse and keyboard behavior Action Effect Single click Select an object / select a category (one click on an asset card selects it; a second click runs the default action) Double-click an asset card Run the "double-click command" (change the default in Settings → Context menu, see 8.9.5 ) Right-click Open the menu for that object (asset cards, category nodes and empty space all differ) Ctrl / Shift + click Multi-select (several categories filter together; several assets are batch-operated) Ctrl + wheel Zoom asset cards in the icon view (the same as the thumbnail slider on the toolbar) Enter Run the search from the search box Click ✕ at the right of the input box Cancel the current search / clear the filter and restore all assets of the current category Which operations can be undone (important) Operation Undoable How Delete an asset ("Move to recycle bin") Yes Recycle bin on

items.title: Toolbar overview and button index
synonyms: what are those icons on top
items.summary: One-line summary: the whole top row is both toolbar and title bar — collapsing and search on the left; refresh, AI tools, quick tools, panels and layout, mainte
items.text: One-line summary: the whole top row is both toolbar and title bar — collapsing and search on the left; refresh, AI tools, quick tools, panels and layout, maintenance, Maya target, settings and help on the right; the window controls in the far corner. Where the toolbar is and how to use it The toolbar is always the top strip of the window and needs no "opening". Three general rules: All buttons are icons only ; hover to see the Chinese name and a description. The toolbar is also the drag area : there is a blank strip on each side of the search box, and dragging it moves the whole window; double-click the blank area to maximize or restore. Menu buttons (with a dropdown arrow) open a menu on click and never run an action directly. Left to right: button index Position Control What it opens / does Details Far left Squirrel icon Brand mark; hover to see the full title and version (such as "Squirrel Asset Manager - version 1.0.0") This page Right of the icon Collapse / expand left sidebar Shrinks left navigation to a narrow icon strip and expands it again; it does not close the panel 8.2.2 ① Search box Search by name / tag / ID; tick AI search to search with a sentence 8.2.3 ① inside the left of the search box Upload, screenshot, screen recording (recording in the audio category) Search by image, search animation by frame, search audio by sound 8.2.3 ① right of the search box AI search checkbox Switch between plain keyword search and AI semantic search (on by default) 8.2.3 ② Refresh Reload the current asset library (on the favorites page it refreshes favorites) 8.2.4 ③ AI tools ▾ AI thumbnail analysis / AI search preview / AI assistant / stop AI broker service 8.2.7 ④ Quick tools ▾ Run the 10 tools in the quicktools directory (including the script browser) 8.2.6 ⑤ Panels and layout ▾ New panel, new area, reset layout, lock / unlock layout 8.2.5 ⑥ Maintenance ▾ Rebuild asset index, fill in missing thumbnails, clean invalid assets, export diagnostic log, restore historical versions 8.2.8 ⑦ Maya target ▾ Choose which Maya to drive when several are open; only appears in the standalone edition when not mounted by Maya 8.2.4 ⑧ Settings Open the settings window (AI / font size / language / asset library…) 8.2.4 , 8.9.1 ⑨ Help Open the help center; falls back to the legacy help page when unavailable 8.2.4 , 8.15.1 Far right (unnumbered) Collapse / expand right sidebar Shrinks the right properties / preview panels to a narrow strip and expands them again 8.2.2 Outside the toolbar card (unnumbered) Window controls Minimize (to a floating icon), maximize / restore, close 8.2.2 Two easy misreadings "Maya target" is not always there : when running inside Maya the plug-in already lives in Maya, and a standalone edition mounted by Maya has its target locked — neither form shows the button, which is normal and not a missing feature. The blank space beside the search box is not a button : it is the drag area and dragging it moves the window; the search box tries to stay centered, so both blanks are always equally wide. Beginner pitfalls Clicking an icon "does nothing" : buttons with ▾ only open a menu; you then click an item in that menu. Cannot find "Maya target" : first confirm you are in the standalone edition and did not start it from inside Maya (see the previous section). The toolbar got dragged around / panel titles disappeared : the toolbar is not at fault; open 8.2.5 and click Reset layout to restore the default. Related Item-by-item notes for each button: 8.2.2 ~ 8.2.7 . Where the toolbar sits in the whole interface (introductory version): 3.1.2 .

synonyms: how to hide the left bar
does the plug-in exit when I close it
where did it go after minimizing
items.summary: One-line summary: besides the toolbar buttons, the top row also holds two sidebar toggles and the window controls — they govern what the window looks like, and
items.text: One-line summary: besides the toolbar buttons, the top row also holds two sidebar toggles and the window controls — they govern what the window looks like, and change nothing in the asset library. How to open them Nothing to open; they are always at the top of the window: Collapse / expand left sidebar : the fold icon at the far left of the toolbar, right of the squirrel icon. Collapse / expand right sidebar : the fold icon at the far right of the toolbar. Minimize / maximize / close : the three square buttons outside the toolbar card, hugging the window's right corner. Hovering any button shows its Chinese name (such as "Collapse/expand left sidebar", "Minimize (to floating icon)"). Item-by-item details Button Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Collapse / expand left sidebar Toggles left navigation between the full bar and a narrow icon strip None Collapsed shows a single column of icons (Category / Project / Favorites plus top-level category icons); click again to restore the full bar It only narrows the panel and never closes it; the width is remembered for next time Collapse / expand right sidebar Hides the right-most column (it collapses the vertically stacked properties / preview panels together) At least two columns remain in the layout The right column hides and the center asset area widens; click again to restore the panels collapsed by this action With only one column left it refuses to collapse (there would be nowhere to dock), so an unresponsive click is protection; panels you closed yourself earlier are not reopened Minimize Shrinks the window to a floating icon on the desktop None The window disappears and a squirrel floating icon appears on the desktop Single-click the icon to restore; drag it anywhere; this is not quitting and background tasks keep running Maximize / restore Toggles between filling the screen and the previous size None The window grows or returns to its previous size The icon changes with state (maximize ↔ restore down); double-clicking the toolbar blank area does the same Close Closes this plug-in window None See "What closing actually closes" below It does not save the scene and does not affect the Maya scene What closing actually closes Closing behaves differently per form (Maya-embedded / standalone), so never assume it quits the program : Form What clicking close does How to reopen Maya-embedded (opened from shelf / menu) Only the plug-in window closes ; Maya and the current scene are untouched, and the AI assistant keeps following Maya Open the plug-in again from the shelf / menu Standalone with the AI assistant running (or starting) Collapses to a floating icon while the AI assistant and its process keep running in the background Single-click the floating icon; its right-click menu also has Open asset library Standalone with no AI assistant running Ends the whole plug-in process Start the plug-in again How to undo : in the Maya-embedded edition closing only closes the window and you can reopen at any time; in the standalone edition collapsing to the floating icon is restored with a single click. The action that really ends the process is Quit in the floating icon's right-click menu — it has no protection beyond a second confirmation, so avoid it while AI tasks are running. Beginner pitfalls The left sidebar "disappeared" after collapsing : it actually became a column of icons. Hover an icon to see its name, and click it to switch to the matching tab. Cannot find the window after minimizing : look for the squirrel floating icon near the bottom-right of the desktop or the taskbar and single-click it. If the window was fully covered, the icon may sit at the screen edge. Closing inside Maya and assuming Maya quit : it did not; only the plug-in window closed, and Maya and the scene are still there. The right sidebar will not collapse : your layout has been reduced to a single column and the plug-in refuses. Restore it with the toolbar's Panels and layout → Reset layout , see 8.2.

items.summary: One-line summary: the capsule-shaped input in the middle of the toolbar is the search bar — typing is keyword search, and with the upload / screenshot / screen
items.text: One-line summary: the capsule-shaped input in the middle of the toolbar is the search bar — typing is keyword search, and with the upload / screenshot / screen recording buttons on its left it means "take an image, a video or a sound and find similar assets". How to open it Nothing to open; it is always in the middle of the toolbar. Usage: Click into the input, type, and press Enter to search; Or click the icon buttons embedded on the left of the input (upload ▾ / screenshot / screen recording) for media search; The AI search checkbox sits on the right of the input and is ticked by default . Item-by-item details Control Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Search input Search by name / tag / ID; with AI search ticked it understands natural language None After Enter only matching assets remain in the grid An ✕ appears on the right when the box has content; click it to cancel the search Upload search (▾) Choose a local image / video / audio file and find similar assets of that kind AI search is ticked Opens a format submenu (below); a file chooser follows The button routes automatically to the matching search (image / video / sound) from the file type you choose Screenshot search Drag a rectangle over the screen and find similar assets by image AI search is ticked Enters rectangle selection and starts the similarity search once you finish Good for "a material / texture very much like this reference" Screen recording search Select an area, record it, and find similar animation by frames AI search is ticked and you are not in the Audio category Enters recording selection and searches once you stop Only appears in visual categories Recording search Records the sound the computer is playing and finds similar audio AI search is ticked and you are in the Audio category Starts recording; click again (or hit the limit) to stop and search It records system sound, not the microphone ; the microphone is captured only if the system plays it AI search checkbox Switches between plain keyword search and AI semantic search None Immediately changes the placeholder and shows / hides the media buttons on the left On by default; your choice is remembered for next time Clear ✕ Cancels this search and restores all assets of the current category The box has text, or a media search is running The grid returns to the full list Media searches (image, recording, screen recording) never write keywords into the box, so ✕ means "cancel this media search" Query thumbnail Shows the image / media currently used for the search A media search is running Clicking the thumbnail cancels the search Also appears when the query came from a dropped image / asset card Submenu: upload search ▾ Sub-item Description Upload image search Choose a local image file and find similar assets by image (common image formats are supported) Upload video search Choose a local video file and find similar animation by frames Upload audio search Choose a local audio file and find similar audio by sound The placeholder text changes The placeholder is not fixed; it reflects what pressing Enter will do right now: Current state Roughly what it says AI search ticked (default) Describe the asset you want in one sentence, press Enter for AI search AI search unticked Search name, tag, ID... In the Audio category Describe the sound / music you want in one sentence In the Animation data category Describe the animation you want in one sentence (frames / content) A media search result is already shown A hint that results are isolated, click ✕ to cancel You can also drop files straight in Drop an image / video / audio file onto the search box and it picks image search, video search or audio search from the actual file format, with no button needed first. You can also drop an asset card into the search box and use that card as the "similarity reference". Beginner pitfalls No icon buttons on the left of the input : AI search is not ticked. items.title: Refresh, Maya target, settings, help
synonyms: which Maya is the plug-in connected to
items.summary: One-line summary: four buttons at the right of the toolbar: refresh re-reads the asset library, Maya target decides which Maya the plug-in drives, settings open
items.text: One-line summary: four buttons at the right of the toolbar: refresh re-reads the asset library, Maya target decides which Maya the plug-in drives, settings opens the settings window, and help opens the help center. How to open them They sit on the right of the toolbar, in this order: refresh → AI tools → quick tools → panels and layout → maintenance → Maya target → settings → help (this page covers only refresh, Maya target, settings and help; the menus in between are in 8.2.5 ~ 8.2.8 ). Hovering an icon shows its name, for example "Refresh material library", "Choose the Maya to drive (used when several are open; each Maya gets a window thumbnail in the menu)", "Settings (AI / font size / language / asset library…)", "Help". Item-by-item details Button Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Refresh Re-reads the current asset library (category tree and asset cards) and throws away the thumbnail pixel cache before reloading The asset library is loaded The grid and category tree redraw from the latest content on disk; the status bar numbers update On the Favorites tab it refreshes the current favorites set and does not throw you back to the category page; it rescans .zasset packages on disk, but loose files do not become assets this way Maya target ▾ Chooses which Maya the plug-in drives (how it tells instances apart) Standalone edition and not mounted by Maya Opens the Maya list menu (next section) Not shown in the Maya-embedded edition or when mounted by a host, which is normal Settings Opens the settings window None Opens the non-modal settings window (only one at a time; clicking again brings the open one forward) Changes only persist after you press the settings window's own OK / Apply , see 8.9.1 Help Opens the help center None Opens the help center page in the browser If the help center cannot open it falls back to the legacy help page; if both fail, only the Script Editor logs it and no dialog appears Submenu: Maya target ▾ The menu rescans online Maya instances every time it opens, so a Maya that just started appears and one that just closed disappears. Menu item / row Description Auto select (prefer newest) The default. Without naming one, the plug-in picks an online Maya from the bridge ports; the check lands on the instance it selected (Maya 2025 in the example) One row per Maya Each row shows "Maya version + scene name (an unsaved scene reads 'Unsaved scene') + PID + port", with that Maya's window thumbnail at the start; clicking the row switches the target, and the current one ends with a ✓ (No online Maya found — start Maya first, or make sure its bridge port is open) A gray hint meaning nothing was detected Maya (bridge port not open) The process was detected but its bridge port is closed, so the plug-in cannot connect. Clicking this row does not switch the target ; it copies a repair command to the clipboard and brings that Maya forward — paste and press Enter in its Script Editor to open the port No frame captured / Maya minimized A hint in the thumbnail slot. Windows does not render minimized windows, so no thumbnail can be captured; clicking the row restores it and brings it forward Beginner pitfalls Changes did not appear after refresh : refresh rescans .zasset packages on disk and rebuilds categories, so a complete asset package you copied in by hand does show up; but loose files (unpacked images / models / textures) do not become assets this way and need the import flow, see 4.1.3.5 . Cannot find "Maya target" : you are in the Maya-embedded edition or a host-mounted standalone edition, so the target is fixed and cannot be switched here. Switched Maya but assets still import into the other one : check which row carries the ✓; the plug-in only uses that row's port. After switching, look at the status bar or export a test asset to confirm. Clicking Settings does nothing : it may already be open elsewhere (non-modal singleton); clicking again brings it forward instead of opening a second one. Related T

items.title: Panels and layout menu
synonyms: how to recover a messed-up layout
items.summary: One-line summary: when the interface is dragged into a mess, panels are closed, or you want another properties / preview panel, come here — it is both the layou
items.text: One-line summary: when the interface is dragged into a mess, panels are closed, or you want another properties / preview panel, come here — it is both the layout's main entry and its fallback. How to open it Find the grid-like icon on the top toolbar (tooltip "Panels and layout"), left of the dropdown arrow; Click to open the menu (no prior selection needed; it works on any tab). Item-by-item details The menu has 11 items in total (including New panel and its 8 sub-items). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes New panel ▶ Create another panel of a given type None Expands 8 sub-items (next section); after choosing a type it opens as a floating window Several panels of the same type can be open at once; to dock a floating window back, drag it onto the main interface Reset layout Restores the default layout None Existing areas are cleared and rebuilt by default into the three columns "navigation / assets / properties and preview" Cannot be undone ; your custom splits, ratios and floating positions are lost; asset library data is unaffected Unlock layout (reads "Unlock layout" when checked, otherwise "Lock layout") Locking forbids dragging / splitting / closing areas None The checked state toggles immediately; the menu rebuilds its text and icon from the current state each time it opens Checked = locked ; areas still work while locked, only layout changes are blocked; Reset layout still works while locked Submenu: New panel ▶ The submenu has 8 items : the first 7 are panel types and the last is an empty area. Sub-item Description Navigation Creates a left navigation panel (Category / Project / Favorites tabs plus the category tree) Assets Creates a center asset grid Properties Creates a properties panel (fields / tags / notes) Preview Creates a preview panel (thumbnail and action buttons) AI assistant Creates an AI assistant area (opens / closes the dsh chat panel) AI search preview assets Creates an "AI search preview assets" panel (chat-style natural language search) Script browser Creates a script browser panel (browse / run script assets) New area Creates an empty area whose panel type you pick later from the area header menu Submenu items always open as a torn-off floating window and do not dock to the main interface; to dock one back, drag it onto the edge of the main interface (this uses Qt's own docking mechanism). Beginner pitfalls A panel was closed / the properties panel is missing : no need to reopen the plug-in. New panel → Properties restores one immediately; if the whole layout is a mess, use Reset layout . Regretted clicking "Reset layout" : there is no undo. The reset rebuilds areas, so previous ratios, splits and torn-off windows are gone — you must arrange them again. Layout saving and restoring are covered in 3.2.5 . Areas will not drag or split : the layout is probably locked; check whether the menu item reads "Unlock layout" (= currently locked) and click it, see 3.2.4 . Thinking "Unlock layout" means "click to lock" : it is the opposite. The menu text says what will happen when you click it : "Unlock layout" means it is locked right now. Related How areas dock, float and tear off: 3.2.1 ; splitting and merging: 3.2.2 . Switching panel types and the area header menu: 3.2.6 . Saving, restoring and resetting the layout: 3.2.5 .

items.title: Quick tools menu
items.summary: One-line summary: the 10 batch tools behind the "tools" icon on the toolbar — conversion into the library, batch processing, material mapping and script browsin
items.text: One-line summary: the 10 batch tools behind the "tools" icon on the toolbar — conversion into the library, batch processing, material mapping and script browsing all start here. How to open it Find the tools icon on the top toolbar (tooltip "Quick tools: run the scripts in the quicktools directory"); Click to open the menu; Click an item to run that tool. Item-by-item details The menu has 10 items , one per script file in the quicktools directory (underscores in file names are shown as spaces). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes hdr to zasset Converts an HDR environment image into an HDR asset and adds it to the library An HDR file and target category are selected / specified Opens the "HDR to asset" window for preview and writing Pure file tool; runs without Maya; see 8.14.1 model to zasset Converts a model file (.ma/.mb/.fbx and so on) into a model asset Model file and target category chosen Opens the "Model to asset" window See 8.14.2 pbr to zasset Packs a set of PBR textures (basecolor / roughness / normal…) into a material asset Texture name suffixes must be recognizable (suffixes can be changed in settings) Opens the "PBR textures to asset" window See 8.14.3 Image format conversion tool Batch-converts images to another format / color space Source folder and output settings chosen Opens the "Image format conversion" window Pure file tool; does not depend on Maya; see 8.14.4 Batch process Maya files Batch-processes .ma/.mb files (open, clean, save as and so on) A list of files to process is chosen Opens the "Batch process Maya files" window See 8.14.5 Batch mirror copy Batch-mirrors and copies models / objects Objects and mirror axis chosen Opens the "Batch mirror copy" window Pure file / scene tool, see 8.14.6 Material import/export (material management) Imports and exports materials between the library and the scene, and manages them in batch Materials or assets selected Opens the "Material import/export" window See 8.14.7 Material node attribute mapping tool Maps the attributes of one material node type onto another (across renderers) Source / target material types specified Opens the "Material node attribute mapping" window See 8.14.8 Material conversion tool Converts materials across renderers (Arnold / Redshift / V-Ray…) Materials selected or specified in the scene Opens the "Material conversion" window See 8.14.9 Script browser Browse / search / run script assets None Opens the script browser panel or window The same feature as New panel → Script browser ; see 8.14.10 Submenus This menu has no second level (all 10 items either run directly or open the matching tool window; nothing has ▶). Where this menu comes from The contents are not hard-coded : every time it opens, the .py files in the quicktools directory are scanned and rebuilt in file-name order. So dropping a script into that directory makes it appear the next time you open the button; when the directory is empty a gray line reads "No quick tools". The menu has a dashed line at the top and can be torn off into a floating window for repeated clicks. Differences between the plug-in edition and the standalone edition Form Where tools run Maya-embedded edition In place, in the local Maya Python Standalone edition Tools that need Maya are dispatched to the Maya selected in Maya target ; pure file tools (such as Image format conversion tool , Batch mirror copy and the three to-zasset tools) run locally Beginner pitfalls Clicking does nothing / just a flash : most of these tools open their own window before running; if no window appears, check the Maya Script Editor log (the standalone edition also prints hints such as "no online Maya found"). "No online Maya found" in the standalone edition : confirm a Maya with an open bridge port exists and is selected in Maya target , see 8.2.4 . Clicking twice : this opens two tool windows / runs the task twice, so avoid repeating operations that write to the library. Assuming these are all the tools : o

items.title: AI tools menu
items.summary: One-line summary: the AI entry behind the "brain" icon on the toolbar — analyze thumbnails, chat-search assets, turn the AI assistant on or off, and stop the AI
items.text: One-line summary: the AI entry behind the "brain" icon on the toolbar — analyze thumbnails, chat-search assets, turn the AI assistant on or off, and stop the AI broker all live here. How to open it Find the brain icon on the top toolbar (tooltip "AI tools: analyze assets / AI search preview / AI assistant"); Click to open the menu, then click an item. Item-by-item details The menu has 5 items (including one gray placeholder); when the AI chat panel is already open an extra Recall AI panel item appears in the middle (making 6). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes AI thumbnail analysis Lets AI look at thumbnails and suggest category / tags / Chinese name / notes Assets are selected; AI dependencies are available Opens the "AI analyze assets" window and starts analyzing The text changes with the selection: with a selection it reads "AI thumbnail analysis (N selected assets)", without one it reads "AI thumbnail analysis (right-click asset → AI analysis)" — clicking it with nothing selected tells you to select assets in the grid first ; see 8.13.3 AI search preview assets Opens the chat-style natural language search surface where you see matches while chatting AI dependencies are available Opens the "AI search preview assets" panel / window Complements AI search in the search bar: this one supports multi-turn dialogue and reference images; see 4.5.5.3 AI assistant (text follows state) Turns the dsh chat panel on / off None (the first use guides you through installing dsh) AI assistant starts the chat panel; when it is already open the text becomes Close AI assistant and clicking it closes the panel Whether the chat panel stays in Maya or opens in a browser is decided in settings, see 8.9.3 ; while starting it shows "Starting AI assistant…" Recall AI panel Brings the already running AI chat panel back into view The chat panel is running (state: on) Reuses the existing service to show the chat panel again Only appears when the chat panel is running; it neither restarts the service nor kills the process Stop AI broker service Stops the resident AI broker process The broker is running Stops immediately; AI features in the menu become unavailable afterwards AI tasks in progress are interrupted; the next AI feature starts the broker again automatically Add more AI tools to this menu... Gray placeholder hint — Not clickable Only says the menu can be extended; it is not a broken item The menu has a dashed line at the top and can be torn off into a floating window for repeated clicks. Submenus This menu has no second level (nothing has ▶; every item either opens a window or runs directly). About "Initializing..." When the interface has just opened and the asset grid is not ready, the whole menu shows only a gray "Initializing..." line and nothing can be clicked. Wait for the main interface to finish loading and click again; no restart is needed. Beginner pitfalls "AI thumbnail analysis" does nothing : read the menu text — if it says "(right-click asset → AI analysis)" nothing is selected, so select one or more assets in the grid first. All AI features are unclickable / dependencies are reported missing : the local AI dependencies are not installed; go to Settings → AI and run AI dependency check and one-click install , see 8.9.3 . The AI assistant will not open : the first use requires installing dsh, and the plug-in shows an install guide, see 8.13.6 . Mistaking "Stop AI broker service" for closing the menu : it really stops the service, cutting off running AI analyses / searches; the next AI feature starts it again automatically. Related Full usage of AI analysis: 4.5.4.1 . Opening / recalling / stopping the AI assistant: 4.5.3.3 . The AI search preview assets panel: 4.5.5.3 . The overall toolbar index: 8.2.1 .

items.title: Maintenance menu
synonyms: fill thumbnails for the whole library
items.summary: One-line summary: four kinds of housekeeping — fix the display, fill gaps, produce evidence and roll back — live behind this one button. It never touches asset
items.text: One-line summary: four kinds of housekeeping — fix the display, fill gaps, produce evidence and roll back — live behind this one button. It never touches asset content itself, only the manifest, thumbnails, invalid entries, logs and overwrite history. How to open it On the top toolbar, between Panels and layout and Maya target , is the wrench / maintenance icon (tooltip "Maintenance: rebuild index / export diagnostic log"). Click to open the menu; nothing needs selecting first. Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Rebuild asset index Deletes the on-disk manifest cache, rescans the whole library and refreshes the UI An asset library is open When done a dialog reports "N assets / M categories / took X seconds"; assets that failed to load add a notice Touches no .zasset and deletes no assets; with a large library it takes a while Fill missing thumbnails… Scans the whole library, lists assets missing a thumbnail or holding only a placeholder , and generates thumbnails headlessly for the selected ones An asset library is open Opens the "Fill missing thumbnails" window (all selected by default); Start generating leads to the background render options, then a separate mayapy process renders Read-only scan that does not touch the scene; rendering overwrites the existing thumbnails of those assets, see 8.12.8 Clean invalid assets Scans for invalid assets missing meta.json / holding only an empty directory , then repairs them or moves them to the recycle bin after confirmation An asset library is open Opens the "Clean invalid assets" window: open paths to check by hand, restore meta.json , repair all, or clean all (move to recycle bin, restorable) It never deletes directories automatically; only Clean all moves them to the recycle bin, see 8.12.9 Export diagnostic log… Packs logs, a desensitized configuration snapshot and the asset manifest into a zip None (reproduce the issue first if possible) Opens a save dialog (default name SquirrelAssetManager-logs-<timestamp>.zip ) and reports the path after saving Contains no asset file contents ; the configuration snapshot is already desensitized Restore historical version… Restores the old version kept before an overwrite export of the currently selected asset Select an asset in the grid first Opens the "Restore historical version" window listing history points; choose one and click Restore selected version History comes from overwrite export ; restoring also creates a new history entry, so a wrong restore can be undone again Rebuild asset index: when to use it Assets clearly exist on disk but are missing from the list, or the count does not match; You reorganized the library directory by hand ( not recommended ), or suspect the manifest cache is corrupted; First open after moving machines or copying the whole library. It means "read the disk again" — not "recompute thumbnails" — and it changes no asset metadata. Fill missing thumbnails: render the whole library Instead of right-clicking Background render one asset at a time, this item scans the entire library: Candidates are assets missing thumb.sicon or holding only a placeholder ; the two kinds are tagged "Missing thumbnail" and "Placeholder only" in the list; The list is selected entirely by default ; adjust with Ctrl / Shift; right-click offers Locate asset / Open asset path / Remove from list (removal affects this list only and the item returns on a rescan); Start generating first asks for renderer / preset model / environment light / size and quality ( 8.12.6 ), then a separate mayapy process renders in batch (progress window in 8.12.7 ); Rendering overwrites those assets' existing thumbnails; the job runs in the background and does not occupy the current Maya viewport. The older "fill geometry formats" entry has been removed: format conversion needs source geometry, so with zero geometry there is nothing to fill. Per-asset format conversion is still under right-click Format conversion ( 8.5.16

items.title: Navigation area overview and the three tabs
path: Navigation area overview and the three tabs
items.summary: One-line summary: this vertical strip on the left is the master switch for "which library, which type, which folder you browse" — three tabs give three entry se
items.text: One-line summary: this vertical strip on the left is the master switch for "which library, which type, which folder you browse" — three tabs give three entry sets, with the category tree and the recycle bin below. How to open it It is always on the left of the window and needs no "opening". If the whole column is gone, first check whether it was collapsed into a narrow icon strip (the fold button at the far left of the toolbar, see 8.2.2 ). What this column holds, top to bottom Position Control Effect Details Title bar "Navigation" plus the fold button Shows the name of this block; the fold button collapses / expands the whole column into a narrow icon strip 8.2.2 Tab row Category / Project / Favorites Three entry sets: the main asset library, the current project's library, favorites This page Top of the Category tab Library dropdown Switches between several main asset libraries 8.3.2 Body of the Category tab Category tree All assets / sub-libraries / categories / sub-categories / scripts, deciding which assets the grid shows 8.3.3 Bottom left of the category tree Recycle bin (with count) Opens the recycle bin view to restore or permanently delete deleted assets 8.8.3 Project tab Create / refresh plus the project library category tree Manages the project library that follows the current Maya project 8.3.5 Favorites tab Favorites list plus "+" Browses assets you marked, per favorites set 8.3.6 What the three tabs are Tab What the library is What the center grid shows after switching Good for Category The main asset library (a globally reused library; several can be configured) The selected category in the current main library Daily asset lookup, import and export Project The project library : the SquirrelLib folder inside the current Maya project directory Categories of the project library Assets that belong only to this project and travel with it Favorites Favorites ( stored per library ; main-library favorites and project-library favorites do not mix) Assets inside the selected favorites set Keeping a few frequently used assets together Right of the tab row is the collapse / expand entry for the whole column (at the far left of the toolbar, see 8.2.2 ); collapsed it shows a single column of icons (the three tabs plus top-level category icons) with the same features. Which page covers clicks and right-clicks Clicking any tab / node → the center grid follows; behavior rules in 8.3.3 . Right-clicking a category tree node → different nodes show different menus, see 8.3.4.1 ~ 8.3.4.4 . Right-clicking a favorites set → adding, editing and deleting favorites, see 8.3.6 . Beginner pitfalls The whole left column vanished : 99% of the time it was collapsed. Click the fold button at the far left of the toolbar; if that fails use Panels and layout → Reset layout ( 8.2.5 ). Assets seem fewer after switching tabs : each tab maps to a different library / favorites set, so the contents differ by design; assets are not lost. Changed a category on the Favorites tab and found no change back on the Category tab : the two tabs operate on different libraries; check which tab you are on. The recycle bin is not in the tree : it is a separate entry button at the bottom left of the category tree, not a category node. Related The complete tutorial for left navigation: 4.1.2 . Click behavior of each category tree node: 8.3.3 .

items.title: Asset library dropdown
items.summary: One-line summary: the dropdown at the very top of the Category tab switches between main asset libraries — switching libraries means switching the whole categor
items.text: One-line summary: the dropdown at the very top of the Category tab switches between main asset libraries — switching libraries means switching the whole category tree and asset set. How to open it Left navigation → click the Category tab; Click the dropdown at the top of the tab (it shows "library name — library path"); Click another library in the expanded list. Item-by-item details The number of items equals how many asset libraries you configured in settings (2 in the example environment). Every row is formatted as "library name — full library path". Menu item / row Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Current library (the one shown in the dropdown) Indicates the library you are viewing The library is loaded — (clicking it does not switch) If you cannot tell which library you are in, read the path in the dropdown text Another library (one row each) Switches the main asset library to this row That path really exists Reloads the library: the category tree rescans, the asset grid switches to the new library's All assets , and the status bar numbers update Switching only affects the main asset library , not the project library or favorites; the currently selected category resets Submenus This dropdown has no second level : every row is one library, clicking switches immediately with no further expansion. Adding and removing libraries is not here This dropdown only switches ; it offers no add / create / remove / set default. Those live in the settings window → General page → Asset library management : What you want Where to go Add an existing library Settings → General → Asset library management → Add asset library , see 8.9.2 Create an empty library Settings → General → Asset library management → Create asset library Remove a library from the list Settings → General → Asset library management → Delete selected Make it the startup default Settings → General → Asset library management → Set as default Beginner pitfalls After switching libraries all assets and categories changed : normal. Each library has its own category tree and assets; this is "switching libraries", not "switching categories". Switch back in the dropdown to return. The library I want is not in the dropdown : it has not been registered in settings yet; go to Settings → General → Add asset library . Clicking another library does nothing but shows a warning : that library's path no longer exists (drive letter changed, folder moved or renamed). Restore the folder, or remove the invalid entry in settings. Thinking switching deletes something : switching only changes which library is displayed; it moves and deletes no assets. Related Complete description of several libraries: 4.1.11.1 ; creating a new library: 4.1.11.3 . Navigation area overview: 8.3.1 . The settings page holding Asset library management : 8.9.2 .

items.title: Category tree: node types and click behavior
path: Category tree: node types and click behavior
items.summary: One-line summary: the category tree is the asset library's "file manager" — nodes come in several types, and clicking one only filters the central assets withou
items.text: One-line summary: the category tree is the asset library's "file manager" — nodes come in several types, and clicking one only filters the central assets without changing them. How to open it Left navigation → Category tab → the tree in the body. It is always shown and needs no opening; when the library dropdown changes libraries, the tree switches to that library's categories. Node types at a glance Node Appearance What it represents What the grid shows after a click All assets Top row, with a total count after the name Every asset across all sub-libraries (not limited by sub-library categories) All assets of the current library Sub-library root Second level, with a colored icon (materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / HDR / animation / images / audio / animation data / node tree) One asset type All assets of that sub-library (including every category below it) Category One level under a sub-library root, folder-like A folder you created Assets in that category and all its sub-categories Sub-category Deeper levels, nestable A finer folder Same as above, rooted at that node Custom category Auto-created by the plug-in in some sub-libraries Catch-all for assets that belong to no specific category Same as a normal category; cannot be deleted Scripts Last row of the tree, code icon Not a disk category but the entry to the script browser The main area switches to the script browser (not the asset grid) Recycle bin A separate button at the bottom left of the tree (not inside it) Deleted assets / categories The main area switches to the recycle bin view The (N) after a node name is the number of assets it contains; no number means zero. Icon colors differ per sub-library so materials (pink), models (blue) and the rest are recognizable at a glance. What single-click, double-click and the arrow do Action Effect Single-click the node name Selects and filters : the grid shows only assets in that node and all its sub-categories Single-click the arrow in front of a node Only expands / collapses that level without changing the current filter Double-click the node name (when it has children) Expands / collapses that level (the special case is All assets : it expands or collapses every sub-library) Ctrl + click Adds / removes categories; the grid shows the union of several categories Shift + click Selects a contiguous range of categories Double-click All assets Expands / collapses all sub-libraries together and also switches to the All assets view Rules to keep in mind Clicking a category never changes assets : a category is only a filter view and an asset's home is decided by its folder. To move an asset between categories use Move to , see 8.5.15 . Multi-select shows a union : with Materials + Models selected the grid shows both; to return to one category, single-click a node normally. The Scripts node cannot be multi-selected with asset categories : it is an entry for a whole different view (it switches the main area away), so Ctrl-clicking it keeps only itself. Some sub-libraries are missing : the top-level category may be hidden in settings, see 4.1.2.4 . Where the context menus are documented In the same tree, right-clicking different nodes opens different menus, documented by node type across four pages: Right-click location Page The All assets node / blank space in the tree 8.3.4.1 A sub-library root node (materials / models / lights…) 8.3.4.2 A category / sub-category node 8.3.4.3 The Scripts node and the recycle bin entry 8.3.4.4 Beginner pitfalls The asset count did not change after clicking a category : that category may have no assets of its own and the count shows those in sub-categories; try another node. Double-click did not expand but changed the filter : the double-click window is fairly wide (about 800 ms), so two slow clicks count as two single clicks; the arrow in front is the safest. The tree is blank / only shows "All assets" : the library is still loading or its path is invalid; check that the dropdown points

items.title: The All assets node
synonyms: how to create a top-level category
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking the top "All assets" row (or blank space in the tree) opens a menu with a single item — Add top-level category — which creates
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking the top "All assets" row (or blank space in the tree) opens a menu with a single item — Add top-level category — which creates a new major category under the library root. How to open it Left navigation → Category tab; Right-click the All assets node at the top of the tree; Or right-click blank space in the tree (both locations open the same menu). This menu has exactly 1 item : Add top-level category. Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Add top-level category Creates a top-level category under the asset library root (in effect a new custom major category) The current library is loaded; you are on the Category or Project tab Opens the "Add category" dialog with folder name + readable name + type ; on confirm a top-level node appears at the root and is selected The folder name must not duplicate an existing category or a built-in sub-library (such as materials ), otherwise the dialog reports "Cannot create a category named …" and refuses; a new top-level category comes with a Custom sub-category for assets that belong to no specific category How to fill the dialog Field What to enter Notes Folder name The folder name on disk and the internal category id; English letters / digits are recommended Required; must not conflict with an existing category chain; it becomes the folder name and cannot be changed afterwards (the field is read-only in the later Edit dialog) Readable name The Chinese name shown in the tree May be left empty, in which case the folder name is shown Type Which asset type this top-level category behaves as (materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / HDR / animation…) This matters : it decides which context menu assets under this category get and which import modes they support; a wrong choice makes the Import / Create options behave unexpectedly Submenus This menu has no second level (one item measured, nothing with ▶). Add top-level category opens a dialog directly rather than another menu. Risks and how to undo Creating a category touches no existing asset ; it only adds an empty folder level. Created it wrongly: right-click that top-level category → Delete category (it goes to the recycle bin and can be restored), see 8.3.4.3 . A wrong folder name cannot be renamed here (it is read-only in the edit dialog), so you must delete and recreate — name carefully the first time. Beginner pitfalls Expecting to import / create assets by right-clicking All assets : you cannot. It is only the library-root entry and its menu only creates top-level categories; importing assets is in 8.4.2 . Right-clicking a sub-library root shows only 6 items with no "Add top-level category" : menus differ per node. On a sub-library root the item is called Add sub-category , see 8.3.4.2 . No idea where the assets went after creating : a new top-level category automatically contains a Custom sub-category, which is where created / imported assets land by default. Chose "materials" as the type and now want models : right-click the node → Edit and switch the type (this only changes the category's type tag and does not convert existing assets). Related Category tree node types and click behavior: 8.3.3 . The sub-library root menu: 8.3.4.2 ; the category node menu: 8.3.4.3 . The tutorial version of creating a category: 4.1.3.1 .

items.title: Sub-library root nodes (materials / models / lights…)
synonyms: why the materials category cannot be deleted
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking a sub-library root such as Materials, Models or Lights opens a category management menu — add a sub-category, open the folder o
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking a sub-library root such as Materials, Models or Lights opens a category management menu — add a sub-category, open the folder on disk, move it, change its display name, expand or collapse. How to open it Left navigation → Category tab; Find the sub-library root in the tree (second level, with a colored icon, such as Materials, Models, Lights); Right-click that node. Item-by-item details The menu has 6 items (separators not counted). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Add sub-category Creates a category under this sub-library The node is operable Opens a dialog with folder name + readable name (sub-categories have no type field and inherit the parent type); on confirm a new level appears and is selected The folder name must not collide with a name in the same category chain or with a built-in sub-library; see 4.1.3.1 Open folder Opens this sub-library's disk directory in Explorer The directory exists Opens the system file manager at that folder This is the entry for changing files outside the plug-in ; after manual changes, refresh or rescan in the plug-in to see them Move to... Re-parents this node At least two candidate parents exist Opens a "Choose target category" dropdown offering root or other top-level categories; on confirm the node moves It moves the whole category and its contents ; the target list never includes itself; move it back if you made a mistake — there is no automatic undo Edit Changes the display name and type tag The node is operable Opens a dialog: folder name ( read-only ), editable readable name, switchable type; on confirm the tree and breadcrumb update The folder name cannot change; changing the type only affects this category's context menu / import support and never converts existing assets Expand all Expands every level under this node The node has sub-categories Expands the whole subtree at once Display only, no filtering Collapse all Collapses every level under this node The node has sub-categories Collapses the whole subtree at once Display only, no filtering Submenus This menu has no second level (all 6 items run directly or open a dialog; nothing has ▶). Why there is no "Delete category" The 11 sub-libraries Materials / Models / Lights / Textures / Scenes / HDR / Animation / Images / Audio / Animation data / Node tree are built-in defaults that the plug-in relies on to decide how assets are used, so deletion is not offered. What you will see: Right-clicking one of these 11 built-in roots → the menu has only the 6 items above, no Delete category . Right-clicking a top-level category you created at the library root → Delete category appears (see 8.3.4.3 ). Even if you reach the deletion logic another way, built-in sub-libraries are refused with "built-in default sub-libraries cannot be deleted; hide them with Show in main UI". To keep one out of the left column: Settings → Sub-libraries and categories → clear Show in main UI (assets and disk folders remain). Beginner pitfalls Wanting to add categories such as "metal" or "wood" but right-clicking All assets : that creates a top-level category. To add under materials, right-click Materials → Add sub-category. The target you want is missing from "Move to..." : the dropdown only lists top-level categories and root ; moving directly under a deep sub-category is not supported. The folder name cannot be edited under Edit : by design — the folder name is the category id and changing it would break the index; only the readable name and type can change. Assets placed by hand via "Open folder" do not appear : refresh only re-reads registered assets; use import or category sync, see 4.1.3.5 . Related Category tree node types and click behavior: 8.3.3 . The context menu of a category node (one level deeper): 8.3.4.3 . Tutorials for creating a category, renaming and moving: 4.1.3.1 , 4.1.3.2 , 4.1.3.3 .

items.title: Category nodes (including sub-categories)
synonyms: can a deleted category be recovered
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking a specific category (the level under a sub-library and deeper custom categories) opens the "add sub-category / open folder / mo
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking a specific category (the level under a sub-library and deeper custom categories) opens the "add sub-category / open folder / move / rename / delete" set. How to open it Left navigation → Category tab; Expand a sub-library (such as Materials) and find a category or sub-category under it; Right-click that category node. Item-by-item details The number of items is not fixed ; it depends on the kind of category and whether it has sub-categories — measurements show 4 / 5 / 6 / 7 items: Menu item Effect Prerequisite (when it appears) What happens on click Notes Add sub-category Adds another level under this category Present on every category node Opens a dialog with folder name + readable name; on confirm a level is added and selected Sub-categories have no type field and inherit the parent type; duplicate names are refused Open folder Opens this category's disk directory in Explorer Present on every category node Opens the system file manager at that folder After copying in a complete .zasset package by hand, Refresh in the plug-in shows it; loose files never become assets automatically and need the import flow Move to... Moves the whole category under another parent Present on every category node Opens a "Choose target category" dropdown offering root or another top-level category It moves the whole category and contents; there is no automatic undo, so move it back if you err Edit Changes the readable name and type tag Present on every category node Opens a dialog: folder name (read-only), readable name, type; on confirm the tree and breadcrumb update The folder name cannot change; changing the type does not convert existing assets Delete category Moves this category together with its sub-categories and assets to the recycle bin Only on deletable categories : not the 11 built-in sub-libraries and not the auto-created Custom category Runs two confirmations (next section); after confirming, the folder disappears from the tree and its contents go to the recycle bin Risky: sub-categories and assets go along; it can be restored from the recycle bin, see 8.8.3 Expand all Expands every level under this category Only appears when the node has sub-categories Expands the whole subtree Display only Collapse all Collapses every level under this category Only appears when the node has sub-categories Collapses the whole subtree Display only Why someone else's menu has more or fewer items Node situation Item count Difference Auto-created Custom sub-category (no sub-categories) 4 items No Delete category — it is the catch-all for a top-level category and the plug-in forbids deleting it A category you created (no sub-categories) 5 items Adds Delete category Auto-created Custom sub-category (with sub-categories) 6 items The 4 items + expand all / collapse all A category you created (with sub-categories) 7 items The 5 items + expand all / collapse all Submenus This menu has no second level (nothing with ▶). It does have a multi-step flow though — the two confirmations for deleting a category, covered below. Delete category: two confirmations and how to undo Clicking Delete category runs two confirmations; answering No at either step aborts: Step Content Description ① First confirmation "Delete category "X"?" plus the number of sub-categories if any, plus "assets under this category will be moved to the recycle bin" A normal confirmation dialog ② Second confirmation A strong warning that the category and its contents go to the recycle bin (restorable from the recycle bin in the left column); the asset count is stated explicitly when there are assets Focus defaults to No to prevent slips; a confirm button Execution The whole category folder moves to the recycle bin and its parent category is selected It disappears from the tree immediately How to undo : open Recycle bin in the left column → find that category record → right-click Restore , see 8.8.3 . Note that restoration brings back the whole category , not asset by

items.title: Scripts category, recycle bin and other nodes
path: Scripts category, recycle bin and other nodes
keywords: recycle bin has no context menu
synonyms: how to open the recycle bin
items.summary: One-line summary: the "Scripts" row at the end of the category tree is not a disk category but the entry to the script browser; the recycle bin at the bottom le
items.text: One-line summary: the "Scripts" row at the end of the category tree is not a disk category but the entry to the script browser; the recycle bin at the bottom left is not a tree node either but a separate button. Both menus are short. How to open them Scripts node : left navigation → Category tab → the last row Scripts in the tree → right-click it. Recycle bin : left navigation → Category tab → the Recycle bin N button at the bottom left of the tree → left-click to enter the recycle bin view. Blank tree space : right-click an area of the tree with no node. Item-by-item details Scripts node (1 item) Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Open scripts directory Opens the folder holding script assets in Explorer You are on the Category tab Opens the system file manager at the scripts directory The Scripts node has no add sub-category / move to / edit / delete — it is not a disk category, so those operations make no sense Left-clicking (not right-clicking) the Scripts node switches the main area view: the center changes from the asset grid to the script browser , see 8.14.10 . Recycle bin entry (no context menu) Action Effect Description Left-click Recycle bin N The main area switches to the recycle bin view N is the current number of entries; the button stays highlighted blue while you are in the recycle bin Right-click Recycle bin N No menu appears (zero items measured) Restore / delete permanently are not done here; right-click a specific entry inside the recycle bin view Right-click an entry inside the recycle bin view Opens Restore / Delete permanently and similar See 8.8.3 Blank tree space Action Effect Description Right-click blank space Opens one item, Add top-level category Exactly the same menu as right-clicking the All assets node, see 8.3.4.1 Submenus None of these three entries has a second level (nothing with ▶). What goes into the recycle bin and what does not Goes into the recycle bin Does not Assets deleted with Move to recycle bin Things deleted with Delete permanently (files removed directly) Deleted categories together with their sub-categories and assets The main library and project library each have their own independent recycle bin Replaced / deleted versions and LODs (per the prompt of the specific operation) Files deleted by hand in Explorer Beginner pitfalls Right-clicking Scripts to create a sub-category : not possible; it is not a disk category, and scripts themselves are managed in settings / the script browser. Right-clicking the recycle bin does nothing and seems broken : by design, there is no menu there. Enter it and right-click an entry to get actions. Deleted items from the main library are missing from the recycle bin : check whether the current tab is Category or Project — the two libraries have separate recycle bins. Expecting a one-click empty recycle bin : there is no such button. Entries can only be deleted one by one via Delete permanently , which is irreversible, so read the confirmation text before acting. Related Category tree node types and click behavior: 8.3.3 . The recycle bin view and its context menu: 8.8.3 . The script browser: 8.14.10 .

items.title: Project tab
synonyms: what does the create button do
items.summary: One-line summary: the Project tab manages the asset library that belongs only to the current Maya project — it lives in the project's SquirrelLib folder, so swi
items.text: One-line summary: the Project tab manages the asset library that belongs only to the current Maya project — it lives in the project's SquirrelLib folder, so switching projects switches libraries. How to open it Left navigation → click the Project tab. The plug-in tries to load the project library automatically; when the project has none yet it shows "Project library not created". What this page offers Control Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Create Initializes the project library in the current Maya project directory The project directory has no SquirrelLib yet Creates the SquirrelLib folder and the standard sub-library directories, writes the library configuration and loads it It never overwrites existing assets; when a library already exists, clicking it simply re-confirms the directory structure Refresh Re-reads the project library from disk The project library exists Redraws the project category tree and asset grid from the latest disk content, keeping the current category where possible It rescans .zasset packages on disk (a complete package copied in by hand appears after refreshing); loose files still need the import flow Project library category tree The same tree as the Category tab (All assets / sub-library / category / sub-category) The project library is loaded Click to filter, right-click to change categories, same behavior as the main library Node behavior in 8.3.3 , context menus in 8.3.4.2 / 8.3.4.3 Recycle bin The project library's own recycle bin The project library is loaded Opens the project library recycle bin view Separate from the main library's recycle bin; items deleted from the main library never appear here Status hint Shows the project library path / "Project library not created" None — The path is "project directory / SquirrelLib" Where the project library lives Path = the workspace root of the current Maya project + SquirrelLib . In Maya you can query the project directory with cmds.workspace(q=True, rootDirectory=True) . The standalone edition (with no Maya running) reads its own current working directory — so the project library location there may differ from inside Maya; trust the path shown in the status hint. When to use the Project tab Scenario Which tab A set of assets reused across projects The Category tab (main asset library) Assets for this project only, packaged / delivered with it The Project tab (project library) Picking frequently used assets out separately The Favorites tab, see 8.3.6 The difference between the main library and the project library, and how favorites relate to them, is covered in 4.1.1.3 . Beginner pitfalls Switching here only shows "Project library not created" : that is the normal state (a new project has none by default); click Create . Assets imported on the Project tab cannot be found on the Category tab : they are not lost, they are in the project library; switch back to the Project tab to see them. Assets deleted on the Project tab are missing from the main recycle bin : the two recycle bins are separate; look in the one at the bottom left of the Project tab. The project library is "empty" after switching projects : the project library follows the project directory, so switching projects switches libraries rather than losing data. Related Tutorial for using the project library: 4.1.2.2 ; main library versus project library: 4.1.1.3 . Category tree node behavior and context menus: 8.3.3 , 8.3.4.1 ~ 8.3.4.4 . The recycle bin view and its context menu: 8.8.3 .

items.title: Favorites tab
synonyms: how to create a favorite set
items.summary: One-line summary: the Favorites tab is a set of favorite sets: collect frequently used assets to browse separately, without changing their categories or copying
items.text: One-line summary: the Favorites tab is a set of favorite sets: collect frequently used assets to browse separately, without changing their categories or copying files. How to open it Left navigation → click the Favorites tab. On switching, the plug-in syncs the current library's favorites data and selects the favorite set you used last. What this page offers Control Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Favorites title plus the + button Creates a favorite set None Opens an input for the name; on confirm a new row appears and is selected The name is only a label and may repeat within one library ; the plug-in tells sets apart by internal id Current library hint Shows "Current library: main asset library / project library" None — Favorite sets are stored per library : main-library and project-library sets do not mix Favorite set list Each row reads "set name (asset count)" None Click to select; the center grid then shows only that set The default set has a star and a bold name; other sets use a folder icon Favorite set context menu New / empty / rename / delete See the next section Opens a menu Right-clicking blank space offers only New favorite set Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes New favorite set Creates a new set None (present both on a list row and on blank space) Opens an input;
