on confirm a new row appears and is selected An empty name creates nothing Empty favorite set Removes every asset from this set The set holds at least one item Asks for confirmation ("Remove all assets from favorite set …?"); after confirming the count drops to 0 It only removes the favorite relation and never deletes assets ; assets stay in their original categories; the emptying itself has no undo, just favorite them again Rename Changes the set name The set is not the default set Opens an input pre-filled with the old name; on confirm the list shows the new name Only the display name changes; the assets inside are untouched Delete favorite set Deletes this set The set is not the default set Asks for confirmation; after confirming the set disappears and selection falls back to the default set It deletes only the set itself; the assets inside are not deleted from the library ; the default set cannot be deleted (but can be emptied) How to put assets in Three ways with the same effect (all just add a "favorite relation"): Drag and drop : drag an asset card onto a favorite set in the left column (the row highlights on hover) and release. Star : click the star on an asset card to add or remove it from the currently selected set . Context menu : right-click an asset → Add to favorite set , see 8.5.14 . Beginner pitfalls Assets are missing from a favorite set : check the Current library hint — you may have switched to another library (main-library favorites are not visible in the project library). Assuming assets were deleted after emptying a set : they were not. Emptying only clears the favorite relation and the assets remain in their original categories; to really delete assets use right-click Move to recycle bin , see 8.5.16 . Assets disappeared after deleting a favorite set : assets are never deleted, only the set. They do not appear in the recycle bin either. The default set cannot be renamed or deleted : by design, it is the fallback set; it can be emptied. Editing assets on the Favorites tab seems to do nothing : on the Favorites tab the star follows the selected set, and edit / move entries still work but mind which library you are in; confirm on the Category tab afterwards. Related Tutorials for favoriting and un-favoriting: 4.1.9.1 ; adding, editing and deleting favorite sets: 4.1.9.2 . Add to favorite set in the asset context menu: 8.5.14 . Navigation area overview: 8.3.1 .

items.title: Asset area overview
synonyms: that row of buttons in the middle
items.summary: One-line summary: the row above the center asset grid is the "asset area toolbar" — import and create on the left, where you are in the middle, and filtering, v
items.text: One-line summary: the row above the center asset grid is the "asset area toolbar" — import and create on the left, where you are in the middle, and filtering, view, sort and thumbnail size on the right. Where it is Below the title strip of the center block (the asset grid) there is a horizontal row of buttons, and it needs no "opening". It follows the current area: if you split the layout and opened several asset panels, each asset panel has its own. The recycle bin view reuses the same row (import / create / tags are temporarily disabled). Left to right: control index Numbers ①~⑦ on the screenshot match the 7 items in the table (numbered left to right). Music playback and result count only appear in some categories / filter states, have no numbers on the image, and their positions are described in the table text. Control Effect Details ① Import from outside ▾ Brings external files / folders / .zasset packages into the current category 8.4.2 ② Create asset Creates a new asset from the current Maya selection (opens the creation dialog) 8.4.3 Music playback ▾ (only in the Audio category when audio exists) Play / pause, previous / next, sequential / shuffle / repeat one / repeat all This page ③ Breadcrumb Shows where you are in "library → category → sub-category → asset → version / LOD"; click earlier segments to jump back 8.4.4 Result count Shaped like "Materials: visible/total", showing how many remain after filtering This page ④ Edit tags Opens the tag editor to filter the current list by tag 8.4.5 ⑤ Icons / List ▾ Switches between card view and table view 8.4.6 ⑥ Name ▾ (sort) Chooses the sort key (name / type / category / time) and ascending / descending 8.4.7 ⑦ Thumbnails: "Thumbnail:" plus a slider Adjusts card size (effective in icon view) 8.4.8 When things gray out or disappear State What you see Why Sitting on All assets (no specific category) Import from outside and Create asset are gray There is no definite target category, so the plug-in does not know where to import or create Sitting in the recycle bin Import / create / edit tags are gray; view, sort and thumbnail still work Assets cannot be imported into the recycle bin Sitting in the Images or Audio category Create asset is hidden Those assets are files themselves, so "create from scene" does not apply Sitting in the Animation data category The button text becomes Export animation This category can export a selected hierarchy from the scene as an animation asset All assets / favorites The music playback button is hidden Nothing to play Beginner pitfalls Cannot find the import button : it is above the asset grid at the far left, labeled Import from outside with a dropdown arrow — not in the top-right corner. Imported but nothing appeared : first confirm a specific category is selected (not All assets), then that the file format is supported by that category, see 8.4.2 . Changing view or sort also changes the recycle bin : intentional; the recycle bin shares view, sort and thumbnail with the asset page. Assuming the thumbnail slider works in list view too : list rows have a fixed height, so the slider mainly affects icon view (it applies when you switch back). Related Operating the center asset grid itself (select, double-click, rubber-band select): 3.1.4 . The asset context menu (where most features live) starts at 8.5.1 .

items.title: Import from outside menu
synonyms: how to bring external files in
items.summary: One-line summary: this button turns files and folders on disk into assets in the library — it is a dropdown, and which items it contains depends on the category
items.text: One-line summary: this button turns files and folders on disk into assets in the library — it is a dropdown, and which items it contains depends on the category you selected. How to open it In the left category tree, select a specific category (not All assets, and not inside the recycle bin); Click the dropdown arrow next to Import from outside at the far left of the asset area toolbar; Choose an import mode from the menu. Item-by-item details In the Materials category the menu has 3 items (separators not counted), exactly the three in the screenshot: Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Import from file Packs a project file (.ma/.mb/.fbx and so on) into a new asset The current category supports "file" assets; Maya is online (for thumbnails / dependency cleanup) Opens a file chooser (multi-select allowed), runs the packing flow and then adds asset cards to the grid It creates an asset and never overwrites an existing one with the same name; same-name behavior follows the name conflict setting, see 8.12.5 Import .zasset asset Registers a ready-made .zasset package (folder) into the current library A .zasset directory is selected Opens a directory chooser and starts import / copy Use this to move assets between machines; it fails when the package structure is not .zasset , see 4.3.6.4 Import textures Combines several textures into one PBR texture asset The current category supports textures; one or more images are selected Opens a file chooser, detects basecolor / roughness / normal and so on from suffixes, and combines them into one texture asset A multi-selection counts as one set ; when a suffix cannot be recognized it falls back to the name of the last file; suffix rules can be changed in settings, see 8.9.7 Submenus This menu has no second level (nothing with ▶) — the layer opened by Import from outside ▾ is the final menu, and every item opens a file / directory chooser directly. Items change with the current category The same button shows different items per category (the plug-in lists only the import modes that category really supports), which explains "someone else's menu has more items than mine": Current category Items that appear Materials Import from file, import .zasset asset, (separator) import textures Textures Import .zasset asset, import textures ( does not accept project / model files) Models / lights / scenes / animation / node tree Import from file, import .zasset asset HDR Import .zasset asset, import HDR Images Import images Audio Import audio Animation data Import animation data, import .zasset asset All assets / recycle bin The button itself is disabled (gray) and the menu does not open Not in the mood for menus? Drop files in Dropping files or folders from Explorer straight onto the asset grid is equivalent: the plug-in first checks whether the category accepts them and which import mode applies, then runs the same flow. Rejected files are explained in the log and in the dialog. Risks and how to undo Importing adds to the library and never deletes or overwrites existing assets (same-name conflicts follow your settings and may ask you to rename or overwrite). Importing writes to disk (copying / packing files, generating thumbnails), so large files or batches take time. Imported by mistake: delete the new asset with right-click Move to recycle bin (restorable), see 8.5.16 . The dependency collection policy (textures / caches) decides whether an asset is self-contained, see 4.3.6.5 . Beginner pitfalls The menu will not open / the button is gray : no specific category is selected, or you are in the recycle bin. Select a category first. The new card is a hollow shell / has no thumbnail : usually Maya is not connected or dependencies were not fully collected; see the prerequisites in 8.4.3 and the checks in 4.3.6.1 . Import textures brought in only one image : texture import follows the "one PBR set" logic and suffixes must line up; to place a single image choose Import images (Images cat

items.title: Create asset button
synonyms: how to save scene objects as an asset
items.summary: One-line summary: Create asset exports what is currently selected in Maya into a new asset in the library, so it needs a specific category and something in Maya
items.text: One-line summary: Create asset exports what is currently selected in Maya into a new asset in the library, so it needs a specific category and something in Maya worth exporting. How to use it Select a specific category in the left category tree (materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / animation / node tree and so on); Select the objects to export in the Maya viewport (the dialog opens without a selection, but export then has nothing to take); Click Create asset on the asset area toolbar; Confirm the configuration in the "Create asset" dialog and run the export. What this button does Item Description Effect Opens the "Create asset / export" dialog and exports from the current Maya scene into the current category Source of content The objects selected in the current Maya scene (in the standalone edition, the selection of the Maya chosen as Maya target ) Prerequisites ① A specific category is selected (not All assets, not a favorite set, not the recycle bin); ② the category is not Images or Audio; ③ Maya is connected (always true in-edition; the standalone edition must pick a Maya target); ④ the scene holds exportable data What happens on click Opens a non-modal creation dialog (fill it in while watching the scene); on confirm the export starts and a new card appears in the grid Notes It writes to the library (new folder + metadata + thumbnail); same-name cases follow the name conflict setting: prompt / auto rename / manual overwrite, see 8.12.5 How it varies per category Current category Button behavior Materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / animation / node tree Shows Create asset normally Animation data The text becomes Export animation and exports the selected hierarchy frame by frame as an animation asset ( .zasset ), with matching hints Images / audio The button is hidden (those assets are files themselves, so "create from scene" does not apply) All assets The button is gray (no target category, so nowhere to save) Recycle bin The button is gray Submenus This button has no dropdown (no ▾); clicking opens the dialog directly. Details of every tab / field in the dialog are in 8.10.1 ~ 8.10.8 . Risks and how to undo Create vs overwrite : the default is "create a new asset"; only when you choose an update / replace mode in the dialog does it overwrite an existing asset — read the confirmation before overwriting. An interrupted export can leave a half-finished asset (hollow shell / missing textures): confirm in the library that the card has a thumbnail and can be imported, and delete and re-export if not, see 4.3.5.1 . Undo: delete a new asset with right-click Move to recycle bin (restorable); overwrite operations rely on the backup / version mechanism offered in the dialog, see 8.5.16 . Beginner pitfalls The button is unclickable : check whether you are on All assets or in the recycle bin, and whether the category is Images / Audio (where the button is hidden). The exported asset is empty : nothing was selected in Maya before exporting, or the selection holds nothing exportable (an empty group, for example). Select in the viewport first. The standalone edition reports that it cannot connect to Maya : first choose an online Maya in Maya target , see 8.2.4 . The export does nothing / spins forever : large assets or thumbnail rendering are slow; watch the dialog and status bar and do not click repeatedly (it exports again). Related Export flow overview: 4.3.1 . Item-by-item details of the create / export dialog: 8.10.1 ; bottom buttons and results: 8.10.8 . The other way into the library is Import from outside , see 8.4.2 .

items.title: Breadcrumb navigation
synonyms: how to go back a level
items.summary: One-line summary: the "A › B › C" line in the middle of the asset area is the path of where you are — click an earlier segment to jump back, and the last segmen
items.text: One-line summary: the "A › B › C" line in the middle of the asset area is the path of where you are — click an earlier segment to jump back, and the last segment marks your current position (not clickable). Where it is In the middle of the asset area toolbar, right of Create asset and left of the result count. It is always shown and needs no opening; it changes when you click a category, enter favorites, or open an asset's versions / LODs. What each segment represents Segment Example Description Library root / All assets All assets › Materials › Metal The first part is the library root; All assets means across every sub-library Sub-library root Materials, Models, Lights… The current sub-library Category / sub-category Metal › Copper The category level you clicked into, possibly several Asset name Metal › Copper › openpbr_Aluminum_Brushed An extra segment after you double-click an asset to enter its asset scope Version / variant / LOD … › openpbr_Aluminum_Brushed › Versions › LOD Extra segments added while browsing versions / variants / LODs inside an asset Behavior of each segment Action Effect Notes Hover a clickable segment The text underlines and the cursor becomes a hand Only non-current segments are clickable Click an earlier category segment Jumps back to that category and refilters the grid by it Same effect as clicking that category in the left tree Click the segment before the asset name Leaves the asset scope and returns to the category's asset list This is the way "out of an asset's version view" Click the version / variant segment Switches between the version list and the variant list Only appears once you are in the matching scope Click the last segment (current scope) Nothing happens (bold, unclickable) The last segment always marks where you are What happens when space runs out On a narrow window the breadcrumb protects the tail (your current position is always visible) and compresses / omits earlier segments from left to right; when clipped, an "…" appears at the far left. Widen the window or collapse the side bars and the full path shows again. Submenus The breadcrumb is not a menu and has no dropdown or submenu; clicking a segment jumps directly. Beginner pitfalls Looking for a back button to go up one level : clicking the previous segment in the breadcrumb is faster. The path starts with "…" : normal; it means outer levels were omitted. Widen the window to see them. "The list disappeared" after double-clicking an asset : you entered that asset's asset scope (version / LOD views); click a category segment or the segment before the asset name to return to the list. The breadcrumb disagrees with the left tree : trust the breadcrumb — it reflects what the main area really shows (with several categories multi-selected on the left, the grid shows their union). Related Asset area toolbar overview: 8.4.1 . Selecting categories in the tree: 8.3.3 . The version browser and asset scope usage: 4.1.10.7 , 8.5.18 .

items.title: Edit tags tag filter
synonyms: what happens when a tag is deleted
items.summary: One-line summary: click Edit tags to open the tag editor and click tags to filter the list down to assets carrying them; it only changes the filter and never to
items.text: One-line summary: click Edit tags to open the tag editor and click tags to filter the list down to assets carrying them; it only changes the filter and never touches assets. How to open it On the right of the asset area toolbar, find the Edit tags button (left of View and Sort ); Click it → a non-modal "Edit tags" window opens (only one at a time; clicking again brings it forward); Click tag chips in the window to filter; the filter stays active after you close the window. What the window contains Control Effect Values / actions Notes Top hint "Click a tag to filter \ right-click a tag to delete" — Reminds you of both mouse actions Tag chip area The common tags of the current category type Left-click = select / deselect; right-click = remove from common tags Scroll when there are many tags; selections apply immediately New tag input plus Add Adds a new tag to the common tag list Type a name → click Add It only adds the name to the common tag library and does not tag any asset; to tag assets use Edit in 8.5.16 Clear filter Clears all tag filtering at once One click It also removes tag keywords from the search box, restoring the list Close Closes this editor window One click The filter state is kept; closing the window does not clear it Filtering rules Rule Description One tag selected Shows only assets carrying that tag Several tags selected Union : assets carrying any one of them are shown Combined with keyword search Keywords and tag filters apply together (intersection) Combined with a category The scope is first limited to the current category (and sub-categories), then filtered by tag inside it Visibility of the filter Selected tags are written into the search box as text , so you can see at a glance what is filtering; the ✕ at the right of the search box appears as well Clearing Click Clear filter , or the ✕ at the right of the search box (both remove keywords and tags together) Submenus The Edit tags button itself has no dropdown ; clicking opens the window directly. The only context item in the window is Delete (for one tag), which is not a menu level either. Risks and how to undo Tag filtering is fully reversible : Clear filter or ✕ restores everything and changes no asset. Right-click Delete on a common tag only removes that tag name from the common tag list (written to configuration); it never batch-deletes tags already applied to assets. To undo, add it back manually. Adding a tag likewise only extends the common list; deleting a common tag does not change tags shown on existing assets. Beginner pitfalls The word I want is not in the tag list : common tags are stored per category type (materials / models…) , so confirm the current category; if it is missing, add it manually. Clicking a tag changes nothing : the current category may simply have no assets with that tag; try another category or clear the keyword search first. Assuming multi-selected tags mean "all of them" : it is a union (any match), not an intersection. Assuming deleting a common tag removed it from assets : it did not. The assets keep their own tags; this filtering entry just no longer lists it. Trying to filter tags in the recycle bin : Edit tags is gray (disabled) there; tag filtering only works on the asset page. Related The tutorial version of tag filtering: 4.1.5.2 . Batch-tagging assets: 4.1.6.3 . Asset area toolbar overview: 8.4.1 .

items.title: Icons / List view menu
items.summary: One-line summary: two ways to look at the same asset list — Icons is a wall of thumbnail cards, List is a table with one asset per row; switching only changes p
items.text: One-line summary: two ways to look at the same asset list — Icons is a wall of thumbnail cards, List is a table with one asset per row; switching only changes presentation, not content. How to open it Find the view button on the right of the asset area toolbar (it shows the current mode : "Icons" means card view, "List" means table); Click it (it has a dropdown arrow) to open the view menu; Click the other item to switch. Item-by-item details The menu has 2 items and is either-or. The menu items carry no check mark — read the toolbar's View button text for the current mode ("Icons" = card view, "List" = table view). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Icons Shows assets as a wall of thumbnail cards None The grid arranges cards and the thumbnail size becomes adjustable (see 8.4.8 ); cards show the star and name, and audio cards also show a play button Use this to browse assets and pick by thumbnail; card size follows the window and the slider List Shows assets as a table with one per row None Switches to a table whose columns are favorite star / name / type / category / tags ; clicking the name / type / category headers also sorts No large thumbnails; row height is fixed, so the slider barely affects list view; good for comparing type, category and tags quickly Submenus This menu has no second level (only two items, nothing with ▶). What the two views share and how they differ Item Icon view List view Sorting Decided by the Name sort menu ( 8.4.7 ) Also follows the sort menu; additionally clicking column headers sorts Tag / keyword filtering Works the same Works the same Double-click Runs the default double-click command Also runs the default double-click command Context menu The asset context menu ( 8.5.1 ) The list row context menu (see 8.5.19 ) Thumbnail size slider Takes effect Barely affects it (row height is fixed) Recycle bin page The recycle bin reuses the same view switch and stays in sync Same Beginner pitfalls Assuming assets became fewer after switching to list : they did not; it went from a few large cards per screen to many rows. Scroll down. Cannot find a thumbnail adjustment in list view : list view has no large thumbnails, and the size slider mainly serves icon view. Sorting looks different after switching views : both views share one sort setting; if it really looks wrong, check which item the Name sort menu currently has. Switching views after multi-selecting : the selection follows the content, but the batch bar acts on what is currently selected, so confirm the count after switching. Related The tutorial version of view modes: 3.3.3 . Sort menu: 8.4.7 ; thumbnail size: 8.4.8 . List view and blank-area context menus: 8.5.19 .

items.title: Name sort menu
items.summary: One-line summary: the sort button on the asset area toolbar: its text is the current sort key and its arrow is the direction; click it to change the sort. How t
items.text: One-line summary: the sort button on the asset area toolbar: its text is the current sort key and its arrow is the direction; click it to change the sort. How to open it Find the sort button on the right of the asset area toolbar (its text is the current key, such as "Name"); Click it to open the sort menu; Click a sort key, or click Ascending / Descending to change direction. Item-by-item details The menu has 6 items in two parts (above the separator you choose the key, below it the direction). Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Name Sorts by the asset display name None The list re-sorts and the toolbar button reads "Name" The item carries no check mark; it sorts by the readable / display name, not the disk folder name Type Sorts by the asset's sub-library (materials / models / textures…) None Assets of the same sub-library group together Inside a type, assets keep a stable name order Category Sorts by the display name of the asset's category None Assets of the same category group together It uses the category display name (Chinese / readable name), not the category id Time Sorts by the asset files' modification time None Reorders chronologically It is file modification time, not "import time"; to find the newest import, sort by time descending Ascending Small to large / earliest to latest None Direction becomes ascending and the button arrow points up Direction items carry no check and no arrow icon : read the toolbar button arrow for the current direction Descending Large to small / latest to earliest None Direction becomes descending and the button arrow points down As above; clicking the same item twice does not toggle, so click the other item Submenus This menu has no second level (all 6 items apply immediately, nothing with ▶). In list view you can also click column headers After switching to list view, clicking the Name / Type / Category column headers also sorts (the time column is not in the header and needs this menu). Both routes give the same result, and the button text and check stay in sync. The recycle bin behaves the same The recycle bin page reuses the same sort button: sorting there only affects the recycle bin list, and returning to the asset page keeps the asset page's own sorting. Beginner pitfalls Cannot tell whether it is ascending or descending : read the arrow direction on the toolbar sort button; the Ascending / Descending items carry no check and no arrow, so do not look for one there. Sorted by time but the newest is not first : the direction is ascending (old to new). Click Descending . Name sorting does not match alphabetical order : names sort by display name (possibly a Chinese readable name), and Chinese order is not identical to English letter order. Selected assets disappeared after changing the sort : sorting only reorders the display and never changes the selection; if it really is empty, you probably clicked blank space earlier and cleared it. Related The tutorial version of sorting and filtering: 3.3.4 . View switching: 8.4.6 ; list view context menu: 8.5.19 .

items.title: Thumbnail size slider
items.summary: One-line summary: the slider after the "Thumbnail:" label at the far right of the asset area toolbar controls card size — left for smaller cards and more per sc
items.text: One-line summary: the slider after the "Thumbnail:" label at the far right of the asset area toolbar controls card size — left for smaller cards and more per screen, right for larger cards and clearer detail. Where it is At the far right of the asset area toolbar: the text label "Thumbnail:" followed by a horizontal slider about 120 px wide. It is always there and needs no opening; in icon view dragging applies immediately. What the two directions mean Drag direction Cards Columns per screen Good for Left (small) Smaller More, up to 16 columns Scanning the library quickly for general shapes Right (large) Larger Fewer, down to 2 columns Inspecting thumbnail detail and comparing material texture It defaults to about 8 columns. Internally the slider stores a "level": level = 10 - current columns , so more columns means a lower level. What happens after dragging Observation Description Cards rearrange immediately There is a short delay while dragging, then everything rearranges at once so the UI does not stall refreshing every card mid-drag A wider window adds columns first Card size is the "primary state"; a wider window prefers more columns rather than stretching cards The recycle bin follows The recycle bin page reuses this slider and the level applies to its cards too Restored next time The level is saved with the interface state, so the next launch keeps the same size It is the same thing as Ctrl+wheel In icon view, holding Ctrl and scrolling the mouse wheel also zooms cards: up to enlarge, down to shrink, with the slider moving in sync. Both change the same "card size", so either works. Submenus The slider has no menu and no dropdown; it is a continuous adjustment bar. Beginner pitfalls Dragging the slider does nothing : most likely you are in list view . List rows have a fixed height, so thumbnail size mainly shows in icon view; switch back to Icons. Thumbnails are too small to read : drag right, or Ctrl+scroll up. To return to default, drag to the middle-right (about 8 columns). Assuming the slider changes "the thumbnail file itself" : it only changes display size and never regenerates or modifies thumbnail images on disk. Column count will not increase on a narrow window : the column count is also limited by window width; widen the window or collapse the side bars first. Related Icon / list view switching: 8.4.6 . Basic asset grid operations: 3.3.3 . Asset area toolbar overview: 8.4.1 .

items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking an asset card in the asset area opens this menu; it is the main entry to plug-in features, and every sub-library's menu differs
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking an asset card in the asset area opens this menu; it is the main entry to plug-in features, and every sub-library's menu differs. This page first gives a "who has what" table, then links to per-item details per sub-library. How to open it On the left Category tab (or the Project / Favorites tab), click into any category; In the center asset area, right-click any asset card . Icon view and list view share the same menu: right-clicking a row in list view opens exactly the same contents. The image shows the materials menu. Other sub-libraries add or remove items on it — the top segment (import / reference / apply / convert) differs per sub-library, while the common segments below are broadly the same. The menu has 6 segments The order from top to bottom is always the same, and remembering the segments is easier than remembering items: Segment Content Description ① Sub-library specific Import / add reference / apply… / convert import / create material / import textures / create dome light / import to timeline… Only some sub-libraries have these , see the table below ② Favorites and selection Add to favorite set ▶, select all, duplicate, open folder Present in all 11 sub-libraries ③ Organization Move to ▶, copy to ▶ Present in all 11 sub-libraries ④ Maintenance Edit, update thumbnail ▶, update asset ▶, delete ▶, format conversion Update thumbnail / update asset are missing on images and audio; format conversion exists in only some sub-libraries ⑤ View and AI Preview node ▶, AI thumbnail analysis Preview node depends on whether the asset contains node files ⑥ Last item Asset details Present in all 11 sub-libraries, always at the very bottom The 11 sub-libraries: item counts and unique items Sub-library Details page Whole-menu item count Items unique to this sub-library Materials 8.5.2 228 Import (zmetal / ma), assign material to selection, apply material parameters, convert import (18 target types), preview node Models 8.5.3 203 Import ma, add reference, format conversion Lights 8.5.4 212 Import (zlight / ma), apply light parameters to selected lights, convert import (including its own type = restore in place) Textures 8.5.5 220 Assign material to selection, create material , import textures , assign texture to material, open image Scenes 8.5.6 205 Import ma, add reference, format conversion, preview node HDR 8.5.7 206 Import hdr, create dome light , assign texture, open image Animation (ani) 8.5.8 209 Import ▶ (ma / abc), add reference ▶ (ma / abc), format conversion Images 8.5.9 188 Import as file node, create imagePlane, assign to selected material slot, open image Audio 8.5.10 189 Import to timeline / time editor / Trax editor / camera sequencer, convert to WAV Animation data 8.5.11 207 Import animation ▶, import animation (hierarchy mapping)…, import to selected attributes ▶ Node tree 8.5.12 205 Import ma, add reference, format conversion, preview node (selects newly created nodes after import) "Item count" is measured with submenus and the Move to / Copy to category cascades fully expanded (same asset, same manifest). items.title: Materials assets
synonyms: what is in the materials menu
assign a material to a model
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking a materials asset card in the asset grid opens this menu. Materials is the only sub-library with all three entries — assign to
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking a materials asset card in the asset grid opens this menu. Materials is the only sub-library with all three entries — assign to objects, write parameters, and cross-renderer conversion. How to open it Left Category tab → click Materials or any category under it (metal / stone / skin…); In the center asset grid, right-click any materials card (you may also single-click to select first). Right-clicking a materials card on the All assets , Project or Favorites tab opens the same menu. Menu order from top to bottom Segment Items ① Sub-library specific Import ▶ (zmetal / ma), add reference, assign material to selection, apply material parameters, convert import ▶ ② Favorites and selection Add to favorite set ▶, select all, duplicate, open folder ③ Organization Move to ▶, copy to ▶ ④ Maintenance Edit, update thumbnail ▶, update asset ▶, delete ▶ ⑤ View and AI Preview node ▶, AI thumbnail analysis ⑥ Last item Asset details Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Import ▶ Imports the material into the current Maya scene Maya is connected; the asset holds zmetal / ma The submenu lists available formats; clicking one imports directly and selects the new material node When the current renderer differs from the material's source, a dialog asks whether to convert to the current renderer Add reference Brings the material's file in as a Maya Reference The asset contains a referenceable format such as .ma / .mb (the material's ma qualifies) A reference node appears in the scene and the material exists as a reference It references the file inside the asset package; moving or deleting the package breaks the reference Assign material to selection Assigns this material to the selected objects Objects (meshes / groups) are selected in the scene The selected objects switch to this material and their previous material is replaced It overwrites the objects' existing material; press Ctrl+Z once if you dislike it Apply material parameters Writes the asset's parameter values onto an existing material node in the scene (not an assignment) A material node is selected in the scene Same type writes values directly, different types convert through the mapping table first; the changed material is selected afterwards Cross-type mapping may drop parameters, see 4.2.5.4 Convert import ▶ Imports and converts the material to a chosen material type in one step The asset is a .zasset (otherwise a warning appears); the mapping table has a path to the target type Imports first, then converts to the target type and selects the converted material It only changes the scene material and never the asset itself Add to favorite set ▶ Adds the asset to a favorite set The asset library is loaded The submenu lists the default set plus your own sets; click to add, click again to remove An already-favorited set shows a filled gold star Select all Selects every visible card in the grid Cards exist in the asset area All cards highlight Only the filtered / searched results are selected, not the whole library Duplicate Puts the asset on the clipboard None The internal clipboard records the asset and the asset folder is written to the system clipboard To really duplicate, right-click blank space in the target category and choose Paste Open folder Opens the asset's location on disk The asset is a .zasset directory The system file manager opens at that asset folder It only opens the folder and changes nothing Move to ▶ Moves the asset to another category The asset library is loaded After cascading to a target category, the asset leaves the current category and appears in the target Cross-sub-library moves are allowed, see 8.5.15 Copy to ▶ Copies the asset into another category The asset library is loaded The target category gains the same asset while the original stays It copies the whole asset package and doubles disk usage Edit Changes the asset's Chinese name, category, tags and notes None Opens the "Edit asset" d

items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking a models asset card in the asset grid opens this menu. There is no "apply" item here — models only bring geometry into the scene, and materials come along with the asset. How to open it Left Category tab → click Models or any category under it (architecture / characters / props…); In the center asset grid, right-click any model card . Menu order from top to bottom Segment Items ① Sub-library specific Import ma / mb, add reference, import variant / version ▶ ② Favorites and selection Add to favorite set ▶, select all, duplicate, open folder ③ Organization Move to ▶, copy to ▶ ④ Maintenance Edit, update thumbnail ▶, update asset ▶, delete ▶, format conversion ⑤ View and AI AI thumbnail analysis ⑥ Last item Asset details Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Import ma / mb Imports the model geometry into the current Maya scene Maya is connected; items.title: Common items: import and reference
synonyms: how to bring an asset into Maya
items.summary: One-line summary: these two items are the front door for "bring asset content into Maya". How they look on the menu depends on how many importable formats the a
items.text: One-line summary: these two items are the front door for "bring asset content into Maya". How they look on the menu depends on how many importable formats the asset holds. Which sub-libraries have these two items Sub-library Import Add reference Materials / models / lights / scenes / HDR / animation / node tree ✓ ✓ Textures — (uses Import textures ▶ ) — Images — (uses Import as file node and similar) — Audio — (uses Import to timeline and similar) — Animation data — (uses Import animation ▶ ) — Sub-libraries without a generic Import are not unable to import; they each have a more specific entry — see their own pages. The three forms of Import on the menu Form When it appears Example Single row "Import <format>" The asset has only one usable format Models: Import ma ; HDR: Import hdr "Import ▶" submenu The asset has several usable formats Materials: zmetal / ma; lights: zlight / ma; animation: ma / abc Sub-library specific entry That sub-library's import is more than "import a file" Textures Import textures ▶ , images Import as file node , audio Import to timeline… , animation data Import animation ▶ Every submenu item is a "format name" (even with a single format the row reads like "Import ma"), and choosing one imports in that format. "Import ▶" may also contain "import version / LOD" When the asset is a master asset with versions, variants or several LODs , the Import ▶ submenu gains a block of internal items (the heading varies with content): Item Description Import variant / version ▶ (or "Import variant ▶", "Import version / LOD ▶") Expands the asset's versions / variants / LODs so you can import just one of them Version nodes (such as V1 , V2 ) The version itself; go in and pick its LOD or geometry format Variant Variant entries, whose label carries a face count (such as "— 12,345 faces") Main version The content of the asset's main version View versions / view variants / view LOD management Not imports but a switch of the asset area into an "internal view" that browses internal entries like folders The context menu of internal entries themselves (a reduced version) is in 8.5.18 . The two forms of Add reference Form When it appears Single row "Add reference" The asset has only one referenceable format "Add reference ▶" submenu The asset has several referenceable formats (typically animation's ma / abc) The referenceable formats are always this set: .ma / .mb / .fbx / .abc / .usd / .obj . When the asset holds none of them, the row does not appear. Import or reference? What you want Choose Why Edit geometry or material in the scene Import What comes in is real editable nodes Just place it / follow asset updates Add reference The scene stores only a path, so reloading picks up asset updates Keep the scene file small Add reference Content stays in the asset package and is not written into the scene The price of referencing: moving, renaming or deleting the asset package breaks the reference (the scene then reports a missing file). Importing has no such problem, but content enters the scene and later asset changes do not follow. What you see after clicking Import : content is created in the current scene; materials, lights and node trees select the newly created nodes automatically so you can keep working. When the current renderer differs from the asset's source, a "convert?" prompt appears once. Add reference : a reference node appears in the scene (marked as a reference in the Outliner) and the file itself is untouched. Clicking import / reference with a multi-selection : it runs once for every selected asset (same format), not only the one you right-clicked. Notes Import does not copy asset files : materials are still read from the package, so moving the package loses the textures in the scene. Name conflicts ask first : when a node with the same name exists, the setting decides (ask / auto rename / overwrite), see 4.3.6.1 . Where the docs say "Import", the UI may read "Import ma" : the same command with a different look;

items.summary: One-line summary: all 11 sub-libraries have these four, positioned right below the sub-library specific block. They only touch lightweight state such as selecti
items.text: One-line summary: all 11 sub-libraries have these four, positioned right below the sub-library specific block. They only touch lightweight state such as selection and favorites, never asset content. Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Add to favorite set ▶ Adds the asset to a favorite set The asset library is loaded The submenu lists every set (including the default set and your own); click to add, click again to remove Already in the set → filled gold star; not in it → outlined gray star Select all Selects every currently visible card in the grid Cards exist in the asset area All cards highlight and the properties panel shows the last one Only the filtered / searched results, not the whole library Duplicate Puts the asset on the clipboard None The internal clipboard remembers the asset and the asset folder path is written to the system clipboard This is not "copy into the current category"; you must paste to materialize it Open folder Opens the asset's disk location The asset is a .zasset directory, or an already-imported loose file The system file manager opens at that asset folder Opens only; changes nothing Submenu: Add to favorite set ▶ Sub-item Description Default favorites The built-in set, which always exists Your own sets Sets you created, listed here by name; each new one adds an item When no sets exist Only Default favorites remains Two details: State is visible : a set already containing the asset shows a filled gold star and others show an outlined gray star — no need to open it to check. Multi-selection applies to all selected assets : after multi-selecting, clicking a set adds or removes all of them together. What "Select all" really selects It selects the cards visible in the current view : after filtering tags, searching keywords or filtering by category, Select all only covers the result set. On the All assets tab, select all means every visible asset of the whole library (potentially a large number, so be careful with subsequent batch operations). After selecting all you can right-click for batch operations, see 8.5.21 . What "Duplicate" actually copies Layer Content Plug-in internal clipboard The asset id and the asset package path System clipboard The path of the asset folder (the .zasset directory) Therefore: Right-click blank space → Paste in the asset area copies the clipboard asset as a duplicate into the current category (see 8.5.19 ); Pasting in Windows Explorer copies the whole asset folder out (useful for backups or sending to a colleague). Internal virtual entries such as versions / variants are not duplicated — they are not independent assets. Which folder "Open folder" opens A .zasset asset: the asset package directory itself (holding meta, geometry, textures, thumbnails). A loose-file asset (images / audio): the folder containing the file. Once inside, do not casually rename or delete files : the library index points at these paths, and deleting them corrupts the asset. To free space, use Delete → Move to recycle bin . Notes Favoriting is not copying : favoriting only adds a reference in a favorite set and the asset stays in its category. A mistake after select all is a batch mistake : before batch deleting or moving, check that the status bar's "N assets selected" is right. Duplicating does not rename : pasting into the same category goes through the name conflict handling (ask / auto rename), see 8.12.5 . items.summary: One-line summary: these two are the only entry for "changing an asset's category" , structured identically, differing in one sentence: move to = take it away, c
items.text: One-line summary: these two are the only entry for "changing an asset's category" , structured identically, differing in one sentence: move to = take it away, copy to = make another one. What they look like Opened, they are a cascading submenu : the first level is the 11 top-level categories (materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / HDR / animation / images / audio / animation data / node tree), and each level below expands that category's sub-categories. Move to ▶ ├─ Materials ▶ │ ├─ Materials ← with back arrow: selects this top-level category itself │ ├─ ───── │ ├─ Custom │ ├─ Fabric │ ├─ Metal │ └─ … ├─ Models ▶ │ ├─ Models │ ├─ ───── │ ├─ Architecture │ └─ … └─ … Two ways to read it: The item with the back arrow (an arrow pointing left) = selects "this category itself" without going deeper; The All assets node does not appear in the cascade — it is not a real storage location. Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Move to ▶ Takes the asset to the target category The asset library is loaded The asset disappears from the current category and appears in the target; the tree refreshes and jumps to the target Moving bypasses the recycle bin, but you can move it back Copy to ▶ Copies the asset into the target category The asset library is loaded The target category gains the same asset while the original remains It copies the whole package and doubles disk usage Move vs copy Scenario Which one The asset really belongs in another category Move to The same asset should be findable in two categories Copy to Keep the original and try a modified version Copy to (then edit the copy) Save disk space Move to With a multi-selection Right-clicking Move to / Copy to with several assets selected applies to all selected assets — a whole batch moves at once. The tree refreshes and stops on the target category so you can keep organizing. Notes specific to these items Cross-sub-library moves are allowed : a material can move into models, a texture into HDR; the menu does not block it. But an asset of the wrong type sitting in another sub-library may not open / preview as expected there, so use this carefully. Think about the target first : choosing wrongly costs one more move, not a re-import. Extra copies are yours to delete : there is no "undo the duplicate" button, so remove unwanted copies with Delete → Move to recycle bin . Tree counts may lag : if counts do not change after a move / copy, click refresh on the toolbar or switch to another category and back. tick target formats and start Existing formats are kept; conversion runs and is verified in a temporary directory outside the library before writing back Submenu: Update thumbnail ▶ (7 items) Sub-item Source Result Prerequisite Capture Shows a screenshot overlay to select an area Overwrites the current main thumbnail A screen to capture Import Choose a local image file Overwrites the current main thumbnail A local image Maya playblast Asks the frame mode first (current frame / timeline range), then playblasts Overwrites the main thumbnail Maya is connected and a viewport can be captured Render image Asks the frame mode, then renders with the current renderer Overwrites the main thumbnail Maya is connected and a renderer is available Add Choose a local image file Stored in a new slot (multiple thumbnails) A local image Capture and add Shows a screenshot overlay to capture an image Stored in a new slot A screen to capture Background render Starts a separate mayapy process for headless offscreen rendering Generates a new thumbnail Maya / mayapy is installed; it does not touch the current viewport or scene Key points: The difference between Capture / Add and Capture and add is overwrite versus append : items with "add" go into a new slot and keep the previous main thumbnail. Background render is the only one independent of the current viewport : it renders in another process, so you can keep working in Maya; with a multi-selection it processes all selected assets. Playblast and render ask the frame mode first : animation assets should use "timeline range", stills "current frame". Submenu: Update asset ▶ (7 items) Sub-item Effect Prerequisite Replace asset Re-exports and overwrites this asset's content with the current scene selection Objects are selected in the scene Append format Adds another geometry format to the same asset (existing formats kept) Objects are selected in the scene Append as LOD Exports the current selection as a new LOD of this asset Objects are selected in the scene Create new version Exports the current selection as a new version (V1/V2…) of this asset Objects are selected in the scene Add new variant… Exports the current selection as a variant of this asset Objects are selected in the scene Batch add variants… (one per selected object) Produces one variant for each selected object Several objects are selected Variant management… Opens the variant management window for batch rename / delete / reorder The asset already has variants Additional notes: Each item first opens the export configuration dialog (pre-filled for the current asset) and writes only after you confirm formats and options — it does not overwrite on a single click. path: Common items: preview node, AI analysis, asset details
synonyms: how to see material node connections
items.summary: One-line summary: these are the three "take a look" items at the bottom of the menu : look at node connections, look at how AI reads this thumbnail, look at ass
items.text: One-line summary: these are the three "take a look" items at the bottom of the menu : look at node connections, look at how AI reads this thumbnail, look at asset details. Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Preview node ▶ Read-only view of the connections inside the asset's node files A .zmetal or named .ma node file is found in the asset The submenu lists node files (such as aiStandardSurface1.ma , aiStandardSurface1.zmetal ); clicking one opens the node editor preview It does not import nodes into the scene; use Import for that AI thumbnail analysis Lets AI read the thumbnail and suggest category / tags / Chinese name / notes AI dependencies are complete (local Ollama + embedding model) Opens the AI analysis window with results and suggestions; on confirm they are written back to the asset Without AI dependencies the feature first guides you through installation Asset details Shows this asset's details on its own None Assets with versions or variants open the version browser ; the rest open the asset inspection window Same path as double-clicking the preview image on the right What "Preview node" actually shows It reads the node files in the asset and draws nodes and connections in the node editor, answering "how is the network inside this material / scene wired". Files that get listed Files that do not .zmetal (material networks) The generic node.ma (the default node file produced on export) Named .ma files (such as aiStandardSurface1.ma , place2dTexture1.ma ) Textures, caches and thumbnails, which are not node files .zmetal and named .ma inside variant / LOD directories (shown as variants/<version>/<file> ) Cases where the asset holds no node file at all (the row does not appear) So "my menu has no preview node" usually means this asset has no named node file — the menu is not broken. Compare with the "Conditional" row in 8.5.1 . Further reading: material node preview 4.4.1.4 , previewing .ma node connections 4.4.3.4 . What "AI thumbnail analysis" does and writes back It opens the AI analysis window and hands your thumbnail to the vision model; It suggests category , tags , Chinese name (readable name) and notes ; After you confirm or adjust each item and apply, the result is written into the asset metadata (the card's name, tags and category follow). Prerequisites and limits: AI dependencies must be complete (Ollama + embedding model and so on). When missing, the plug-in offers the one-click install in Settings → AI . It analyses the thumbnail , not scene data; better thumbnails give better suggestions. It changes no geometry and no textures, only proposes metadata. To undo a write-back, change it back in the edit dialog. Which window "Asset details" opens Asset situation What opens Has versions (V1/V2…) or variants The version browser: lists all versions / variants / LODs, can import and manage An ordinary single-version asset The asset inspection window: large preview plus detail information Two notes: This item is always at the very bottom of the menu, after a separator, and closes the menu. Right-clicking inside the asset inspection window reuses this menu but no longer shows Asset details (otherwise it would only open an identical window). Notes Preview node is read-only : it reads files and draws connections and builds nothing in your scene; go back to Import to import. AI suggestions are not always right : the model only sees the thumbnail, so check category and tag suggestions against your conventions before applying. Asset details equals double-clicking the preview image : two entries, one result — use whichever is convenient. path: Context menus of version, variant and LOD entries

why can I not move this
items.summary: One-line summary: versions / variants / LODs are not independent assets but entries inside a master asset; right-clicking them gives two reduced menus that only
items.text: One-line summary: versions / variants / LODs are not independent assets but entries inside a master asset; right-clicking them gives two reduced menus that only act on "this one copy". How to get here Right-click the master asset card → expand the Import ▶ submenu; Click View versions / View variants / View LOD management ; The asset area switches to the internal view where cards become version / variant / LOD entries; Right-click an internal entry card. Context menu of version / variant entries Segment Item Description ① Import <format> Imports only this copy (this version / variant); with a single format the row shows the format name ① Add reference Brings this copy in as a Reference ① View LOD management Appears when the entry has several LODs; switches to its LOD list ① Append LOD… Appends a new LOD to this copy ② Add to favorite set ▶ It favorites the master asset (internal entries cannot be favorited themselves) ② Select all / duplicate / open folder Duplicate and open folder both act on the master asset ; internal entries are never duplicated ③ Edit Unavailable on the main version (gray, tagged "(main version)") ③ Update thumbnail ▶ Capture / import; variants also have Maya playblast / render image; add / capture and add. No background render ③ Update asset ▶ Version entries offer: replace asset / append format / append as LOD / create new version (gray on sub-versions) / add new variant… / batch add variants…; variant entries have only one Update asset row ③ Delete The main version cannot be deleted (gray, stating the main version cannot be deleted) ④ Asset details Opens the version browser / asset inspection window Context menu of LOD entries (even leaner) Segment Item Description ① Import <format> Imports only this LOD ① Open folder Opens the master asset folder ② Set as default LOD Appears only when this is not the default; sets this LOD as default ② Rename LOD… Renames it (only this LOD's display name) ③ Append LOD… Adds another LOD to this version ③ Delete this LOD Gray when only one LOD remains (at least one must stay) ④ Asset details Opens the version browser / asset inspection window Why these menus are so short Internal entries (versions / variants / LODs) are not real assets , only a slice of the master asset. Therefore: What a normal asset can do Why an internal entry cannot Move to / copy to a category It has no directory of its own and cannot be moved; move the master asset instead Edit name / category / tags Metadata lives on the master asset Delete the whole asset Only "this copy" can be deleted (LODs have a minimum), and deleting the package is done on the master asset Render thumbnails in the background Background rendering works per whole package, and a single entry has none There is a real upside: a mistake in this menu at worst changes this one copy and never the master asset's content or location. Notes Favoriting hits the master asset : favoriting from an internal entry puts the master asset in the favorite set, not this version. "Set as default LOD" changes master asset behavior : the default LOD is the one used on import / drag, so think before switching. Deleting a variant deletes only its own geometry and thumbnail : shared textures / materials are unaffected (the confirmation states this). Paste does not copy internal entries : duplicating an entry never reaches the clipboard. items.text: One-line summary: where you right-click decides which menu opens — on a card it is the asset menu, on blank space with no card it is this short "area menu", and right-clicking a row in list view equals right-clicking a card. Three locations, three menus Where you right-click What opens Details On an asset card (icon view) The full asset menu 8.5.2 ~ 8.5.12 Blank space in the asset area (icon view) The area menu (create asset / paste / select all; under All assets only these three, which is what the screenshot shows) This page On a row in list view Exactly the same full menu as right-clicking a card Second half of this page Blank space in list view has no menu — the list is rows and blank space belongs to no location, so right-click does nothing. Item-by-item details of the blank-space menu Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Create asset Exports the scene selection as a new asset into the current category A definite top-level category is current (not All assets) Opens the create asset / export dialog and writes into the current category on confirm In the animation data category this row becomes Export animation , exporting the selected hierarchy as animation data Paste Copies the clipboard asset into the current category You right-clicked an asset and chose Duplicate earlier The current category gains that asset Name conflicts follow your settings (ask / auto rename / overwrite) Select all Selects every visible card Cards exist All highlight Only the filtered / searched results Import from outside ▶ Collects files / folders from disk into the current category A definite top-level category is current The submenu is trimmed per category, see the table below Does not appear under All assets (no target category) Submenu: Import from outside ▶ (trimmed per category) Sub-item Meaning Categories where it appears Import from file Packs a project file (.ma/.mb/.fbx and so on) into a .zasset asset Materials / models / lights / scenes / animation / node tree / custom top-level categories Import .zasset asset Registers a ready-made .zasset package into the library Every category except Images and Audio (materials / textures / models / lights / scenes / animation / HDR / animation data / node tree / custom) Import textures A whole PBR texture set (several resolutions) → one texture asset Materials, textures Import HDR .hdr / .exr → an HDR environment asset (with a thumbnail) HDR Import images Copies loose image files straight into the current category Images Import audio Copies loose audio files straight into the current category Audio Import animation data Packs .atom into a standard animation data asset Animation data Two rules: Locked under All assets : Create asset is gray and Import from outside disappears entirely, because the plug-in cannot tell which category you want. Custom top-level categories get everything : a category you created has an unknown type, so all four packing routes are listed — better too many than missing. Right-click in list view Behavior Same as icon view Menu opened on a row Identical (same construction code, trimmed by sub-library the same way) Right-click after selecting several rows Same: applies to all selected rows plus the one you right-clicked Right-click on blank space Icon view has the area menu; list view does not So "list view has fewer features" is usually an illusion — the items are identical and only blank-space behavior differs. Notes What counts as blank space : if the cursor is over a card it is not blank and the asset menu opens. To get the area menu, right-click a gap between cards. Paste targets the current category : click into the target category before pasting; if you paste into the wrong one, move it with Move to . Create asset is unavailable under All assets : click into a specific category first.
