items.title: Space marking menu (quick import ring)
synonyms: press space to open a menu
how to use the marking menu
items.summary: One-line summary: with the cursor over an asset card, pressing Space opens a cross-shaped marking menu around the cursor — up and down, left and right each hold
items.text: One-line summary: with the cursor over an asset card, pressing Space opens a cross-shaped marking menu around the cursor — up and down, left and right each hold one family of import commands, and dragging toward a direction runs it. It uses the same commands as the context menu but extracts the most common block into a quick ring. How to open it Move the cursor onto a card in the asset area (it need not be selected first); Press Space once (without Ctrl / Shift). Details: If that card was not selected, the plug-in selects it first — the same rule as right-click (the menu's target asset must be in the selection). It works in icon view only ; list view has no ring. When the asset has no import-type commands at all, nothing opens. How to read the image : a marking menu expands on hover , so a static screenshot can only expand one direction. The image expands "up = import", while the other three (left reference / right apply / down convert) only expand when the cursor moves there, which is why only the end markers show. A materials asset really has all four: up = import, left = add reference, right = assign material to selection + apply material parameters, down = convert import. What the four directions are Direction Family Typical content Up Import Import / Import ▶ / Import textures ▶ / Import to timeline and so on Left Reference Add reference / Add reference ▶ Right Apply Assign material to selection / apply material parameters / create material / assign texture / apply light parameters Down Convert Convert import ▶ (materials, lights) A direction with no matching command stays empty (not even a pill is drawn), following Maya marking menu semantics. How to read the pills Appearance Meaning One pill (a single line of text) A specific command ; drag onto it and release to run Several stacked pills in one direction That direction holds several commands (textures, for example, have three to the right) A pill with ▸ after it It has sub-items : hovering or dragging onto it removes the first level and leaves this pill plus its sub-item list A submenu with a single sub-item It degrades into the pill itself, saving one click Many sub-items The submenu lists them separately and the wheel pages when they exceed the visible rows Every row in a sub-item list is an executable command (for example the 18 material types under Convert import ▶ ). How to use it Action Result Hold Space to open → drag toward a direction → release Space Runs the highlighted item (the smoothest usage) Click a pill or a sub-item after opening Runs it too Arrow keys to pick a direction, Enter to enter sub-items / run Full keyboard operation In the second level, ↑↓ (or Tab) to move, ← to return, Enter to run Keyboard inside the submenu Esc Cancel Highlight rests in the center / release without reaching a pill Cancels and runs nothing The bottom hint reads "Release Space / Enter to run · Esc to cancel"; read it when you forget. The four directions per sub-library (typical form) Sub-library Up (import) Left (reference) Right (apply) Down (convert) Materials Import ▶ (zmetal / ma) Add reference Assign material to selection, apply material parameters Convert import ▶ (18 types) Models Import ma Add reference — — Lights Import ▶ (zlight / ma) Add reference Apply light parameters to selected lights Convert import ▶ (4 types) Textures Import textures ▶ (each texture plus import all) — Assign material to selection, create material ▶, assign texture to material — Scenes / node tree Import ma Add reference — — HDR Import hdr — Create dome light ▶, assign texture — Animation Import ▶ (ma / abc) Add reference ▶ (ma / abc) — — Images Import as file node, create imagePlane — Assign to selected material slot — Audio Import to timeline, import to time editor, import to Trax editor, import to camera sequencer — — — Animation data Import animation ▶, import animation (hierarchy mapping)…, import to selected attributes ▶ — — — This table shows the typical form : the actual number and n

items.title: Multi-select batch operation bar
synonyms: how to batch edit several assets
how to restore a batch delete
items.summary: One-line summary: selecting two or more assets makes a batch bar "grow" at the right of the top toolbar , turning the most common batch actions into a row of bu
items.text: One-line summary: selecting two or more assets makes a batch bar "grow" at the right of the top toolbar , turning the most common batch actions into a row of buttons so you no longer right-click one by one. When it appears Situation Bar Two or more assets selected (rubber band / Ctrl+click / Shift+click, or right-click Select all ) Appears Only one asset selected, or nothing selected Hidden After clicking Clear selection Collapses automatically It appears inside the top toolbar, to the right of the search box , scales in height with the font size in settings, and never squeezes out other toolbar buttons. The bar holds six controls Control Effect What happens on click Notes N assets selected A count hint only (not a button) — This is where you verify "how many did I really select" Batch rename Renames assets in bulk Opens the batch rename window ( 8.12.1 ), renames one by one on confirm and reports "N succeeded" The naming rule is set in the window; check the preview before confirming Batch tags Adds / removes / overwrites tags in bulk Opens the batch tag window ( 8.12.2 ) with Add / Remove / Overwrite ; writes back on confirm Overwrite clears existing tags, so choose carefully Batch move Moves this batch into another category Opens a "Choose target category" list ( only categories of the current sub-library ), then moves one by one and refreshes For cross-sub-library moves use right-click Move to ▶ Batch copy Copies this batch into another category Same as above; copies one by one after choosing the target Doubles disk usage Batch delete Deletes this batch Opens a confirmation (listing the first 20 names and the total); moves to the recycle bin on confirm Restorable : recover it in the recycle bin, see 8.8.3 Clear selection Empties the current selection All cards unhighlight and the bar collapses Does not affect asset content Layout: a blue count label on the left, a row of buttons in the middle (delete uses the red danger style), and the low-key Clear selection at the far right. How it differs from right-clicking a multi-selection (important) Action Batch bar Context menu (after multi-select) Rename / change tags ✓ has dedicated windows ✗ use Edit one by one, or just use the bar Target range for move / copy Only the current sub-library's categories Full cascade of all 11 sub-libraries, cross-sub-library allowed Delete ✓ one batch delete (to the recycle bin) ✓ Delete ▶ offers move to recycle bin or delete permanently Delete permanently ✗ no such entry ✓ right-click Delete ▶ delete permanently Conclusion: to shuffle things inside one sub-library the bar is handier; to move across sub-libraries or delete permanently use the context menu. A typical usage Rubber-band select a dozen materials in the Materials category; The bar at the top right reads "12 assets selected"; Click Batch tags and add an old-library migration tag; Click Batch move , choose the target category in the list and confirm; The bar collapses as the selection empties, the tree refreshes, and the assets are in the new category. Notes and risks Check the count first : before batch deleting or moving, look at the bar's "N assets selected" and the status bar to confirm nothing extra is selected. Batch delete is not "delete permanently" : it goes through the recycle bin and can be restored; to erase them for good use right-click Delete ▶ Delete permanently , which is irreversible. Batch rename / tags write back to asset metadata : to undo, change the names / tags back (the dialogs have no bulk revert). With a selection spanning categories, batch move uses the first asset's sub-library : when the selection mixes sub-libraries, the target list follows the first asset's sub-library, so use the context menu for cross-sub-library moves. Related Multi-select and rubber band: 4.1.4.1 ; batch move and copy: 4.1.8.1 ; batch delete: 4.1.8.2 Batch rename window: 8.12.1 ; batch tag window: 8.12.2 Favorite / select all / duplicate on cards: 8.5.14 ; move to / copy to: 8.5.15 Sub-

items.title: Properties panel fields
synonyms: what is in the properties panel
items.summary: One-line summary: selecting an asset in the asset grid lists all of its information fields in the Properties area on the right. The properties panel is for look
items.text: One-line summary: selecting an asset in the asset grid lists all of its information fields in the Properties area on the right. The properties panel is for looking only; to change something use the context menu (see 8.6.2 ) or the edit button in the title bar (see 8.6.3 ). How to open it Click any category in the left navigation to enter the asset grid; Single-click any asset card (no double-click needed); The Properties area on the right immediately shows that asset's fields. If the panel was closed, do not worry: the Panels menu at the top reopens the Properties area (see 8.2.5 ); the area can also be dragged, split and torn off (see 3.2.1 ). Field table The table follows the panel from top to bottom. "Editable" means editable after entering edit mode, not changeable with a single click. Field What it shows Editable How to edit Notes Name The readable name (Chinese name, name_cn in meta) Yes Right-click the row → Edit , or the pencil button in the title bar This is what the card and status bar show; when empty the card shows only the asset name Asset name The real asset name (English name, name in meta), used by files and nodes No — The whole row hides when there is no value; to rename, change Name via right-click Edit , not the file name on disk Node type The Maya node type, such as aiStandardSurface , VRayMtl Yes Right-click the row → Edit (the row is called "Material type" in edit mode) It is readable text only; a wrong value does not change the real node in the scene, and import decides by the real node type Asset type Which sub-library it belongs to (materials / models / lights / textures…) No The dropdown is gray in edit mode To change sub-library, move the asset into a category of another sub-library (see 4.1.6.4 ) Category The readable name of the asset's category No The dropdown is gray in edit mode To change category use right-click Move to / Copy to (see 8.5.15 ) Format The formats the package really contains, such as zmetal , ma , fbx ; there may be several badges No — Loose-file assets take the source file extension; to add a format use right-click Update asset → Append format (see 8.5.16 ) Animation format The animation formats an animation data asset contains No — Only animation assets have content; other assets hide the whole row Size Disk usage of the asset files (for .zasset , the sum of every file in the package) No — Disk size, not VRAM / memory usage Resolution Pixel dimensions of a texture, such as 2048 × 2048 No — Shown only for texture-type assets whose image size can be read; other assets hide the whole row Audio Duration · sample rate · channels, such as 3.2 s · 44.1 kHz · Stereo No — Shown only on music / audio assets Software The software that produced the asset (such as Maya, Substance) Yes Right-click the row → Edit Recorded information only and does not change import behavior; shows "-" when unrecorded Renderer The renderer a material / light belongs to (arnold / redshift / vray) Yes Right-click the row → Edit As above, recorded information; import looks at the real material type Color space The color space recorded for this asset, such as sRGB , Raw , ACEScg Yes Right-click the row → Edit ; pick from presets or type directly Changing this never changes the color space of textures already imported into Maya Created When the asset was created / exported, such as 2026-11-03 10:24 No — The whole row hides when unrecorded Tags All tag chips attached to this asset Yes Double-click a tag chip, or right-click the tags row → Edit Clicking a tag filters by it; Ctrl + click filters by several (see 4.1.6.1 ) Notes Free-text remarks, multiple lines allowed Yes Right-click the row → Edit With no notes it shows gray "right-click to edit"; recycle bin entries write the deletion time here Rows that come and go The panel does not always draw all 16 rows; these appear and hide by asset (not seeing one is not a bug): Row Appears when Asset name meta has name Animation format The asset carries an animation format

items.title: Field edit menu (right-click)
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking any field in the properties area opens a menu with copy / copy ID / edit, and only Edit enters an editable state. First, a comm
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking any field in the properties area opens a menu with copy / copy ID / edit, and only Edit enters an editable state. First, a common misunderstanding: double-clicking a field no longer enters edit mode (older versions did, which caused accidental edits when you only wanted to look). Double-click has exactly one use — double-clicking a tag chip enters tag editing. The edit entry for fields is right-click , or the pencil button in the title bar (see 8.6.3 ). How to open it Select an asset in the asset grid; Hover any row in the properties area (the field name, the value, even blank space); Right-click to open the menu. Recycle bin entries open this menu too, but Edit is gray (read-only). Item-by-item details Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Copy Puts this field's text on the clipboard The field has text Selected text is copied; with nothing selected the whole value is copied Read-only fields (asset name / category / format / size / resolution / audio / created) use this menu too, so copying always happens here Copy ID Copies the asset's unique id ( id in meta) The asset has an id The clipboard holds the id string The id is not shown in the properties area, so search-by-id and external communication must start here Edit Enters edit mode and focuses the field for this row Not a read-only recycle bin entry The properties area switches to the edit card with the cursor in the matching input Clicking Edit on a read-only field only enters edit mode without focusing that row (it cannot be changed anyway) The items gray out automatically: no text means Copy is gray; no id means Copy ID is gray; a read-only entry means Edit is gray. After clicking Edit: what edit mode offers Edit-mode field Control Editable Description Name Single-line input Yes The name shown on the card (the readable name) Material type Single-line input Yes Corresponds to Node type in display mode; plain text Asset type Dropdown No (gray) Decided by the asset's sub-library Category Dropdown No (gray) To change category use right-click Move to Software Single-line input Yes Recorded information Renderer Single-line input Yes Recorded information Color space Editable dropdown Yes Presets: sRGB / Raw / ACEScg / Linear sRGB / Utility - Raw / Output - sRGB, and you may type freely Tags Tag chips plus + Add tag Yes + Add tag opens a popup: type a new tag and press Enter, click a common tag to add it quickly, or click ✖ on a chip to remove it (see 4.1.6.1 ) Notes Multi-line input Yes The input has a maximum height and scrolls internally for long notes Two more conventions in edit mode: The wheel hovering over the asset type / category / color space dropdowns does not change their values (to prevent accidents); Clicking the asset card area (the center grid) while editing applies the current changes and leaves edit mode. Save and cancel Action Result Undoable Title bar ✓ (save) Writes the changes back to asset metadata and refreshes the panel and card After saving there is no undo stack , so Ctrl+Z cannot revert it; edit again to restore the old values Title bar × (cancel) Discards all changes from this session and restores the pre-edit snapshot Fully restored, so clicking it is safe Clicking the card area (auto apply) Same as save Same as the first row 警告 Property editing changes asset metadata (the meta inside .zasset ), which is lost only if the asset is deleted or overwritten; but after saving the plug-in offers no "undo this property change", so a mistake must be fixed by hand. When changing several fields at once, think it through before saving. A typical operation: add notes and tags to an asset Select the asset → right-click the Notes row → Edit ; Type the explanation in the notes box; click + Add tag and type a tag or add a common one quickly; When everything looks right click ✓ in the title bar (or click the asset card area); The panel returns to display mode with the notes and tags immediately visible; the status

items.title: Properties panel title bar buttons
synonyms: the properties panel has no favorite
items.summary: One-line summary: the top of the properties area is a single row — "Properties" on the left, a row of small icon buttons on the right, and the area function but
items.text: One-line summary: the top of the properties area is a single row — "Properties" on the left, a row of small icon buttons on the right, and the area function button at the far right. This row doubles as the area's grip (dragging blank space moves the area), which is why the buttons are so small. Button overview Button Icon When it appears What it does Favorite Hollow gray star / filled gold star An asset is selected and it is not a read-only recycle bin entry Toggles the favorite state immediately (no save needed): hollow = not favorited, filled gold = favorited; the card and favorite sets refresh Edit Pencil Always shown (also with no asset selected, where clicking does nothing) Enters property edit mode; equivalent to right-clicking a field → Edit Save Check mark (green) Only in edit mode Writes edit-mode changes back to asset metadata and returns to display mode Cancel × Only in edit mode Discards unsaved changes and returns to display mode (fully restored) Area function button Main icon plus a small attached down arrow, tooltip "Properties" Always shown Opens the area menu: dock back to main window / various splits / tear off / tear off a copy / maximize / restore / merge into / close this area The four small buttons are mutually exclusive: State Favorite Edit Save Cancel No asset selected Hidden Shown Hidden Hidden Asset selected (display mode) Shown Shown Hidden Hidden Asset selected (edit mode) Hidden Hidden Shown Shown Read-only recycle bin entry Hidden Hidden Hidden Hidden Area function button menu This button does not belong to the properties panel itself; it is the entry shared by every area , and only the tooltip shows the current area name ("Properties" here). Its items include: Menu item Effect Details Dock back to main window Returns a torn-off floating window to the main window 3.2.1 Split right / down / left / up Splits this area to create an extra empty area 3.2.2 Tear off / tear off a copy Turns the properties area into an independent floating window (a copy opens another one) 3.2.1 Maximize / restore Temporarily fills the window with this area / restores it 3.2.3 Merge into… Merges this area into an adjacent one 3.2.2 Close this area Closes this properties area See below How to get the properties panel back after closing it Reopen the Properties area from the Panels menu at the top (see 8.2.5 ); Or use Reset layout to restore every area to default (see 3.2.5 ). Common questions Symptom Cause What to do The star button is missing No asset selected, or the selected item is a recycle bin entry Select a normal asset in the asset grid Save / cancel are missing You are not in edit mode Click the pencil first (or right-click a field → Edit ) Clicking the pencil does nothing No asset selected / read-only recycle bin entry / within half a second after clicking cancel (misclick protection) Select an asset and wait a moment before clicking The star disappears while editing The favorite button hides in edit mode by design It returns after saving or cancelling Related What each field means → 8.6.1 The right-click edit menu and edit-mode details → 8.6.2 Dragging, splitting and tearing off areas → 3.2.1 , 3.2.2 The Panels and layout menu → 8.2.5

items.title: Preview area and thumbnail slots
synonyms: how to switch to the next image
items.summary: One-line summary: the Preview area on the right shows the selected asset's thumbnail (possibly several), and double-clicking opens a larger viewer. It shows a t
items.text: One-line summary: the Preview area on the right shows the selected asset's thumbnail (possibly several), and double-clicking opens a larger viewer. It shows a thumbnail , not a live Maya viewport render. To change the image use the context menu ( 8.7.2 ) or the four buttons below ( 8.7.3 ). How to open it Pick any category in the left navigation to enter the asset grid; Single-click any asset card and the Preview area on the right shows the image immediately; With no asset selected the preview is a blank canvas with a faint placeholder icon. If the panel was closed, reopen the Preview area from the Panels menu at the top (see 8.2.5 ); it can also be dragged, split and torn off (see 3.2.1 ). The preview area itself Feature Description Size Always a 1:1 square whose side follows the column width; on a narrow column it shrinks to the available height and never draws outside the area Empty state A dark canvas with a translucent placeholder icon in the center Right-click Right-clicking the preview image opens the Update thumbnail menu ( 8.7.2 ) Double-click Opens a larger viewer: an ordinary asset opens the asset details / inspection window ( 8.11.1 ); an asset with versions or variants opens the version browser ( 8.11.2 ) Animated images When the asset carries a GIF / MP4 it plays right in the preview Video preview Playblast videos of animation data assets (mp4 in .cache ) play in the preview Recycle bin Read-only display; every thumbnail control and context menu is disabled Thumbnail slots: one asset can hold several images Slot Naming in a .zasset asset Naming in a plain folder asset First image (main) thumb.sicon / thumb.aicon / thumb.png / thumb.mp4 <asset name>.sicon Second onward (extra slots) thumb_2.sicon , thumb_3.sicon … <asset name>_2.sicon , <asset name>_3.sicon … The main image is the card cover and cannot be deleted ; it can only be overwritten by capture or import; Extra images start from the second and can be deleted; Extra image numbering continues after the highest existing number and never collides. Switching between several thumbnails When a selected asset has several images, a counter appears below the preview (such as 2/3 ) and you can switch three ways: Method Operation Description Hover arrows Move the cursor into the preview and ◀ ▶ appear on both sides ◀ is gray on the first image and ▶ is gray on the last Wheel Scroll the wheel while hovering the preview Up = previous, down = next Automatic slideshow No action needed; it advances every 2 seconds by default and loops Hovering pauses it; it does not run while an animation / video plays or when there is only one image Deleting an extra thumbnail Switch to the image to delete (the counter must not read 1/n ); Click Delete below the preview; That image file is removed from the asset directory immediately and the preview falls back to the remaining images. 警告 Deleting an extra thumbnail has no confirmation and does not use the recycle bin; it deletes the image file on disk. Check the counter while switching, and never click delete on the main image (the delete button is gray there). Previewing audio assets Music / audio assets gain two things: A large translucent button in the middle of the preview: play / pause (the icon follows the state); A timeline below showing current time / total duration that you can drag to seek. Common questions Symptom Cause The preview stays a blank canvas No asset selected, or the selection is a virtual entry / recycle bin entry The preview image is small / shrank The column width or area height is insufficient and the square side was reduced; widen the right column It does not show the newest capture The preview reads the thumbnail file and never refreshes live; capture or generate it again Double-click did not open a viewer It may be a read-only entry, or the asset has versions / variants and double-click opens the version browser Related The Update thumbnail menu on preview right-click → 8.7.2 The four buttons below the preview

items.title: Update thumbnail menu
items.summary: One-line summary: right-clicking the preview image opens this thumbnail menu — the same implementation as Update thumbnail ▶ in the asset card context menu. How
items.text: One-line summary: right-clicking the preview image opens this thumbnail menu — the same implementation as Update thumbnail ▶ in the asset card context menu. How to open it Select an asset in the asset grid (the preview shows an image); Hover the preview image and right-click (it opens on press, no need to wait for release). Recycle bin entries and virtual entries such as versions / variants do not have this menu. Item-by-item details The menu has four groups separated by horizontal lines: Menu item Effect Prerequisite What happens on click Notes Capture Opens the full screenshot tool to capture, and the result overwrites the main image The Maya window is visible (it captures the screen) A screenshot overlay appears (with a toolbar and screen recording); the capture is written back to the main image Different from the Capture button below, which captures the dragged rectangle immediately (see 8.7.3 ) Import Choose a local image as the thumbnail, overwriting the main image A local image exists Opens a file chooser and replaces the main image immediately The file filter is *.sicon *.jpg *.jpeg *.aicon *.bmp (switchable to all files); overwriting has no undo Maya playblast Generates a thumbnail by playblasting the current Maya viewport Inside Maya with content in the scene Asks for the frame mode, then playblasts Frame modes: current frame / sequence (captured over the timeline range) Render image Renders one image with the current renderer as the thumbnail The current renderer works and the scene has content Asks for the frame mode, then renders Slower than playblast; the renderer's materials / lights must already be set up Add Choose local images and store them in new thumbnail slots Local images exist Opens a file chooser (multi-select) and stores each as an extra image Does not overwrite the main image (the same behavior as the Add button below) Capture and add Captures and stores into a new thumbnail slot The Maya window is visible Opens the screenshot overlay and the capture becomes an extra image Does not overwrite the main image Background render Starts a separate headless mayapy process to render a new thumbnail A usable headless renderer exists locally A background job renders and replaces the main image when finished It does not touch the current viewport or scene, so you can keep working; it is the slowest, see 4.1.7.1 When the whole menu is missing Whether this menu appears is controlled by the per-sub-library switch in Settings → Context menu (see 8.9.5 ): Switch Behavior when off Update thumbnail Right-clicking the preview opens nothing , and the submenu is gone from the asset card menu too Background render The menu remains but the last item, background render, is not shown Sub-library scope When a sub-library does not allow headless rendering, background render is not shown in the first place How it differs from the four buttons below the preview Action This menu (preview right-click) Bottom buttons ( 8.7.3 ) Capture The full screenshot tool (toolbar / recording) Drag a rectangle and it captures immediately , overwriting the main image Import Overwrites the main image Overwrites the main image (same action) Add Imports files into new slots Imports files into new slots (same action) Capture and add Captures into a new slot Captures into a new slot (same action) Playblast / render image / background render Present Absent (context menu only) Risks and how to undo Capture / import / Maya playblast / render image / background render all overwrite the main image : the old cover is gone with no undo. To undo, do it again (background render or another capture is safest); if you really have no good image, you may recover a backup of the old one from the asset directory. Add / Capture and add create a new slot and leave the main image alone; if you do not want it, switch to that image in the preview and click Delete (deletion is irreversible and again has no confirmation). 提示 Just want a new cover without capturing anything

items.title: Bottom buttons: capture, import, add, capture and add
path: Bottom buttons: capture, import, add, capture and add
synonyms: the four buttons under the preview
how to change the cover image
difference between capture and capture and add
items.summary: One-line summary: a row of four buttons below the preview area decides which image becomes this asset's thumbnail and whether extra images are stored. Remember
items.text: One-line summary: a row of four buttons below the preview area decides which image becomes this asset's thumbnail and whether extra images are stored. Remember one dividing line and you cannot go wrong: Capture and Import replace the cover (main image); Add and Capture and add append new images and leave the cover alone. When they are usable All four share one condition and are all gray when it fails: Condition Description A normal asset is selected All four are gray with no asset selected It is not a recycle bin entry The recycle bin is read-only and all four are gray It is not a version / variant virtual entry Virtual entries have no thumbnail of their own and all four are gray Item-by-item details Button Effect Overwrites the main image What happens on click Notes Capture Select a screen area ; the capture is taken immediately as the cover Yes (overwrite) The screen dims for selection; drag a box, release, and it is written to thumb.sicon ( <asset name>.sicon for folder assets) No toolbar and no recording; the capture is scaled proportionally so the long side matches Settings → General → Default thumbnail size (factory 512) Import Choose a local image as the cover Yes (overwrite) Opens a file chooser and replaces the main image immediately; the card cover refreshes Filter *.sicon *.jpg *.jpeg *.aicon *.bmp (switch to all files to pick png and others); the old cover is gone Add Stores local images into new thumbnail slots No (append) Opens a file chooser (multi-select) and copies each into thumb_2.sicon , thumb_3.sicon …; the preview jumps to the new image The main image is untouched; several images fill empty slots in order Capture and add Opens the full screenshot tool and stores captures in new slots No (append) A screenshot overlay appears (with a toolbar); each capture advances to the next empty slot so you can capture several in a row Same behavior as Capture and add in the context menu ( 8.7.2 ) Quick comparison Capture Import Add Capture and add Result Overwrites the main image Overwrites the main image New slot New slot How the image is taken Drag with the mouse (immediate) Pick a local image Pick local images (multi-select) Full screenshot tool (repeat captures) Shows a toolbar No No No Yes Good for Quickly grabbing a cover Using an existing image as cover Collecting a few alternatives Precise selection / several captures A typical operation Change the cover (most common) Select the asset so the preview shows an image; Click Capture , drag a box around the area you want as the cover, release; The preview and card cover immediately show the new image (scaled to the default thumbnail size). Add an alternative image Click Add and pick local images (multi-select); A counter appears below the preview (such as 2/3 ); click ▶ or use the wheel to view; If you do not want it, switch to that image and click Delete . Undo and risks Operation Undoable How to undo Capture / import (overwrite the main image) No Capture another or import another image; the old cover has no backup Add / capture and add (new slots) Yes (delete the new image) Switch to the new image and click Delete ; deleting itself is irreversible Deleting an extra image No No confirmation and no recycle bin (see 4.1.7.5 ) 警告 Capture and Import overwrite the main image directly and the plug-in offers no "undo the last thumbnail"; if the old cover matters, copy the asset directory's thumb.sicon in Explorer before operating. Related Complete rules for the preview area and thumbnail slots → 8.7.1 The Update thumbnail menu on preview right-click → 8.7.2 Where the output size is configured (default thumbnail size) → 8.9.2 General notes on multiple thumbnail slots and deletion → 4.1.7.5

items.title: Bottom status bar
path: Status bar, AI area and recycle bin
synonyms: what is that line at the bottom
items.summary: One-line summary: the thin strip at the very bottom of the window reports counts on the left and which asset is selected on the right. It spans the right work a
items.text: One-line summary: the thin strip at the very bottom of the window reports counts on the left and which asset is selected on the right. It spans the right work area (excluding the leftmost navigation column), has a fixed height, cannot be dragged and takes no working space. What the two text segments are Position Content Meaning Left Materials: 84/84 The left of the slash is the number of assets visible in the current view , the right is the total number of assets loaded in the library Left (appended when selecting) `\ Selected: 3` How many assets are selected (meaningful when multi-selecting) Right Selected: CARTOON12 The readable name (name field) of the selected asset; with multiple selected it shows the first "Materials" is historical wording and here simply means "assets"; it has nothing to do with how many material assets the library holds. When the numbers change Operation Effect Switching category / sub-library / favorite set The visible count changes (the total does not; the total is for the whole library) Keyword search / tag filter / AI search / search by image The visible count changes — this is "how many matched right now" Multi-select / rubber band / deselect "Selected" appears or disappears Creating, importing or deleting assets and refreshing The total changes While the library is loading Placeholder text first; real numbers once loading finishes The right segment also shows other things temporarily The right-hand information slot does not only show asset names; many operation results temporarily occupy it (until the next asset selection): Scenario What the right side may show An asset is selected Selected: asset name AI search / search by image Result notes such as "AI search 'keyword': found n assets", "Image search: …" Text search for video / music Notes such as "Text search for video: matched n animations" Background rendering / UUID repair Progress such as "Generating n thumbnails with …", "Repairing UUIDs: 3/20" A layout operation failed Hints such as "At least one area must remain" So changed text on the right is not necessarily an error; just read what it is talking about. Common questions Symptom Cause The two numbers differ (such as 12/84 ) Normal: the left is the visible count in the current category / search and the right is the whole library The number stays 0 The library did not load, or the current category really has no assets "Selected" never disappears The selection is still active; single-click blank space in the asset grid to clear it and it empties No asset path anywhere The status bar does not show paths; see them in the asset details window ( 8.11.1 ) Related The AI assistant area on the right → 8.8.2 In the recycle bin the status bar switches to entry count and usage → 8.8.3 Selecting / multi-selecting in the asset grid → 4.1.4.1 Overall notes on the status bar, floating bubble and quick open → 3.1.7

items.summary: One-line summary: the AI assistant area holds a single toggle button: click once to start the dsh chat panel, click again to close it completely. It is not a ch
items.text: One-line summary: the AI assistant area holds a single toggle button: click once to start the dsh chat panel, click again to close it completely. It is not a chat window itself — what actually talks to you is the dsh web chat panel , and this area is responsible for starting that panel, showing it and closing it. What the area contains Part Description The AI assistant label in the area header The area name; the area can be dragged / split / torn off (see 3.2.1 ) Area function button (tooltip "AI assistant") The shared area menu: dock / split / tear off / maximize / merge into / close Toggle button The entire feature of this area: turn the dsh chat panel on / off The three button states Button text Color Meaning AI assistant Neutral secondary dsh is not running (off) Starting AI assistant… Neutral secondary The dsh process is starting (usually a few seconds) Close AI assistant Blue accent dsh is running and the chat panel is open What a click does Current state Result Off Starts the dsh web end: depending on settings it docks the chat panel inside Maya (default) or opens it in the system browser ; when done the button becomes "Close AI assistant" Starting Wait for it; do not click repeatedly (extra clicks do not start another process) Already on Closes the panel and ends the dsh process (a real close, not a minimize); clicking again starts it fresh 警告 "Close AI assistant" really kills the dsh process ; it does not just hide the panel. Opening it again is a fresh start, and the conversation context depends on the sessions dsh saved itself. Embedded panel or system browser This is decided by Settings → AI → AI chat panel → Embed the AI chat panel in Maya (ticked by default), see 8.9.3 : Option Behavior Ticked (default) The chat panel docks inside Maya and is available whenever it is open; its title automatically carries the current scene name so it is distinguishable from your other dsh windows Unticked The same dsh chat panel opens in the system browser; sessions and tools are identical, only the window lives outside After changing this option, the next click on AI assistant uses the new mode; Maya does not need a restart. The panel is gone / the browser tab was closed This is the most common way to get stuck: dsh is still running but the chat panel is not visible. Open the top AI tools menu → Recall AI panel : it only brings the already running chat panel back, without restarting or killing the process ; In browser mode, closing the tab manually is invisible to the plug-in (tabs belong to the browser), so AI assistant then reads "close"; use Recall AI panel to get it back; The floating bubble inside the window does the same: while AI is running it breathes slowly, and clicking it recalls the panel. When dsh is not installed The first click on AI assistant opens the install guide (see 8.13.6 ) with four actions: copy the install command / one-click install the dsh runtime / open the install help / open the website or repository. Click again once it is installed. Common questions Symptom Cause / what to do The button stays on "Starting" The first start has to launch the process and the web service, usually a few seconds; if nothing changes after a minute or two, check the Maya Script Editor output The button is gray and unclickable Rare; usually an abnormal window / panel state. Reopen the panel or restart the plug-in The chat panel opened in the browser and cannot be found Click AI tools → Recall AI panel The previous conversation is gone after closing and reopening Whether dsh keeps a session is up to dsh itself; the plug-in only toggles the process and the panel Related The dsh chat panel and tool calls → 4.5.3.1 Embedded vs browser mode → 4.5.3.2 Opening, recalling and stopping → 4.5.3.3 Switching embedded / browser in settings → 8.9.3 The install guide when dsh is missing → 8.13.6

items.summary: One-line summary: deleting an asset / category / version first moves it to the recycle bin, from where it can be restored; only delete permanently really remove
items.text: One-line summary: deleting an asset / category / version first moves it to the recycle bin, from where it can be restored; only delete permanently really removes it from disk. Remember this difference first Operation Where the files are Restorable Uses disk space Move to recycle bin (asset right-click Delete → Move to recycle bin ) Still in the library, moved into the recycle bin folder Yes Yes (the recycle bin is capped at 100 GB, and you must delete old entries when full) Delete permanently (asset right-click Delete → Delete permanently ) Removed from disk directly, never enters the recycle bin No No Deleting a category or a version Also goes to the recycle bin first Yes Yes Every recycle bin record is labeled as an asset / category / version. How to open the recycle bin Look at the category tree in the left navigation: there is a separate Recycle bin entry at the bottom , followed by the entry count; Click it and the center content area switches to the recycle bin page; To return to assets, click any category (the recycle bin entry unhighlights). The category library and the project library each have their own recycle bin entry, and the counts are per library. The recycle bin page Element Description View Card / list, switched with the same controls as the asset grid; recycle bin cards use a dark red outline so they are instantly distinguishable Sort / thumbnail size The same three toolbar controls (view / sort / thumbnail slider); the recycle bin has no separate row of buttons Entry content Thumbnail + name + subtitle (type · size · deletion time); entries whose files are gone say "File lost (record can still be removed)" Result text The top shows "N items · used / 100 GB limit" and hints "Right-click an entry: restore / delete permanently"; at 90% it adds "approaching the limit, consider cleaning up", and once full, deleting assets is refused with a prompt to clean up first Right panel Selecting an entry shows properties and preview read-only (thumbnail and deletion time in the notes) with every thumbnail button disabled The recycle bin never cleans itself and has no empty-all button : entries can only be deleted one by one with Delete permanently in the context menu. Item-by-item details of the context menu Menu item Effect Where it appears What happens on click Notes Restore Returns this record to its original category / location On an entry The record leaves the recycle bin, the asset returns to its category and the list refreshes Being able to restore means the files still exist; a failed restore shows a prompt Delete permanently Removes this record from disk On an entry Asks "Deleting permanently cannot be undone. Continue?" and deletes the files on confirm Irreversible ; there is no second recycle bin Open recycle bin folder Opens the recycle bin directory in Explorer On an entry / on blank space Opens the library's recycle bin folder so you can inspect files Be careful with manual file changes; the plug-in does not sync them Right-clicking blank space shows only Open recycle bin folder . A typical operation: restore after a mistaken delete Click the Recycle bin entry in the left navigation to switch to the recycle bin page; Find the record (sort by type / name; thumbnails make it easy to recognize); Right-click → Restore ; The list refreshes and the entry disappears; return to its original category and the asset is there. A typical operation: free space when the recycle bin is full Confirm nothing in the recycle bin is still needed (permanent deletion cannot be undone); Right-click the entries to clear → Delete permanently (multi-select works); In the confirmation dialog click Yes; The used figure drops and disk space is released. 警告 Delete permanently is irreversible, skips the recycle bin and has no backup (the same for entries whose files were lost). Confirm before acting; when the library holds important assets, take a library backup first (see 4.1.12.4 ). Common questions Symptom Cause A deleted asset is not i

items.text: One-line summary: everything adjustable in the plug-in lives here across ten tabs, and most tabs are "locked" by default — tick Unlock all settings first. Nine out of ten first-time users get stuck on the same thing: options are visible but cannot be clicked and text cannot be typed . That is not a bug; it is the global lock (see "The most common blocker: the global lock" below). How to open it In the top toolbar of the main window click the Settings button (the gear, see 8.2.4 ); The Settings window opens on the General page; Switch pages with the tabs stacked vertically on the left (long English labels fit there), then save with the buttons at the bottom. What the ten tabs hold Tab Main content Locked by default Details General Font size, UI scale, default view, drag and drop, language, colors, delete permanently, thumbnail size, asset library management, name conflicts, texture / dependency import strategy, import namespace, settings presets No 8.9.2 AI settings AI dependency check / install / remove, vector index update and rebuild, global model, cloud service consent, embedded chat panel (with the dsh release track), external connections, AI / MCP channels, external AI tools No 8.9.3 Export defaults Which export formats are ticked by default per asset type, which formats are locked Yes 8.9.4 Context menu Context menu item switches per sub-library plus double-click commands Yes 8.9.5 Supported formats File extensions the library recognizes (one per line) Yes 8.9.6 Texture suffixes Aliases for each PBR texture channel (one per line) Yes 8.9.7 Sub-libraries and categories Which sub-libraries appear in the left column, sub-library IDs / display names, default category lists Yes (except Show in main UI ) 8.9.8 Other configuration Geometry extensions, image extensions, material node types Yes 8.9.9 License activation Current license status, machine code, activation key, state-driven actions, account No 8.9.10 About Software information, server notices, feedback, agreements and notices No 8.9.10 The most common blocker: the global lock Default state There is a checkbox at the bottom of the window, Unlock all settings , unticked by default . While it is unticked, every checkbox, input and button on the other six tabs is gray, except on General , AI settings , License activation and About : Tab While locked Export defaults Checkboxes gray, lock switches gray Context menu Menu item switches gray, double-click command radios gray Supported formats Text box read-only Texture suffixes Alias text box read-only (the page's Restore defaults button is gray too) Sub-libraries and categories Sub-library list, ID / display name and category list all gray ( the Show in main UI checkbox still works ) Other configuration Text boxes read-only How to unlock Tick Unlock all settings ; A configuration change warning appears, listing which tabs will be unlocked and warning that a wrong configuration can break library features; Click Yes → all six tabs become editable; click No → the checkbox untickes itself and nothing happens; Remember to save; unticking Unlock all settings locks them again (and does not auto-save). 警告 The lock is not a security boundary, only misclick protection. Once unlocked you change the library's underlying behavior (export formats, context menu, file recognition, texture channel recognition), and a wrong value can break import and export. The second confirmation while unlocked Clicking Apply or OK while unlocked shows one more "configuration change confirmation" ("currently unlocked, non-general configuration may have been modified… apply the current settings anyway?"). Answering No means this save does not happen. Bottom buttons Button Effect Notes Unlock all settings (checkbox) Unlocks / locks the six advanced tabs Unticked by default; the unlock state itself is never saved Restore defaults After confirmation, resets a batch of settings to defaults See "What restore defaults really restores" below Settings help (orange que

AI features and dependencies Control Type Effect Default What changing it does Needs unlock AI dependency check Button Inspects AI dependencies, generates a report and opens it in Notepad — (action button) A read-only check that changes nothing; the status line shows the report path and how many items are missing No One-click install AI features and dependencies Button Installs missing dependencies step by step (Ollama / embedding model / index / lightweight image sidecar) — (action button) First asks for confirmation listing the steps and sizes; installation shows progress and can be cancelled; after a failure, clicking again only adds what is missing (tick force reinstall to overwrite) No Remove AI dependencies Button Uninstalls the official pipeline / image sidecar / vector index / Ollama models — (action button) Shows checkboxes plus a second confirmation; installed items are deleted and AI search / analysis stop working No Last check status Read-only text Shows the result of the last check / install "Last check: not checked (click AI dependency check to generate a report)" — No 2. Vector index maintenance Control Type Effect Default What changing it does Needs unlock Update vectors Button Incrementally syncs the current asset library's vector index: only new / changed assets are re-embedded, and image / media indexes only refresh existing entries — (action button) Deletes nothing and needs no confirmation ; it runs the same command as the background auto update. The progress dialog shows live logs and supports cancellation (finished rows are kept and continue next time); the status line reports the result No Rebuild all vector indexes Button Deletes and re-embeds the help, documentation and current library vector indexes (text / image / audio / video) for the current backend — (action button) Asks for confirmation first; this is a full rebuild, not an incremental sync, and the time grows with library size; AI retrieval temporarily falls back to lexical (keyword) search meanwhile No Index status Read-only text Shows "Updating… / Rebuilding…" plus the last result (success, or the number of failures) Empty Update and rebuild share this status line No 提示 To make newly added assets searchable right away, click Update vectors ; only switch embedding models / backends or suspect index corruption before using Rebuild all vector indexes . 警告 Semantic AI search is unavailable during a rebuild (falling back to keywords), which can take a while with large libraries. Do not run a large import while rebuilding, or the fresh index lags again immediately. 3. items.text: One-line summary: this page is one large text box with one file extension per line — they are the whitelist the library treats as "asset files". This page is locked by default : tick Unlock all settings and accept the warning first (see 8.9.1 ). How to open it Settings window → tick Unlock all settings → the Supported formats tab. Controls and defaults Control Type Effect Default What changing it does Needs unlock Extension list Multi-line monospaced text box (one extension per line) The whitelist of extensions the library treats as asset files See the factory list below (40 entries including .zasset , .ma , .png , .wav and so on) Remove one → those files are ignored when collecting a whole folder and rejected on drop; add an unrelated one → unrelated files get collected as asset files Yes Hint line Read-only text "One file extension per line; click Apply after editing" — — No Factory list Category Extensions Asset package / project / geometry .zasset _zasset .ma .mb .fbx .obj .abc .usd .usda .usdc .glb .gltf .dae Cache / proxy / mapping .ass .rs .proxy .vrmesh .vdb .mcm Image / texture / thumbnail .png .jpg .jpeg .exr .hdr .tga .tiff .tif .bmp .psd .sicon .aicon Audio / animation data .wav .mp3 .aiff .aif .flac .ogg .m4a .aac .atom What this list actually governs Scenario Description Collecting a whole folder into the library Uses this whitelist to decide which root-level files count as asset files (geometry / textures / audio…); unknown ones are skipped The Import from outside file chooser The file filter is built from this list (see 8.4.2 ) Drop acceptance When dropping files into the asset area, this list plus the current category's supported import modes decide whether they are accepted Note that it does not decide whether Maya can import a format (that is Maya's / the renderer's business), and it does not replace the geometry / image extensions on the Other configuration page (those only sort files when collecting a whole folder, see 8.9.9 ). Things to watch when editing One per line, with the dot ( .fbx , not fbx ); empty lines are ignored; You must click Apply or OK to write the configuration; Cancel saves nothing; Removing a common suffix shows up as "the files are there but never collected / drops are refused", the most common trap; Adding unrelated suffixes (such as .txt ) makes readme files get collected as assets. Undo Situation How to undo Not saved yet Click Cancel Saved and you want the factory list Restore defaults does not reset this page (see 8.9.1 ); paste the factory list above back by hand, or overwrite with a backed-up config.json ( <plugin dir>\Assets\preset\ ) 警告 This is the library's recognition whitelist, and a mistake directly affects folder collection and drop import. Copy config.json somewhere safe before editing. items.text: One-line summary: three lists: which extensions count as geometry, which as images, and which nodes count as material nodes. This page is locked by default : tick Unlock all settings and accept the warning first (see 8.9.1 ). How to open it Settings window → tick Unlock all settings → the Other configuration tab → select the list to edit on the left. Control details Control Type Effect Default What changing it does Needs unlock Configuration list Left list Chooses which list to edit Geometry extensions The right side shows that item's full explanation and editor Yes Description line Read-only text A full explanation that follows the selected item — — No Edit hint Read-only text "One per line; click Apply after editing" — — No List editor Multi-line monospaced text box (one value per line) Edits the selected list See the three default lists below See each item's "what changing it does" Yes What the three lists are 1. Geometry extensions Effect : extensions recognized as geometry files on import (such as .ma , .fbx , .obj ). Default : .ma .mb .fbx .obj .abc .usd .usda .usdc .glb .gltf .dae .ass .proxy .vrmesh .vdb What changing it does : it only applies to the collect a whole folder into the library path — root-level files are split into node.{ext} (geometry) by this list; collecting a single file infers the sub-library from the built-in table and is unaffected. Trap : without .fbx , FBX files are not recognized as geometry when collecting a whole folder. 2. Image / texture extensions Effect : extensions recognized as image / texture files on import (such as .png , .exr , .hdr ). Default : .png .jpg .jpeg .exr .hdr .tga .tiff .tif .bmp .psd What changing it does : again it only applies to collecting a whole folder (matching files go into textures/ ); texture scanning and single-file collection use the built-in table and are unaffected. Trap : without .exr , EXR textures in a PBR set do not come in with the rest. 3. Material node types Effect : used on export / update asset to decide which scene nodes count as material nodes. Default : aiStandardSurface , standardSurface , lambert , blinn , phong , openPBRSurface , pxrSurface , aiHair , aiSkin , aiVolume , VRayMtl , RedshiftMaterial What changing it does : asset export, right-click Update asset and batch export all read this list; it is their only source . Trap : missing your renderer's material (for example only Redshift installed but RedshiftStandardMaterial not listed) makes export report no material node, producing an empty asset or a "material only" error (see 4.3.5.1 ); adding too much (such as transform ) makes non-material nodes count as materials. General editing rules One value per line; extensions need the dot, and Maya node names keep their original case; Empty lines are ignored; You must click Apply or OK to write config.json ; The three lists are independent, and switching items on the left automatically saves the previous item's edits. Undo Situation How to undo Not saved yet Click Cancel Already saved Click Restore defaults → the three lists on this page return to the built-in factory values (this differs from the Supported formats page, see 8.9.1 ); then click Apply / OK to write them config.json damaged by hand Overwrite with a backed-up config.json ( <plugin dir>\Assets\preset\ ) 警告 Material node types directly affect whether export can detect materials. Before changing them, test an export on a small library and only use it on the real library once it works. items.text: One-line summary: this window decides what from the Maya scene goes into a library asset, in which formats, under which name. What this window is for It is called Create asset on the interface and in its title, and it is the window with the most controls in the whole plug-in and the easiest to be intimidated by. It creates no geometry : it exports the current Maya selection (objects, material nodes) into a .zasset asset, packing thumbnails, textures and material presets into the current category. The window is non-modal : you can keep changing the selection and the viewport in Maya while it is open, then click Create asset on the left. One click does not necessarily produce one asset — it depends on the export mode (see 8.10.2 ). Where it opens from Entry Location Prerequisite What happens on click Toolbar button The toolbar above the asset area, Create asset (disk icon) A specific category is selected in the left tree Opens the window with empty configuration; whatever is selected in Maya gets exported Blank space in the asset area Right-click → Create asset As above As above Updating an existing asset Asset card right-click → Update asset → choose a mode On an existing asset Opens the same window pre-filled with name / tags , with existing formats marked "(exists)" Nothing happens / a prompt appears instead Prompt text Cause What to do Please select a specific category before creating an asset. The tree is on All assets or on a sub-library root node Open the sub-library and select a specific category Please select a target category in the left category tree first. The window is open but the category was switched away when you clicked Select a category and click Create asset again Please select the objects to export in the Maya viewport first (material nodes or objects). Nothing is selected in Maya Select objects or material nodes in the scene / Outliner Assets in the images / audio categories are files themselves; creating from the scene is not supported. You are in the images or audio sub-library Use import for those, not create asset (The window does not appear at all) You are in the Animation data category The same button runs "export animation data", which is a different feature How it is divided The left column decides how this export runs (button, mode, naming, thumbnail source, tags) and the right column decides what content and which formats . items.summary: One-line summary: the right column decides what goes into the package: whether associated files come along, which formats materials and geometry use, and how an
items.text: One-line summary: the right column decides what goes into the package: whether associated files come along, which formats materials and geometry use, and how animation / caches / proxies are carried. Block overview Block (top to bottom) Controls What it governs Details Collect associated files Collect caches / proxies / references loaded in the scene, textures Whether textures and scene dependencies are copied into the package 8.10.5 Export options Material only (skip geometry / proxies) Stores only the material network, no geometry 8.10.6 Material formats / light formats / node formats .zmetal (.zlight for lights), write all into one, material mapping .mcm How material / node presets are stored 8.10.6 Geometry formats (through Maya's native export) Maya ASCII .ma, Maya Binary .mb, FBX .fbx, OBJ .obj, USD .usd Which geometry formats are stored 8.10.6 Animation export Current frame / timeline / keyframes Whether animation is included, and which segment 8.10.7 Cache formats Alembic .abc Whether a point cache is stored 8.10.7 Proxy formats Arnold .ass, Redshift .rs, V-Ray .vrscene, .vrmesh Whether render proxies are stored 8.10.7 Block titles follow the category: materials shows "Material formats", lights shows "Light formats", and models / scenes / node tree show "Node formats". Light assets do not show the material mapping (.mcm) row beyond "material only". Three rules to remember first No usable format ticked = hollow asset . Near the end of the export the plug-in checks whether any file was produced for the expected formats and aborts with an error; but if you untick every format it still produces a shell with only meta and a thumbnail, so tick at least one. A grayed format is not broken , it is unsupported by the current category. Hovering says "this format does not apply to the current category and is locked (adjust in Settings → Export defaults)". Locking rules: materials / lights lock geometry and proxy formats (they have no geometry anyway), while textures / HDR / images / audio / animation data lock nearly everything. The small text after a format is plug-in status : "Ready" = can export; "Not loaded" = installed but not loaded, which may auto-load during export or may fail; "Unavailable" = plug-in missing, and the checkbox turns gray. The status text is not a format description. How to read the plug-in status after a format Status Meaning What happens Ready (green) The plug-in that format needs is loaded, or it is built into Maya (.ma/.mb) Exports normally Not loaded (yellow) The plug-in is installed but not loaded (such as fbxmaya, mtoa, vrayformaya) Most cases auto-load during export; if it still fails, check the Script Editor Unavailable (red) The matching plug-in is not installed The checkbox is disabled and never enters the export configuration The notice in append-format mode When you come in through Update asset → Append format , a yellow notice appears at the top of the right column: "Append format: no format is ticked by default; tick the formats to write this time; ticking an existing format (marked 'exists') replaces it with this export, while unticked formats stay as they are." In this mode all formats start unticked , unlike a normal create asset (which follows the export preset). Suggested minimal configuration Asset type Suggested ticks Materials Material preset .zmetal (plus material mapping .mcm if the asset contains a model and needs multi-material detection) Models Maya ASCII .ma; add FBX .fbx for cross-software use Scenes Maya ASCII .ma plus textures Lights Light preset .zlight Textures / HDR No format ticks needed (these assets are files themselves; just collect textures) Related Collecting associated files and textures: 8.10.5 Material nodes and geometry formats: 8.10.6 Animation, caches and proxies: 8.10.7 Where the default ticks come from (Export defaults page): 8.9.4 , 4.3.4.1 The user-guide version of the right column: 4.3.2.2

items.text: One-line summary: the third block of the left column decides where the asset card image comes from — your own rectangle capture, a Maya playblast, or a render. Item-by-item details Control Type Effect Suggested value What filling it in wrongly does Screenshot tool Radio Clicking Create asset shows a capture overlay; you drag a rectangle over the viewport and release to capture Use this (default) for the first export or when you want an image quickly A crooked frame or an unrelated object ends up on the card; you can redo it later with right-click Update thumbnail → Capture Maya playblast Radio Captures through Maya playblast (the current viewport image) When you want a cleaner viewport image without waiting for a render It briefly occupies the viewport; in batches it captures one by one, which is slow Render image Radio Renders with the current renderer When you want a proper beauty render (Arnold / Redshift / V-Ray) Every image waits for a render, so many assets take a long time; a misconfigured renderer gives black images or failures Create model Dropdown button Lists the models under the plug-in's Assets/Meshes ; selecting one imports it into the current scene; hovering an entry shows a same-named PNG preview For materials / textures / lights, which have no geometry of their own , add a demo model before capturing When the directory is empty the item is gray and reads "(no model files in the Meshes directory)" Create light Dropdown button Lists the HDRIs under the plug-in's Assets/IBL ; selecting one builds a dome light for the current renderer; hovering shows a same-named PNG When the scene has no lights and captures come out black It cannot build when the current renderer is not Arnold / V-Ray / Redshift, and the Script Editor asks you to switch renderers Create model and Create light are import / build-light actions: they write nothing into the asset and do not capture for you — they only give material / texture assets something visible to shoot. How the three sources differ Aspect Screenshot tool Maya playblast Render image How the image is made You frame the viewport Maya playblast output The current renderer Speed Seconds Seconds per image Tens of seconds to minutes per image Image quality Viewport display Viewport display (can include wireframe) Full render Needs a person Yes (frame each time) No No In fully automatic batches Frame the first, reuse the framing afterwards (delay adjustable) Automatic per image Automatic per image Output size From the captured size and the thumbnail size in settings Same Same Screenshot delay It only appears in fully automatic mode, ranges from 0 to 60 seconds and defaults to 2 seconds (the factory value comes from the export preset's delay_ms ). It waits before the automatic capture so the viewport can refresh and the render can settle. Heavy scenes are safer at 3–5 seconds; 0 tends to capture an unfinished frame. Gestures when capturing with the screenshot tool After clicking Create asset a capture overlay appears. Drag a rectangle over the area you want as the thumbnail. Hold Ctrl to lock a square selection (thumbnails should be square, so holding it is recommended). Release to capture. To cancel: press Esc or right-click. This uses the same screenshot tool as Update thumbnail → Capture , see 4.1.7.2 . A complete example (a material asset needing a demo render) The scene is empty or holds only a material sphere: confirm the current renderer (Arnold / Redshift / V-Ray) first, otherwise Create light cannot build. In the left column of the export dialog click Create model , pick a sphere or box and place it. Click Create light and choose an HDRI to build a dome light (or use existing lights). Keep the thumbnail source on Screenshot tool and frame a good angle in the viewport. Click Create asset → drag a rectangle (hold Ctrl) → release. Check the new card's image; if you dislike it, right-click the card → Update thumbnail → Capture and frame again. Troubleshooting Symptom Possible cause
