how to install the AI assistant
items.summary: One-line summary: when you click AI assistant and no usable dsh runtime is detected on the machine, this window opens to say what is missing and how to install
items.text: One-line summary: when you click AI assistant and no usable dsh runtime is detected on the machine, this window opens to say what is missing and how to install it. dsh (DeepSeek Harness) is the runtime behind the plug-in's built-in AI chat panel; it is not a Python package but a Node program. So "installing the AI assistant" really means installing Node plus dsh , and this window guides both steps. When it appears Top toolbar AI tools → AI assistant ; No usable dsh runtime is found → this window opens automatically and the AI assistant cannot start. What the window holds Area / control Content or effect How to use it Warning icon plus summary "No usable dsh runtime detected on this machine, so the AI assistant cannot start." Explains the problem; it is not an error dialog "Install (requires Node ^22.19 or >=24 (24 LTS recommended)):" The Node version requirement (written as `^22.19 \ \ >=24`) Follow it if you install Node yourself Install command (a selectable read-only block) An npm i -g --prefix ... command pointing at the plug-in's runtime directory Use Copy install command below and run it in a terminal "After installing, return to Maya and click AI assistant again." The finishing action after a manual install Come back and click the AI assistant again "For detailed steps… click Open install help below" Points to the full documentation Read it when the command does not work Copy install command Copies the command to the clipboard (and shows an in-Maya notice "install command copied") The first step of the manual route Open install help Opens the bundled install help page (per-platform commands, verification, FAQ, official links) The first stop for troubleshooting Open website Opens the dsh website in a browser — Open GitHub Opens the dsh repository in a browser For source or version notes Close Closes the window without doing anything When you do not want to install now One-click install (recommended) The plug-in installs it: prepares portable Node and pulls dsh dependencies with npm The right choice for most people A complete install flow (recommended: one-click install) AI tools → AI assistant and this window appears; Click One-click install (recommended) ; A progress window appears (it does not block Maya, so you can keep working): titled "Installing the dsh runtime"; the description holds the full log path ( <dsh_home>/dsh_install.log ); a live scrolling log shows where it is stuck; a Cancel button; Wait for it to finish (network required, usually 1–5 minutes, longer on slow networks); Success: the progress window reads "dsh runtime ready, opening the AI assistant…" and the panel opens; Failure: the window shows the reason and suggests Copy install command for a manual install or Open install help for step-by-step instructions. The manual install route Use it when one-click install fails, when a corporate network blocks npm, or when you want to manage the Node version yourself. Click Copy install command in this window; Open a terminal (cmd or PowerShell) and paste and run it; The command's --prefix already points at the runtime directory the plug-in expects, so do not change the path , otherwise the plug-in still cannot find it; Return to Maya and click AI assistant again; If it still fails, click Open install help and follow the per-platform steps and verification. What you see afterwards The AI assistant panel opens normally (the panel itself is in 8.8.2 ); The AI tools menu's AI assistant item text follows the state (open / close / starting); The install log lands in <dsh_home>/dsh_install.log ; include it when reporting a problem. Risks and how to undo One-click install downloads from the network (portable Node plus dependency packages, hundreds of MB), so judge the traffic and time yourself. You can cancel during installation : cancelling only stops later steps and keeps what already installed; the next one-click install continues from what is missing. Installation never touches your asset library or the Maya sce

It only copies files and never changes content, imports into the library or touches Maya . "Mirror" here means "copy the matching files over", not two-way sync, and it never deletes extra files in the target. Where to open it Entry How Top toolbar Quick tools menu Quick tools → Batch mirror copy Script browser Script browser → add the plug-in's quicktools directory → double-click 批量镜像复制.py The window is titled "Batch mirror copy tool". What every control does Control Effect Suggested value Title "Batch mirror copy tool" The window's purpose — Help icon button Opens this tool's detailed help — Source folder: plus Browse Where to look for files Choose the assets' top directory Target folder: plus Browse Where files are copied Never choose the source folder itself (it reports "source and target must differ") File formats (comma separated, e.g. .exr, .hdr, .png) input (default .exr, .hdr, .png, .jpg ) Copies only these extensions; with or without the dot works, but follow the default style with dots Change it as needed to .png , .jpg, .jpeg and so on Checkbox Preview only (do not actually copy) Ticked = scan and log "which files would be copied" with no disk change Always tick it on the first run Checkbox Copy hierarchy Ticked = keep the source subdirectory structure; unticked = flatten everything into the target root Tick it to keep the classification structure Start copy Runs (in preview mode it only writes the log) — Clear log Clears the log area — Close Closes the window — Status line ("waiting to start..." / "processing" / "scanning files..." / "done") Current stage — Operation log: area Prints per entry: source / target scanned, formats, each file's [copied] / [skipped] already exists / [preview] would copy / [failed] , and totals at the end Use it to verify the result A complete flow Quick tools → Batch mirror copy ; Choose the asset directory as Source folder and the destination as Target folder (a new directory is easiest); Fill the formats you want, such as .png, .jpg ; Tick Preview only (do not actually copy) and click Start copy ; Read the totals at the end of the log and sample a few [preview] would copy lines to confirm the scope; Untick Preview only and decide whether to tick Copy hierarchy ; Click Start copy again; this time it really copies; Read the final "operation finished: total X, copied Y, skipped Z, failed W". Where the output lands Copied files land in the target folder ; With Copy hierarchy ticked the source subdirectory structure is rebuilt under the target; unticked, everything piles into the target root (which is how same-named files collide, see below); Failed files appear in the log as [failed] path - reason and are counted in the final totals. Behaviors to know A same-named file already in the target is skipped , with [skipped] already exists: path in the log — it never overwrites . So "replace the old with the new" cannot be done here: delete or rename the old file in the target before copying. It only copies: no deleting and no renaming : extra old files in the target are left alone and never cleaned. Without Copy hierarchy , same-named files from different subdirectories collide in the target root and the later one is skipped as "already exists" — so whenever the source has duplicate names, tick Copy hierarchy . Because the strategy is "skip if it exists", clicking Start copy repeatedly is safe and never piles up duplicates. Risks and how to undo Its only write is "add files to the target directory": no overwrite and no delete , so the risk is low. The worst case is "the target gained a pile of files": delete them using the [copied] paths in the log, or simply delete the whole target directory and start over. items.text: One-line summary: the plug-in's own offline help site — clicking the Use help button at the far right of the toolbar opens a local web page with contents on the left, search on top and on-this-page navigation on the right. It is a local web page , not online documentation: the plug-in starts a small HTTP service on this machine ( 127.0.0.1 , ports 8790–8799) and opens it in the system browser. So it works offline and is fast. Besides keywords, search also uses local semantic retrieval (when the AI dependencies are installed). How to open it The Use help button at the far right of the top toolbar (an icon button, tooltip "Use help"); The browser opens the help home page at an address like http://127.0.0.1:8793/ (the port may differ). Notes: Clicking it again within the same plug-in process reuses the running service (the port does not change). If no browser appears, look for [Help] opened help center: <url> in the Maya Script Editor and paste that URL into a browser manually. When the help service cannot start it falls back to the legacy help page ( Assets/help/help.html ), which has fewer features. Interface areas Area Contents How to use it Top bar Contents toggle (☰) on the left, the site name "Squirrel Asset Manager Help", the search box (placeholder "search features, settings, commands…"), the version on the right The search box is the main entry Left Contents The whole book as a chapter tree, expandable level by level Expansion state is remembered for next time Center body Title, breadcrumb, body; "Was this page helpful?" at the bottom Read it Right On this page The current page's h2 / h3 headings Click a heading to jump; the current section highlights as you scroll Breadcrumb above the body Help home / chapter / section / current page Click any level to go up Previous / Next at the bottom Pages in contents order Use them for sequential reading Home cards "What's new / 5-minute start / Interface overview / Common workflows / Shortcuts / Command reference / FAQ / Support and feedback" Click a card when unsure where to start Home Recent Pages you viewed recently (up to 8) Continue where you left off How to use search Action Effect Type in the top search box Each keystroke filters (lightly debounced); local lexical results appear first, then semantic results replace or merge in ↑ / ↓ Move through the result list Enter Open the selected result Esc Closes the dropdown and leaves the search box Click a result Jumps to that page Each result tells you at a glance whether it is worth clicking: Element Meaning Title The matched page title Type badge Page / concept / reference / troubleshooting / command Path line Its position in the book (chapter / section) Snippet Surrounding text with the matched word highlighted Mode note at the top "semantic + lexical" = both were used; "lexical search" = keywords only; "lexical search · semantic temporarily unavailable" = semantic retrieval is not active Deep links: opening a specific page The part after #/ in the address is the page id, so you can use: http://127.0.0.1:8793/#/15.14.9 — open "Material conversion tool" directly; http://127.0.0.1:8793/#/15.16.2 — open the menu item master index directly; http://127.0.0.1:8793/#/12.1.1?cmd=hdr_to_zasset — open the command reference page and highlight that command ( cmd= takes the command id). The page id is the id in each page's frontmatter, and it matches the heading under each page title in this dictionary. The plug-in also supports calls such as open_help_center("8.14.9") with an id, which behave like deep links. When search finds nothing (keyword tips) Speak plainly first, then use jargon. Search expands synonyms and many colloquial phrasings are already included (such as "font too small", "scale the UI", "model import", "material import", "missing textures", "crash", "frozen", "cannot find", "inaccurate search", "shortcuts", "semantic search"). Start with how you would normally say it. Use the exact UI wording. Help headings and bodies large

items.text: One-line summary: the small windows through which the plug-in talks to you: feedback you submit, and the various confirmation / error / progress prompts. No screenshot yet : the dialog-feedback.png image has not been produced. The control tables below describe the window; the screenshot will be added when available. 1. The feedback window How to open it Settings → About page → Feedback group → Send feedback. What every control does Control Effect How to fill it Type dropdown Feature error / crash / licensing issue / suggestion / other Choose the closest so it can be triaged Title input (placeholder "one sentence describing the issue (max 120 bytes)") One sentence stating the problem Write "what I did + what happened", not just "it broke" Details multi-line box (placeholder "reproduction steps, symptoms, expected result (20–4096 bytes)") The body Use three parts — steps / symptoms / expectation — and the steps are the most useful Contact (optional) input (placeholder "email / QQ / WeChat, optional") For a follow-up You can submit without it Submit feedback button Submits Disabled after success to prevent duplicates Close button Closes the window — Bottom message line Three outcomes: submitted, id: xxx / currently offline, saved locally and will retry when online / submission failed: reason Note the id for later communication A complete feedback flow Reproduce the problem and note the steps and symptoms (screenshots / logs help); Settings → About page → Send feedback ; Choose a type → write the title → write the details; Add contact details if you want a follow-up; Click Submit feedback ; Read the message line: submitted → note the id; offline → the content is stored locally and retried automatically once online (you need not keep the window open); failed → handle the stated reason (an unreachable service address, for example). How to write a useful report Must include : what you did, what you saw, what you expected; Attach when possible : log locations are in 6.8.1 and the report template in 6.8.3 ; No sensitive data : never paste keys / license codes into the description, and the contact field is optional. Risks and how to undo Feedback is sent to the server , and there is no "withdraw" once it succeeds — check the content (especially contact details) before submitting. Queued offline content is stored locally and retried when online; if you do not want it sent, do not submit before the network comes back. 2. Other prompt dialogs you will meet Dialog When it appears How to respond Information / warning / error prompts Immediate feedback on operations (such as "Maya is not connected", failure reasons) Read the text and follow it; note any error code Confirmation (Yes / No) Before dangerous operations (delete, deactivate license, batch convert, overwrite installed skills and so on) Read what it asks before clicking Yes ; clicking No does nothing Progress windows Long operations such as batch export, AI batch analysis, headless jobs and dsh installation Most can be cancelled; cancellation stops at the next checkpoint and finished work is kept Name conflict window Import / export hits a same-named asset Options are in 8.12.5 License prompt A restricted feature is used while unlicensed / expired It leads to the license window, see 8.15.2 Missing AI dependency prompt Semantic search / AI analysis lacks dependencies It leads to Settings → AI settings → install AI dependencies, see 8.9.3 Related Where the license page / software information / feedback live: 8.9.10 The license window (activate / deactivate): 8.15.2 The name conflict window: 8.12.5 Log locations and the feedback template: 6.8.1 / 6.8.3

items.text: One-line summary: the plug-in's built-in purchase page — plans, prices, benefits and the payment QR code all come from the server; scan and pay on your phone and the activation code is filled in automatically, then click Activate. How to open it Entry Condition Settings → License activation page → Buy license Always visible; clickable when unlicensed, expired, or within 15 days of expiry ; greyed out with a hover reason otherwise Account window → Purchase / renew Visible after signing in; same condition With plenty of license time left the button is gray and hovering explains why — this reduces invalid orders and is not a fault. Window structure Area Content Title / subtitle The sales page title and description delivered by the server Notice bar Server-configured announcements (campaigns, invoice notes); hidden when none Content card area Sales cards: plans and prices, benefit descriptions, link cards; content and layout are decided by the server; cards with an amount and working payment have Buy now QR area The "scan to pay" card that appears after clicking Buy now , see the next section Activation code area The Activation code input (placeholder SQAM-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX ) plus Paste and Activate Bottom Refresh on the left, Close on the right, and a status line at the very bottom How QR payment works Click Buy now on a card with an amount; The server creates an order and a scan to pay card is inserted at the top of the window: the payment QR code plus payment notes (including a payment reference code when one exists); Scan the code on your phone and pay; The client polls the order in the background (up to about 10 minutes); on success it: fills the activation code into the input below; sets the status line to "activation code received, click Activate to finish."; Click Activate and the license takes effect with the status line "licensed, you can close this window.". The QR image comes from the server; when it fails to load the card reads "payment code failed to load", so click Refresh at the bottom. Entering or pasting a code manually If you did not scan, or support sent you an activation code directly: Put the code in the Activation code input (or click Paste to take it from the clipboard); Click Activate . With an empty input, activating reports "enter or wait for an activation code first." Status text and exceptions Status / message Meaning What to do Fetching purchase information… Fetching the server's sales content Wait; click Refresh if it stalls Showing the content fetched last time (network unavailable) The fetch failed and the local cache was used Check the network and click Refresh The server has no sales content configured Nothing sellable was delivered Try later or contact sales Unable to fetch purchase information: … Network / server error Read the reason after the colon and retry or contact support Waiting for payment confirmation… (order xxx) The order exists and the payment result is being polled Finish the QR payment; simply close the window if you change your mind This order has expired, click Refresh to fetch again The order timed out (about 10 minutes) Click Refresh to create a new order The order was closed, refresh and retry The order was closed As above Cannot get the machine code… The licensing module is unavailable Open the license window first to check the status ( 8.15.2 ) Risks and how to undo The purchase window never changes the license itself : only clicking Activate (or activating in the license window) takes effect; Orders and QR codes come from the server; closing the window does not cancel an existing order, but unpaid orders expire on their own; Paid but the window is closed: reopen the purchase window and activate with the received code in the Activation code area; Clicking Buy now repeatedly creates new orders; the last QR code is the valid one. items.title: Supported formats and routing
items.summary: On import the extension decides the importer, and that importer turns the file into nodes in the Maya scene. Category Extensions Import behavior Geometry ma, mb
items.text: On import the extension decides the importer, and that importer turns the file into nodes in the Maya scene. Category Extensions Import behavior Geometry ma, mb, fbx, obj, usd, usda, usdc, abc, glb, gltf, dae Handed to Maya's file import; abc and usd are first copied into the project cache; ma/mb additionally rewrite texture paths and redirect linked dependencies Render proxies ass, rs, vrmesh, vrscene, proxy ass creates an Arnold StandIn; rs creates a RedshiftProxyMesh; vrmesh creates a V-Ray proxy; vrscene creates a VRayScene; proxy is imported as an ordinary file Volumes vdb Imported as an ordinary file; actual display depends on the renderer plug-in installed Textures png, jpg, jpeg, tga, tiff, tif, bmp, psd Creates a file node wired to a place2dTexture, with sRGB set by extension HDR hdr, exr Creates a file node set to Raw; importing HDR from the library can also go through "create environment light" Materials zmetal Rebuilds the shading network from the node network; textures are written to disk per the import policy Lights zlight Creates the light for the current renderer; dependencies such as HDR, IES and textures are written per the import policy Images (loose files) png, jpg, jpeg, tga, tif, bmp, exr and others Not through the geometry importer: right-click an image asset → 「导入为 file 节点」 (Import as file node) creates file + place2dTexture; 「创建 imagePlane」 (Create imagePlane) makes a viewport reference image; 「指定到选中材质槽」 (Assign to selected material slot) connects it to the color slot of the selected material Audio (loose files) wav, aiff (mp3 / flac / m4a / ogg / aac are first converted to a WAV copy) Right-click an audio asset → import to timeline / import to Time Editor / import to Trax Editor / import to camera sequencer; Maya only accepts wav and aiff Animation data .atom (packed inside a .zasset ) Right-click → 「导入动画」 (Import animation) (automatic mapping), 「导入动画（层级映射）…」 (Import animation (hierarchy mapping)…) or 「导入到选择属性」 (Import to selected attributes) ; it only writes keyframes, so the target hierarchy must exist in the scene Node trees .ma node networks inside a .zasset Right-click → 「导入 ma」 (Import ma) ; afterwards the newly created nodes are selected from the before/after difference (there may be no visible geometry — look in the Hypershade or Node Editor) Material mapping mcm Import the material first, then assign it to the selected object by vertex, face or edge topology matching The first categories above (geometry / materials / lights / textures / HDR) go through the format list of asset context menu → import ; the last four (images / audio / animation data / node trees) are loose files or special content , whose entries are the sub-library specific menu items rather than the format list — see 5.1.2 and the "Menu reference" pages 15.5.9 to 15.5.12 . hdr and exr are treated as HDR by the unified import entry and not as ordinary textures; when ordinary texture behavior is needed, use the 「导入贴图」 (Import texture) submenu of a texture asset. Texture formats never appear in the context menu's import format list; they are handled by the 「导入贴图」 (Import texture) submenu, and sicon and aicon cannot be imported at all. Available formats are read from formats or exported_formats in meta.json first; when those fields are missing the files inside the .zasset are scanned and inferred. That inference skips ordinary textures under textures/ and keeps only HDRs.

items.title: Choosing an importer
items.summary: When an asset has several formats, the double-click preset decides which one imports by default, while the context menu lets you pick a format for one occasion.
items.text: When an asset has several formats, the double-click preset decides which one imports by default, while the context menu lets you pick a format for one occasion. How the default format is decided Double-click import and drag-into-viewport share one rule: Read that sub-library's entry in Assets/preset/double_click_preset.json , falling back to the default section when it is not registered. Only when that sub-library's double-click command is import is the entry's option treated as an import format; textures double-click to "create material" and HDR to "create environment light", so their option never decides an import format. If that format is among the asset's available formats it is used; otherwise (including an empty option ) it falls back to the first available format . The double-click presets can be changed per sub-library in Settings → 右键菜单 (Context menu) → 双击命令 (Double-click command) . Choosing a format manually With only one available format the context menu shows 「导入 <format>」 (Import <format>) directly. With several formats the context menu shows an 「导入」 (Import) submenu listing each format. Versioned assets go through 「导入版本 / LOD」 (Import version / LOD) , choosing the version and LOD first and the format afterwards. Textures, lights and HDR use their own menus (import texture, create environment light, assign texture and so on). Images, audio, animation data and node trees also have their own entries (see the next section) and are not in the import format list. The four asset types with dedicated import entries These four are not geometry or materials, and their entries are the top items of the context menu , not the format list: Sub-library Dedicated entry after right-clicking the asset Result Details Images Import as file node / create imagePlane / assign to selected material slot / open image A file texture node, a viewport reference image, a texture on a material color slot, or just viewing the image 15.5.9 Audio Import to timeline / import to Time Editor / import to Trax Editor / import to camera sequencer; also 「转换为 WAV」 (Convert to WAV) The sound on a timeline sound node, a Time Editor audio clip, a Trax sound track or a sequencer shot 15.5.10 Animation data Import animation ▶ / import animation (hierarchy mapping)… / import to selected attributes ▶ Writes ATOM keyframes onto hierarchy and attributes that already exist in the scene 15.5.11 Node trees Import ma / add reference / preview nodes The node network enters the scene (new nodes are selected afterwards), or a read-only preview of the connections 15.5.12 A few preconditions: All four require a specific category selected in the left column; under 「全部资产」 (All assets) , favorites or the recycle bin the 「从外部导入」 (Import from Files) button is disabled (greyed out), and the empty-space context menu shows a grey line: 「当前分类不支持从外部导入」 (this category does not support importing from files) . 「指定到选中材质槽」 (Assign to selected material slot) needs a material node selected in the scene (only the color slot is recognized); without a selection it reports a failure. Animation data only writes keyframes and never creates skeletons or objects — when the scene lacks the matching hierarchy, use 「导入动画（层级映射）…」 (Import animation (hierarchy mapping)…) to point at it manually. Seeing nothing in the viewport after importing a node tree is normal: it contains only a node network, so look in the Hypershade or Node Editor; the newly created nodes are already selected. Where available formats come from Available formats come from the .zasset 's meta.json ; when the fields are missing the files inside the package are scanned. Ordinary textures, sicon and aicon never enter the import format list, with HDR as the exception.

items.title: Verifying import results
items.summary: After an import, check the selection, the Outliner, the Hypershade and the Script Editor log to confirm the asset really entered the scene. Prerequisites One li
items.text: After an import, check the selection, the Outliner, the Hypershade and the Script Editor log to confirm the asset really entered the scene. Prerequisites One library import has just finished and the format used is known. Maya's Script Editor is available (to read plug-in logs). Steps Check the current selection: after a material import the new material is selected; after a zlight import the new light is selected; some geometry imports select the new root nodes. Open the Outliner and confirm a new transform or shape exists. Imports go into the root namespace : , and Maya renames same-named nodes automatically. Open the Hypershade (Window > Rendering Editors > Hypershade) and confirm the material network and file node exist. Select the file node and check fileTextureName in the properties panel to confirm the texture points at sourceimages/ , the project cache or .zasset/textures/ . Open the Script Editor and read the logs starting with [ImportExecutor] , [FileImporter] or [Import] . Verify the result The log says 「导入成功」 (import succeeded) or 「已创建 N 个节点」 (created N nodes) and contains no "import failed" or "unknown format". The expected number of new nodes appears in the scene, and materials or lights can be found in the Hypershade and Outliner. Models, textures and lights look right in the viewport; textures are neither black nor missing. Where to verify the four special asset types Images, audio, animation data and node trees produce no geometry, so verification differs from the Outliner / Hypershade steps above: Sub-library Where to look afterwards Images A file node (with place2dTexture) appears in the Hypershade; check that fileTextureName points at a library file. An imagePlane is found in the Outliner by imagePlane Audio A sound waveform appears on the timeline (sound node); the Time Editor gains an audio clip; Trax gains a sound track; the camera sequencer shot carries the sound Animation data The target node's attributes receive keyframes: look at the curves in the Graph Editor / timeline; the matching hierarchy must exist beforehand Node trees You may see nothing new in the viewport — it is not geometry; look in the Hypershade / Node Editor, or simply at the current selection (new nodes are selected after import) If "nothing appears" for one of these four, first confirm with the table above that this is expected, then troubleshoot as described in 5.7.1 . Tips A log line such as 「无 … 映射路径，保留原材质/原灯光」 (no mapping path for …, keeping the original material / light) is not a failure: it means that item has no cross-renderer conversion path and the asset keeps its original type. Seeing only 「材质已创建（无选中物体，未赋予）」 (material created; no object selected, not assigned) means the material was built but nothing was selected to assign it to.

items.title: Import geometry
synonyms: put a model into the scene
items.summary: Right-click a model asset in the grid and choose a geometry format under 「导入」 (Import) to bring the model into the current Maya scene. Prerequisites A Maya scen
items.text: Right-click a model asset in the grid and choose a geometry format under 「导入」 (Import) to bring the model into the current Maya scene. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open and anything that must be kept has been saved. The model asset contains a geometry file such as ma, mb, fbx, obj, usd, abc, glb, gltf or dae. Steps Right-click the target model asset in the asset grid. With only one available format the menu shows 「导入 <format>」 (Import <format>) directly; with several formats expand the 「导入」 (Import) submenu. Choose the geometry format to use. Wait for the import log in the Script Editor. Verify the result A new transform appears in the Outliner; for some formats the plug-in selects the new root nodes. The Script Editor shows 「导入成功」 (import succeeded) or the import log of that format. For ma/mb the texture paths were rewritten and materials look right in the viewport; abc and usd were copied into the project cache. Tips Imports go into the root namespace : ; Maya renames automatically when a same-named node already exists. ma/mb rewrite texture paths per the dependency import policy and redirect linked files under deps/ . Formats that need persistent paths, such as abc and usd, are first copied into the project cache and then imported. If an fbx import does nothing, first check in Maya's plug-in manager that fbxmaya is loaded.

items.title: Import variants, versions and LODs
items.summary: Assets with variants, versions or LODs use the 「导入变体 / 版本」 (Import variant / version) submenu to import only the chosen piece of geometry. Prerequisites The ass
items.text: Assets with variants, versions or LODs use the 「导入变体 / 版本」 (Import variant / version) submenu to import only the chosen piece of geometry. Prerequisites The asset has variants (the variants section of variants.json is not empty), embedded versions (such as V1 , V2 ) or several LODs on its main version. The asset has been right-clicked in the grid. Menu titles Asset contents Menu title Variants plus separate versions 「导入变体 / 版本」 (Import variant / version) Variants only 「导入变体」 (Import variant) Only versions / LODs 「导入版本 / LOD」 (Import version / LOD) The main version is always first, followed by the versions and variants; each entry has a small thumbnail on the left, and hovering shows a large preview beside the menu. Steps Right-click the asset and expand the matching 「导入…」 (Import…) submenu. Choose the target: the main version, an embedded version or a variant entry. Choose the LOD: 「本体几何体」 (own geometry) is that variant's / version's LOD0 , and further levels are listed as LOD1 , LOD2 …; with no LODs the root geometry files are listed directly. When one level has several formats, expand the format submenu; entries are the format name or "format · file name". If that entry also carries .zmetal or .mcm , they are listed alongside the geometry formats and choosing them runs a material import instead. Verify the result Only the geometry of the chosen variant / version / LOD is added to the scene. The Script Editor shows [VariantImport] 导入变体几何体: <file> (<format>) and the import success log. Texture and material for a variant come from the asset root and need no extra selection. Tips Variant geometry is stored flat under variants/ ( <id>.<ext> , <id>_lodN.<ext> ), and the older sub-directory layout variants/<id>/ is still read for compatibility. The default LOD is set by default_lod in lods.json ; LOD0 always points at the geometry in the root and is not placed in a lod0/ sub-directory. To use a version's own materials as well, see "Per-version materials"; variants never carry their own materials.

items.title: Import materials
synonyms: put a material into the scene
items.summary: Right-click a material asset and choose .zmetal ; the plug-in rebuilds the complete shading network in the scene and writes the textures to disk per the import
items.text: Right-click a material asset and choose .zmetal ; the plug-in rebuilds the complete shading network in the scene and writes the textures to disk per the import policy. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open. The material asset contains node.zmetal ; assets exported by the quick tools do not contain node network data. Steps Right-click the material asset. With zmetal as the only format click 「导入 zmetal」 (Import zmetal) ; with several formats expand 「导入」 (Import) and choose zmetal . When the asset has textures at several resolutions, choose one in the 「选择贴图精度」 (Choose texture resolution) dialog; 「取消」 (Cancel) abandons the import. Wait for the node network to be built. Verify the result A complete material network appears in the Hypershade: shader, shadingGroup, file, place2dTexture and so on. The new material is selected after import; the Script Editor reports 「已创建 N 个节点」 (created N nodes) and 「已选中新建材质」 (new material selected) . The file node's fileTextureName points at the disk path for the chosen resolution. Tips Textures follow the texture import policy in Settings → 常规 (General) : copy into the project, read the asset directory directly, or keep the source path. After importing zmetal, if the current renderer differs from the material's original type, the plug-in converts to the current renderer's default material without asking ; to choose a target type, use 「转换导入」 (Convert import) in the context menu. When the log says 「不含 .zmetal 文件（不含节点网络数据）」 (no .zmetal file, no node network data) , use 「应用材质到选中」 (Apply material to selection) instead, or use the ma/mb material network inside the asset.

items.title: Import textures
synonyms: attach a texture in the scene
items.summary: Right-click a texture asset and use the 「导入贴图」 (Import texture) submenu to turn a single texture or a whole set into file nodes in the scene. Prerequisites A Ma
items.text: Right-click a texture asset and use the 「导入贴图」 (Import texture) submenu to turn a single texture or a whole set into file nodes in the scene. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open. The texture asset has readable image files under textures/ . Steps Right-click the texture asset and expand 「导入贴图」 (Import texture) . When the asset has several resolution directories, choose one first (such as 2K or 4K ); with a single level the file names are listed directly. Import one file: click the file name and the plug-in creates a file node and a place2dTexture, then selects that file node. Import the whole set: click 「导入全部」 (Import all) or 「导入全部 (<resolution>)」 (Import all (<resolution>)) and the plug-in creates the file nodes in bulk and makes them share one place2dTexture. Verify the result The matching number of file nodes appears in the Hypershade. After a single import that file node is selected. After a batch import every file node's UV connection points at the same place2dTexture, so adjusting that node changes all UVs together. Tips Color space follows the extension: png, jpg, jpeg, tga, tif, tiff, bmp and psd are sRGB; exr and hdr are Raw. Where textures are stored follows the texture import policy; 「拷贝贴图到项目」 (Copy textures into the project) copies them to sourceimages/squirrel_asset/ in the project. To connect a texture to an existing material use 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) ; to build a new material set use 「创建材质」 (Create material) .

items.title: Import lights
synonyms: put a light into the scene
items.summary: Right-click a light asset and choose zlight ; the plug-in creates light nodes for the current renderer and copies dependencies such as HDR, IES and textures. Pr
items.text: Right-click a light asset and choose zlight ; the plug-in creates light nodes for the current renderer and copies dependencies such as HDR, IES and textures. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open and the current renderer is decided. The light asset contains node.zlight . Steps Right-click the light asset. With zlight as the only format click 「导入 zlight」 (Import zlight) ; with several formats expand 「导入」 (Import) and choose zlight . When the light inside belongs to another renderer, confirm the conversion as prompted; a whole batch asks only once. Wait for the light creation and dependency copying to finish. Verify the result A new light transform and shape appear in the Outliner and the new light is selected after import. The light type matches the current renderer; color, intensity, exposure, color temperature and so on have been written. The Script Editor reports 「已创建 N 个灯光」 (created N lights) and dependencies are written per the import policy. Tips Cross-renderer conversion only supports Arnold, V-Ray and Redshift; native Maya lights are not converted. zlight converts directly into the current renderer's matching light by default; the standalone edition first creates it for the source renderer and then asks whether to convert. When importing formats such as ma/mb that contain lights of another renderer, the whole batch asks once whether to convert. Lights without a mapping path stay as they are, with only the log 「无 … 映射路径，保留原灯光」 (no mapping path for …, keeping the original light) . To apply only the parameters onto an existing light in the scene, use 「应用灯光参数到选中灯光」 (Apply light parameters to the selected light) .

items.title: Import HDRs and dome lights
synonyms: import an HDRI into the scene
items.summary: An HDR asset is used in the scene two ways: create a new dome light, or assign the HDR to an existing dome light. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open. The HDR as
items.text: An HDR asset is used in the scene two ways: create a new dome light, or assign the HDR to an existing dome light. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open. The HDR asset has .hdr or .exr files under textures/ . Steps Create a dome light Right-click the HDR asset and expand 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) . Choose a light template; templates come from the .ma files under the plug-in's Assets/HDR_ligt/ and differ per renderer. The plug-in imports the template, prepares the HDR path per the texture import policy and replaces the template's texture attribute. Assign to an existing dome light Select a dome light in the viewport or the Outliner. Right-click the HDR asset and choose 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . The plug-in connects the HDR to the selected light. Verify the result A new light appears in the Outliner, or the existing light's texture attribute is updated. The HDR file node's color space is Raw. The environment light works in a render preview and the background shows the matching HDR content. Tips The texture import policy decides whether the HDR is copied into the project, read from the asset directory directly or keeps its source path. Dragging an HDR straight into the viewport makes the plug-in silently choose a light template from the current renderer or the double-click preset, without a dialog. Creating an environment light clears the selection when it finishes; select the light manually to keep adjusting it.

items.title: Import scenes and animation
items.summary: Scene and dynamics assets use the same geometry import pipeline; formats that contain animation come in with a time range or frame sequence setting. Prerequisit
items.text: Scene and dynamics assets use the same geometry import pipeline; formats that contain animation come in with a time range or frame sequence setting. Prerequisites The current Maya scene is saved, so imported cameras and lights do not get confused with the existing scene. The scene asset contains ma, mb, fbx, usd, abc or similar, or an ass / rs frame sequence. Steps Right-click the scene or dynamics asset and click 「导入 ma」 (Import ma) (it runs directly with a single format; with several formats expand 「导入 ▶」 (Import ▶) ). Choose the format to import; multi-format assets list each format name. Wait for the import to finish. Play the timeline and check that the animation updates with the frames. Verify the result Nodes for the scene's models, cameras and lights appear in the Outliner. Within the dynamics asset's time range the model changes with the frames. Proxy nodes of ass / rs sequence assets have frame extension enabled ( useFrameExtension ); USD animation is imported over the overridden time range. The Script Editor shows the import success log. Related: four other asset types are not on this pipeline This page covers geometry assets such as scenes and dynamics. Images, audio, animation data and node trees are four other types with different entries and results: Asset Context menu entry Details Animation data (ATOM keyframes) 「导入动画 ▶」 (Import animation ▶) / 「导入动画（层级映射）…」 (Import animation (hierarchy mapping)…) / 「导入到选择属性 ▶」 (Import to selected attributes ▶) 15.5.11 Node trees (node networks) 「导入 ma」 (Import ma) 15.5.12 Audio (music) 「导入到时间轴 / 时间编辑器 / Trax 编辑器 / 摄像机序列器」 (Import to timeline / Time Editor / Trax Editor / camera sequencer) 15.5.10 Images 「导入为 file 节点 / 创建 imagePlane / 指定到选中材质槽 / 打开图像」 (Import as file node / create imagePlane / assign to selected material slot / open image) 15.5.9 Animation data and node trees are often used together : the node tree (or a model) provides the hierarchy in the scene, and then the animation data's keyframes are applied to that hierarchy. Tips USD animation import uses importTimeRange=override and readAnimData=1 , and the working range follows what the asset records. abc and usd are first copied into the project cache and then imported, avoiding temporary paths inside the asset package. A scene asset is merged into the current scene rather than opened as a new file; save the current scene before importing. Whether an ass / rs frame sequence enables frame extension depends on the ani record in the asset's meta.json .

items.title: Reference geometry
items.summary: 「添加引用」 (Add reference) uses a Maya Reference to bring the asset's geometry file into the scene; the scene keeps only the reference relationship and never copies
items.text: 「添加引用」 (Add reference) uses a Maya Reference to bring the asset's geometry file into the scene; the scene keeps only the reference relationship and never copies the model data. Prerequisites The asset contains one of ma, mb, fbx, abc, usd or obj. The Maya scene is saved. Steps Right-click the asset and choose 「添加引用」 (Add reference) . With one referenceable format it runs directly; with several, choose the format in the submenu. The plug-in creates a namespace named after the asset; duplicates get _1 , _2 appended. For ma/mb the default LOD's geometry is preferred, and the dependency import policy decides where the referenced file lives. After the reference is created, confirm the entry in the Reference Editor. Verify the result A namespaced reference node appears in the Outliner. The Reference Editor lists the referenced file and its namespace. For ma/mb the texture paths were rewritten per the texture policy and the referenced objects display correctly. Tips When the dependency policy is 「当前资产目录」 (current asset directory) or 「源文件目录」 (source file directory) the reference points directly at files inside the .zasset ; with 「拷贝到项目」 (copy into the project) they are copied to references/squirrel_asset/ in the project. Referenced objects cannot be vertex- or edge-edited in the current scene; to edit them open the referenced source file or remove the reference in the Reference Editor. Replacing the asset later does not refresh existing references automatically; reload them in the Reference Editor.

items.title: Importing versions and LODs
items.summary: A version represents a different design draft of the asset and a LOD represents a different detail level of the same version; both are chosen at import time. Ve
items.text: A version represents a different design draft of the asset and a LOD represents a different detail level of the same version; both are chosen at import time. Version versus LOD Concept Meaning Storage Effect on import Version Different design drafts of the same asset (such as V1, V2) A version directory under the parent asset, or variants/ on older models Decides which design is imported LOD Different detail levels of one version (such as lod0, lod1) Indexed in lods.json ; lod0 points at the version root geometry and the rest live in sub-directories Decides how many faces are imported Selection rules The context menu's 「导入版本 / LOD」 (Import version / LOD) only appears with several versions or several LODs on the main version . Choose the version first and then the LOD; the menu shows the LOD label and face count. When one LOD has several geometry formats, choose the format last. Without a choice the default_lod from lods.json is used; with no index the default geometry is taken from node.* in the root. Why they are separate Versions preserve design iterations and LODs control scene cost. Keeping them apart lets you switch detail levels inside one version without affecting the others. Tips A version root's .zmetal and .mcm appear in the submenu alongside the geometry files, and choosing them runs a material import. To use only the current version's own materials, import its .zmetal from that version directory after importing the geometry. The version and LOD indexes are written during export; editing the directories by hand does not update the index.

items.title: Per-version materials
items.summary: Per-version materials give one version its own .zmetal and textures, so importing that version can restore just that look. What it is The asset root can hold a
items.text: Per-version materials give one version its own .zmetal and textures, so importing that version can restore just that look. What it is The asset root can hold a shared material node.zmetal ; a version directory can also hold variants/<version>/node.zmetal with its own texture directory. The latter is that version's own material. How it is chosen at import When importing a version's material the plug-in reads variants/<version>/node.zmetal first. When that version has no material of its own it falls back to node.zmetal in the root. The textures of a per-version material are resolved within the version directory and written per the texture import policy. Entry points A version root's .zmetal appears in the 「导入版本 / LOD」 (Import version / LOD) submenu and can be imported by clicking it. variants/<version>/node.zmetal is resolved and imported by import_variant_material ; whether the matching interface menu entry is wired up is to be confirmed, so today it is used through that import function or an AI command. When that import fails it reports 「无法导入版本 … 的材质，请确认该版本包含独立的材质文件」 (cannot import the material of version …; confirm that version contains its own material file) . When it is needed Different versions of the same model use different colors or textures. A version must keep its own look without changing the shared material. Tips Per-version materials are written when a new version is exported, depending on whether zmetal export was checked for that export. The .zmetal entries in the 「导入版本 / LOD」 (Import version / LOD) submenu go straight to a material import, while the version material menu resolves explicitly per version. When a version material has the same name as the shared one, Maya renames it automatically in the scene and never overwrites the existing material.

items.title: Cross-renderer material conversion on import
synonyms: convert an Arnold material to V-Ray
items.summary: 「转换导入」 (Convert import) imports a material asset and immediately converts it to a chosen material type, so one asset fits different renderers. Prerequisites The
items.text: 「转换导入」 (Convert import) imports a material asset and immediately converts it to a chosen material type, so one asset fits different renderers. Prerequisites The material asset is a .zasset with an importable material format ( zmetal preferred). The target material type has a usable conversion path in the mapping table. Steps Right-click the material asset and expand 「转换导入」 (Convert import) . The submenu lists only target types that have a conversion path and labels the renderer (for example VRayMtl（VR） ). Click the target type; the plug-in imports the material network first, then converts each material and replaces the source ones in place. When it finishes the converted material is selected. Verify the result The material node type in the Hypershade equals the chosen target type. The original texture connections have migrated to the new material and the viewport look is broadly preserved. The Script Editor reports the number converted and the target type. Tips Automatic conversion only recognizes Arnold, V-Ray and Redshift; native Maya materials are not converted. Right-clicking 「导入」 (Import) also triggers conversion: zmetal without a confirmation, and other formats ask once per batch whether to convert to the current renderer's default material. Default materials per renderer: Arnold → aiStandardSurface , Redshift → RedshiftStandardMaterial , V-Ray → VRayMtl . With no mapping path the original material is kept and the log says 「无 … 映射路径」 (no mapping path for …) ; that is not a failure.

items.title: MCM material matching
items.summary: .mcm records the original model's vertex, face and edge counts plus the material assignments; on import those 3D signatures decide which material goes to the se
items.text: .mcm records the original model's vertex, face and edge counts plus the material assignments; on import those 3D signatures decide which material goes to the selected objects. Prerequisites One or more meshes to receive the material are selected in Maya. The asset contains .mcm ; having .zmetal as well is recommended, otherwise it falls back to the material network in .ma/.mb . The imported model's topology matches the export: no triangulation, point merging or added / removed faces. Steps Select the target model in the scene. Right-click the mcm asset, expand 「导入」 (Import) and choose mcm . The plug-in imports the material network first: .zmetal gives the node network, and with only .ma/.mb the materials are extracted from it while the imported geometry is deleted. The plug-in counts the selected object's vertices, faces and edges and compares them item by item with match_info in the .mcm . Objects that match receive the material; when the .mcm records per-face assignments they are applied per face as well. Verify the result The selected object shows the connected material in its Hypershade material attributes. The Script Editor reports [MCMImport] MCM 匹配: N/M . With per-face materials different faces of the model show different materials. Tips With nothing selected it reports 「请先选择要赋予材质的物体」 (select the objects to receive the material first) ; when none of the selected objects is a mesh it reports 「选中物体均无 mesh 数据」 (the selected objects contain no mesh data) . Objects that fail to match log 「选择物中无匹配 …，跳过」 (no match among the selected objects for …, skipping) and never receive the wrong material. Topology must match exactly; a model whose vertices, edges or faces changed after export cannot match. When mcm is missing from the context menu's import list, the asset's meta.json has no such entry under formats ; scanning files never infers mcm.

items.title: Apply a material to the selection
path: Apply a material to the selection
synonyms: put a material on a model
give the material to the selection
items.summary: Right-click a material or texture asset and choose 「为当前选择指定材质」 (Assign material to the current selection) ; the plug-in builds the material network and assigns
items.text: Right-click a material or texture asset and choose 「为当前选择指定材质」 (Assign material to the current selection) ; the plug-in builds the material network and assigns it to the selected objects. Prerequisites One or more objects are selected in Maya. The material asset contains .zmetal , or a .ma/.mb with a material network; a texture asset needs a properties record. Steps Select the target objects in the scene. Right-click the material or texture asset and choose 「为当前选择指定材质」 (Assign material to the current selection) . The plug-in picks a path from the asset's contents: With .zmetal : rebuild the node network and assign the root material to the selection. Without .zmetal but with .ma/.mb : import the material network and assign it to the selection. Texture only: create an openPBRSurface , connect the texture and assign it. Wait for the assignment to finish. Verify the result The selected object's shadingGroup points at the new material. The matching material node appears in the Hypershade. The Script Editor reports 「赋予材质 … → N 个物体」 (assigned material … to N objects) . Tips With nothing selected the material is only created, not assigned, and the log says 「材质已创建（无选中物体，未赋予）」 (material created; no object selected, not assigned) . When an asset has several root materials only the first usable one is assigned to the whole selection; for per-face assignment use MCM. A texture asset without properties cannot map channels, so the assignment stops.

items.title: Apply material parameters
items.summary: 「应用材质参数」 (Apply material parameters) only writes the asset's attribute values into the selected material nodes in the scene; it never creates or replaces a mate
items.text: 「应用材质参数」 (Apply material parameters) only writes the asset's attribute values into the selected material nodes in the scene; it never creates or replaces a material. Prerequisites One or more material nodes (shaders) are selected in Maya. The material asset contains .zmetal ; otherwise it falls back to the material network in .ma/.mb . Steps Select the target material node in the Hypershade or the viewport. Right-click the material asset and choose 「应用材质参数」 (Apply material parameters) . The plug-in writes depending on the case: Same type as the source material: the serialized attributes are copied directly. Different type: values are mapped through the .mmap files in Assets/material_mapper_presets/ before writing. Afterwards the modified material nodes are selected. Verify the result The target material's attribute values are updated. Textures and upstream nodes are reconnected per the mapping. The Script Editor reports 「已应用材质参数到 N 个材质」 (applied material parameters to N materials) . Tips With no material node selected it reports 「请先在场景中选中要应用参数的材质节点」 (select the material nodes to receive parameters first) . When the asset holds no material data it reports 「该资产不含材质数据（.zmetal）」 (this asset contains no material data (.zmetal)) . With no usable mapping path it reports 「未应用任何参数（目标材质类型缺少对应的映射文件）」 (nothing applied; the target material type has no mapping file) . This keeps the target material's node type and name and only changes attributes and connections.

items.title: Assign a texture
synonyms: give a texture to a material
items.summary: 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) connects a texture asset's image to the matching channel of the selected material, or connects an HDR to the selected dome light. Prereq
items.text: 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) connects a texture asset's image to the matching channel of the selected material, or connects an HDR to the selected dome light. Prerequisites The texture asset carries a properties record (describing what each texture is for). Texture case: one or more material nodes are selected. HDR case: a dome light is selected. Steps Texture asset: select the material node, right-click the texture asset and choose 「指定贴图到材质」 (Assign texture to material) . HDR asset: select the dome light, right-click the HDR asset and choose 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . The plug-in takes the texture at the asset's default resolution and connects it, according to its PBR role, to the texture attribute of the target material or light. Verify the result The target material gains a file node whose fileTextureName points at the matching texture inside the asset. The dome light's texture attribute points at the HDR file, with the Raw color space. The Script Editor reports how many nodes were assigned. Tips With nothing selected the messages are 「未选中任何对象，请先选中一个材质节点」 (nothing selected; select a material node first) or 「请先选中一个穹顶灯」 (select a dome light first) . 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) only changes connections and never creates material nodes; for a new material use 「创建材质」 (Create material) . Where textures and HDRs are stored follows the texture import policy.

items.title: Create a material
items.summary: 「创建材质」 (Create material) builds a new material node of a chosen type from a texture asset and connects the textures automatically according to their PBR roles.
items.text: 「创建材质」 (Create material) builds a new material node of a chosen type from a texture asset and connects the textures automatically according to their PBR roles. Prerequisites The texture asset carries a properties record. The renderer plug-in for the target material type is installed; uninstalled types are unavailable in the menu. Steps Right-click the texture asset and expand 「创建材质」 (Create material) . Choose a material type: openPBRSurface , aiStandardSurface , VRayMtl , RedshiftStandardMaterial , RedshiftOpenPBRMaterial , standardSurface , lambert and so on, as listed in material_presets in the current config.json . When the asset has several resolution directories, choose one. The plug-in creates the material node and connects base color, normal, roughness, metalness and other textures to their channels by role. Verify the result A new material node of the chosen type appears in the Hypershade. Texture channels are connected and the file nodes point at the matching resolution inside the asset. The Script Editor reports the material name, node type and number of textures. Tips This creates a new material and never modifies existing ones; to change the textures of an existing material use 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . The material name is the asset name plus the last four characters of the asset ID, avoiding clashes with same-named materials in the scene. Creation fails when the textures do not match properties ; check that the asset is a complete PBR asset. Without a chosen resolution the asset's default_resolution in meta.json is used.

items.title: Apply light parameters
items.summary: 「应用灯光参数到选中灯光」 (Apply light parameters to the selected light) writes a light asset's parameters into the light already selected in the scene; it never creates a
items.text: 「应用灯光参数到选中灯光」 (Apply light parameters to the selected light) writes a light asset's parameters into the light already selected in the scene; it never creates a light. Prerequisites One or more light nodes (transform or shape) are selected in Maya. The light asset contains .zlight ; otherwise it falls back to the light network in .ma/.mb . Steps Select the target light in the viewport or the Outliner. Right-click the light asset and choose 「应用灯光参数到选中灯光」 (Apply light parameters to the selected light) . The plug-in builds a temporary light from the .zlight under the source renderer to serve as the parameter source. Parameters are written item by item: same type writes directly, cross type maps through the .mmap files in Assets/light_mapper_presets/ . Afterwards the temporary source light is deleted and the modified light is selected. Verify the result Color, intensity, exposure, color temperature and texture attributes of the selected light match the asset. The Script Editor reports 「已应用 N 处灯光参数」 (applied N light parameter groups) . No temporary light is left in the scene. Tips With no light selected it reports 「未选中任何灯光节点」 (no light node selected) . With nothing applicable it reports 「没有可应用的灯光参数」 (no light parameters to apply) . When .zlight is missing and the .ma/.mb fallback also fails it reports 「.zasset 不含 .zlight 文件，且 .ma/.mb 回退失败」 (the .zasset contains no .zlight file and the .ma/.mb fallback failed) . This only changes parameters and never changes the light's type in the scene.

items.title: Create a dome light
items.summary: 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) builds a dome light from a built-in .ma template and sets the HDR asset as its environment texture. Prerequisites The HDR ass
items.text: 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) builds a dome light from a built-in .ma template and sets the HDR asset as its environment texture. Prerequisites The HDR asset has .hdr or .exr files under textures/ . The matching renderer's .ma template exists under the plug-in's Assets/HDR_ligt/ . Steps Right-click the HDR asset and expand 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) . Choose a template; template names correspond to dome lights of different renderers. The plug-in imports the template .ma and looks for the texture attribute among the nodes it just created. It prepares the HDR path per the texture import policy and writes it into the file node or the light's texture attribute. Generic node names are normalized and the selection is cleared at the end. Verify the result A dome light appears in the Outliner with the renderer's standard name (such as aiSkyDomeLight1 ). The light's environment texture points at the HDR file, with the Raw color space on the file node. The environment light works in a render preview. Tips 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) never modifies existing lights; to swap the HDR of an existing dome light use 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . The template list comes from Assets/HDR_ligt/ ; when that directory is empty there is nothing to choose. Dragging an HDR into the viewport silently picks a template from the current renderer or the double-click preset, matching the double-click behavior. Where the HDR is stored is decided by the texture import policy in Settings → 常规 (General) .

items.title: Drag into the viewport
items.summary: Drag an asset card out of the plug-in window and release over the Maya viewport; the plug-in completes the import automatically according to the asset type. Pre
items.text: Drag an asset card out of the plug-in window and release over the Maya viewport; the plug-in completes the import automatically according to the asset type. Prerequisites A Maya scene is open. The cursor drags from an asset card out of the plug-in window and lands inside the Maya viewport. Steps Hold an asset card and start dragging. Drag out of the plug-in window and move to the position you want in the viewport. Release. Wait for the plug-in to finish importing. Behavior by asset type Asset type Behavior after dropping Models, dynamics, scenes Imports with the default format; with snapping on it lands on the surface under the cursor Lights Imports with the default format; with snapping on it lights along the hit surface normal Materials, textures Assigns to the selected object if there is one; otherwise creates and selects the new material HDR Picks a template from the current renderer or the double-click preset and creates a dome light directly Node trees Imports ma ; the newly created nodes are selected afterwards (no visible geometry is normal) Animation data Asks for 「动画起始位置」 (animation start position) and then imports keyframes by hierarchy mapping; the hierarchy must exist in the scene Images, audio Dropping into the viewport does not import them : they are loose files and not part of the geometry drag pipeline. For images use the context menu's 「导入为 file 节点 / 创建 imagePlane」 (Import as file node / create imagePlane) ; for audio use 「导入到时间轴 / 时间编辑器 / Trax 编辑器 / 摄像机序列器」 (Import to timeline / Time Editor / Trax Editor / camera sequencer) Verify the result The asset appears in the scene, or the material is assigned to the selected object (images and audio do not take this path, see the table). The Script Editor shows a [DragDrop] log. When a multi-selection of snappable assets is dropped, they line up near the drop point. Tips Dragging never opens a format dialog; the format follows the same rule as double-click import. Dropping images or audio into the viewport does not import them (they have no geometry or audio import target), so this is not a "lost drag" — use the context menu. Node trees and animation data can be dropped, but what they import is not visible in the viewport (node network / keyframes). A mixed selection with different placement rules (such as models plus lights) skips snapping and imports item by item. The dragged thumbnail follows the cursor, and snappable assets also show a drop-point preview.

items.title: Snap to the surface
items.summary: With snapping on, dropped models, dynamics, scenes and lights land on the model surface under the cursor instead of at the origin. Prerequisites Settings → 常规 →
items.text: With snapping on, dropped models, dynamics, scenes and lights land on the model surface under the cursor instead of at the origin. Prerequisites Settings → 常规 → 拖放 (General → Drag and drop) → 拖入资产（模型 / 动态 / 场景 / 灯光）时吸附到场景表面 (snap assets dragged into the scene onto the surface) is checked, which is the default. A hittable mesh surface exists under the cursor. Steps Drag a snappable asset to the target position in the viewport. Release. The plug-in casts a ray at the cursor position to get the hit point and normal. After importing, it places the new root node at the hit point: models, dynamics and scenes stand up along the normal and lights shine along it. For a multi-selection drop the groups line up side by side by average width, and lights keep a gap based on the hit distance. Verify the result The asset lands on the surface under the cursor, not at the world origin. The model's local Y axis aligns with the surface normal, and the light's direction follows the normal. The Script Editor prints [DragDrop] 已吸附到 <mesh> 表面 with the drop point and normal. Tips When there is no snappable surface under the cursor or the drop point is outside the viewport, the asset imports at its original position and is never lost. A failed snap placement only falls back to "import at the original position"; the import itself still completes. With snapping off, the drop position is the asset's original position and no drop preview is shown. Images, audio, animation data and node trees do not snap : images and audio are not imported when dropped into the viewport, and animation data and node trees import straight into the scene (no placement and no drop preview). A mixed selection with different placement rules does not snap, avoiding two orientations in one batch.

items.title: Dragging selects
synonyms: the dragged one is not selected
items.summary: Dragging an unselected card first selects only it and then drags it; dragging a selected card brings the whole selection. Prerequisites The asset grid holds sev
items.text: Dragging an unselected card first selects only it and then drags it; dragging a selected card brings the whole selection. Prerequisites The asset grid holds several cards that can be dragged out of the plug-in window. A Maya scene is open. Rule Card state while dragging What is actually dragged in The card is in the selection The whole selection is dragged in The card is not in the selection (something else is selected) Only the dragged card, which is selected first This rule prevents "dragging B but importing the currently selected A". Steps Simply hold and drag the target card; if it is not in the selection it becomes the only selection automatically. To drag several assets at once, multi-select first and then hold any one of them. Drag out of the plug-in window and release in the viewport. Verify the result The cards highlighted during the drag match the assets actually imported. After a multi-selection drag the number of newly added assets equals the number selected. The IDs in the Script Editor's [DragDrop] 收到拖拽: [asset IDs…] match what you expect. Tips A single click also changes the selection; confirm the highlighted range before dragging. Dragging a selected card never changes the selection, and the batch imports using each asset's double-click preset format. A mixed selection of materials and models imports item by item without sharing a format. "Dragging selects" also holds for images and audio, but releasing over the viewport does not import them (see 5.6.1 ).

items.title: Hover preview
items.summary: While dragging an asset the thumbnail follows the cursor; snappable assets also show a translucent indicator disc and axes at the drop point, so you can see whe
items.text: While dragging an asset the thumbnail follows the cursor; snappable assets also show a translucent indicator disc and axes at the drop point, so you can see where it will land before releasing. Prerequisites The snapping toggle is on. Every asset in the batch is a snappable type (models, dynamics, scenes, lights) and uses the same placement rule. Steps Hold an asset card and drag it out of the plug-in window. Move the cursor over viewport surfaces and watch the trailing thumbnail and the drop indicator. Release once the drop point and orientation look right. What you see Drag thumbnail : a roughly 80×80 card thumbnail follows the cursor, with its hotspot at the image center. Drop indicator : when the cursor hits a surface, a translucent square plane is drawn at the hit point with two axes inside and a white dot marking the exact drop point. Models, dynamics and scenes show local X/Z axes; lights show X/Y axes. The axis rotated onto the normal is not drawn. While a drop preview is visible the drag thumbnail fades to 25% so it does not cover the axes. Verify the result Moving the cursor over model surfaces moves the indicator, which follows the surface orientation. The indicator hides when the cursor leaves hittable surfaces. After releasing, the asset's orientation matches the axes shown in the preview. Tips The preview is a translucent overlay on top of the viewport: it creates and deletes no scene nodes, never enters the undo stack and never changes the selection. Dragging materials, textures, HDRs, images, audio, animation data or node trees shows no drop preview, and neither does a mixed selection with different placement rules. Images and audio do not go through viewport import at all (dropping creates no nodes), so a drop preview would be meaningless. When the surface normal points almost straight down (−Y) the in-plane axes roll once abruptly; this is a singularity of the placement formula, not a drawing bug. In large scenes the preview lowers its intersection frequency automatically, favoring drag responsiveness.

items.title: Import failures
items.summary: For a failed import, read the Script Editor log first, then check item by item whether the format exists, the license is valid and the file is readable. Symptom
items.text: For a failed import, read the Script Editor log first, then check item by item whether the format exists, the license is valid and the file is readable. Symptoms Right-clicking 「导入」 (Import) adds nothing to the scene. The log says "import failed", "unknown format", "extraction failed" or "no .zmetal / .zlight / .mcm". A license prompt appears during the import. The 「从外部导入」 (Import from Files) button is greyed out (you are on 「全部资产」 (All assets) , favorites or the recycle bin with no target category). Dropping images or audio into the viewport does nothing; importing a node tree shows nothing in the scene; importing animation data leaves the model unmoved. Common causes and fixes Log or symptom Cause Fix [ImportExecutor] 未知格式 (unknown format) No file of that format inside the asset, or the format name is not in the routing table Choose another format in the context menu; confirm a file with that extension really exists in the .zasset [FileImporter] 提取失败 (extraction failed) Files inside the package are missing or cannot be extracted Re-export from the source files, or re-import the asset from a backup [ImportExecutor] .zasset 不含 .zmetal 文件 (the .zasset contains no .zmetal file) The asset was exported by a quick tool and has no node network Use 「应用材质到选中」 (Apply material to selection) or the ma/mb materials inside the asset [Licensing] 功能 'import' 被拒绝 (feature 'import' denied) The license expired or is invalid, so import is gated Activate or renew, then retry fbx does nothing The fbxmaya plug-in is not loaded Load it in Maya's plug-in manager and retry Proxy or volume formats do not display The matching renderer plug-in is not installed Install Arnold, V-Ray or Redshift and retry The import-from-files button is greyed out / the menu only says "this category does not support importing from files" You are on All assets, favorites or the recycle bin with no concrete target category Select a specific sub-library and category in the left column first Dropping images or audio into the viewport does nothing These are loose files and not part of the geometry drag pipeline Use the context menu: images → import as file node / create imagePlane; audio → import to timeline and so on (see 15.5.9 , 15.5.10 ) Animation data imports but the animation does not change The scene has no hierarchy matching the asset, so automatic mapping fails Use 「导入动画（层级映射）…」 (Import animation (hierarchy mapping)…) to point at the nodes, or select the target hierarchy and use 「导入到选择属性」 (Import to selected attributes) Nothing "visible" after importing a node tree A node tree has only a node network and no geometry; this is not a failure Look in the Hypershade / Node Editor; the new nodes are already selected 「指定到选中材质槽」 (Assign to selected material slot) reports a failure No material node is selected in the scene, or the selection is not a material Select the material node in the Hypershade / viewport first, or use import as file node and wire it yourself Verify the result After changing the format the log says 「导入成功」 (import succeeded) and the Outliner shows new nodes. Once the license is restored the same action no longer reports a denial. If it still fails Confirm the .zasset directory really contains a file of that format and that its size is not 0. For images and audio, first confirm the asset file exists (loose files sit in the category directory), then check that you used the matching import entry. Import using another format to tell whether the problem is one file or the whole import path. Report the full log together with the asset name; the traceback in the log points at the specific importer.

items.title: Missing dependencies
items.summary: Black textures or missing proxies and caches usually mean the path the import policy points at no longer exists, or the asset package never collected its depend
items.text: Black textures or missing proxies and caches usually mean the path the import policy points at no longer exists, or the asset package never collected its dependencies. Symptoms The material exists but the file node's texture path does not, so the viewport shows black or the default color. Proxy nodes for abc, vdb, ass and vrmesh report a missing file. Missing entries appear in the File Path Editor. The log reports texture copy or dependency redirection failures. Common causes Cause Typical situation The texture policy is 「源文件目录」 (source file directory) and the source files were moved or deleted After moving machines or reorganizing a disk The texture or dependency policy is 「当前资产目录」 (current asset directory) and the .zasset was moved The library was moved by hand Linked files were not collected on export, so deps/ is empty Only geometry was exported texture_map in meta.json does not match the actual file names An older asset, or files edited by hand Caches were not copied into the project directory Formats such as abc, vrmesh and vrscene referencing temporary paths An image asset's file was moved out of its category directory Library folders were reorganized by hand while the file node still points at the old path The audio codec is not accepted by Maya, or WAV conversion failed A damaged source file, or an mp3 / flac transcode failure Steps Use the File Path Editor to confirm the missing files' old and new paths. Open Settings → 常规 (General) , change the texture and dependency policy to 「拷贝到项目」 (copy into the project) and import again. Check whether .zasset/deps/ contains the matching caches, proxies and references; when empty, export again with linked-file collection checked. Re-import the asset and confirm the file and proxy nodes point at the new paths. Verify the result The File Path Editor no longer lists missing entries. Textures display correctly in the viewport and proxy nodes load their models. The Script Editor no longer reports copy or path redirection failures. If it still fails Point the texture directly at a file inside the asset package to confirm the file itself is readable. Use 「应用材质到选中」 (Apply material to selection) to rebuild the material network and rule out stale paths from an old material. When an image's file node lost its path, re-import that image into the library, or point fileTextureName back at the image file in the category directory; when audio to WAV fails, convert the source to a standard wav first and then add it to the library.

items.title: Name clashes
items.summary: Name clashes happen at two levels: a duplicate asset name gets a number appended when added to the library, and a duplicate node name is renamed by Maya when en
items.text: Name clashes happen at two levels: a duplicate asset name gets a number appended when added to the library, and a duplicate node name is renamed by Maya when entering the scene. Symptoms After importing an asset, name_001 appears in the grid. Imported nodes in the scene carry a numeric suffix and differ from the asset's original name. MCM matching or material assignment cannot find the target by name.
