Assets may be missing while the index lags, and the next search syncs incrementally. Results are shown isolated and never change asset data; clearing restores the original list. Choosing Use ordinary search when you know the name or tag; use AI search when you only remember the look, need a material description or want to speak colloquially; use the preview panel when you want to chat while looking, add reference images or build a wishlist.

items.title: The asset index
items.summary: The asset index encodes asset metadata and thumbnails into vectors ahead of time, so a search only encodes the query once and compares similarity instead of cal
items.text: The asset index encodes asset metadata and thumbnails into vectors ahead of time, so a search only encodes the query once and compares similarity instead of calling a large model every time. Three kinds of index Index Contents Default location Purpose Text semantic index Name, display name, tags, category, notes, description and so on <asset library>\.squirrel_ai_index\<official / ollama>\ Searching assets with colloquial Chinese Image vector index Image vectors of thumbnails (encoded by the sidecar) img\ in the same directory Search by image Media vector index Audio / video vectors media\ in the same directory Text-to-music, recorded-audio-to-music, video-to-video The index is split by backend : official-pipeline and Ollama vectors are not in the same space, so each backend uses its own sub-directory ( official\ / ollama\ ). Switching backends reads the matching copy, so they never mark each other stale or overwrite each other's rebuilds. With ai_asset_index_dir set, indexes move under that root in sub-directories split by "library + backend": text <root>\<library id>-<official|ollama> , images <root>\<library id>-<official|ollama>\img . Key design points The primary key is the library-relative path , not the asset UUID. UUIDs change between caches, live libraries and indexes, and using them silently mismatches. Every record carries a signature and a text digest, so only changed rows are re-embedded; additions, edits and deletions never require a full rebuild. The index records its library and model; a mismatch marks it unavailable with a rebuild command instead of returning wrong results. What it is not The index is derived data and contains no asset files; deleting it never damages assets and only makes the next search encode again. The index travels with the library, but when several people share a library put the index on each machine's local disk so concurrent writes from the same backend do not wait on each other. Automatic maintenance Opening or switching a library warms up its index in the background, and searches sync incrementally first. Building the index the first time is slower; afterwards usually only changed rows are processed.

items.title: The documentation index
items.summary: The documentation index is a vector copy of Maya commands, nodes, APIs and guides, stored under the knowledge base's kb/semantic ; it only serves Maya documenta
items.text: The documentation index is a vector copy of Maya commands, nodes, APIs and guides, stored under the knowledge base's kb/semantic ; it only serves Maya documentation search and is unrelated to the asset library. What it contains The local knowledge base holds about 17,000 entries typed as command, node, api, devguide or doc. The index only generates vectors for their names and descriptions; the body text is still read from the local knowledge base by source . The vector directory contains meta.json (build record), names.txt (entry names in row order), vectors.i8 (int8 quantized vectors) and scales.f32 (dequantization factors); it is 768-dimensional under the current default embedding model. When it is used Documentation search defaults to auto : lexical first, then semantic results are fused with lexical ones when available. When the semantic index is missing, Ollama is not running or the model is not pulled, it uses lexical only without reporting an error. Rebuilding After changing the embedding model, when dimensions do not match or entries were rebuilt on a large scale, run: python tools\build_semantic_index.py --model embeddinggemma-2:740m The "documentation vector index" step of the one-click install does the same thing and only rebuilds when the model changes. Notes The documentation index and the asset index record their models separately and never replace each other; rebuilding one does not speed up the other.

items.title: Status and diagnostics
items.summary: Index status can be checked without any network access: whether it is usable, which model it uses, how many entries it has, where it lives and whether it lags b
items.text: Index status can be checked without any network access: whether it is usable, which model it uses, how many entries it has, where it lives and whether it lags behind the library. Prerequisites An asset library is open; to check the documentation index the machine needs the knowledge base or the online fallback enabled. Steps Ask the AI assistant for the index status, or call the read-only command asset_semantic_status . Focus on four groups of fields: available and reason (whether and why), model / dim / count (model and scale), index_dir / library_id (location and owning library) and index_lag (whether it lags). For finer environment diagnostics run python tools\asset_index.py --status or --doctor ; for the image index use python tools\asset_vision_encode.py status --library "<library root>" . For the documentation index use maya_docs(action="status") , where semantic.diagnose lists which link is missing and the matching command. Verify the result available=true with index_lag.stale=false means the index is usable and keeps up with the library; reason is empty or only mentions optional features not installed. Tips and warnings The status query reads local files only and never uses the network; only --doctor probes Ollama and the models. index_lag.stale=true is not fatal, since the next search syncs incrementally; it is common on shared libraries. When the index in that directory belongs to another library it reports an error explicitly; never copy an index directory by hand to "fix" it.

items.title: Incremental and full sync
items.summary: Day to day only incremental syncing is needed: only added, changed and deleted rows are re-embedded. A full rebuild is reserved for a model change, a damaged in
items.text: Day to day only incremental syncing is needed: only added, changed and deleted rows are re-embedded. A full rebuild is reserved for a model change, a damaged index or a format upgrade. Syncs that happen automatically Opening or switching an asset library warms up its text index in the background, and search never waits for it. A search performs one incremental sync first; repeated syncing of the same state never touches the model. The image index refreshes only when the library is newer than the index; it is created cold on the first search by image. Manual syncing Settings → AI 设置 (AI settings) → 向量索引维护 (Vector index maintenance) has two buttons: 「更新向量」 (Update vectors) for incremental and 「重建全部向量索引」 (Rebuild all vector indexes) for full rebuilds; the group's description states that it covers the help library, the Maya documentation library and the current asset library's text / image / audio / video vector indexes. The command line works too: Text index (incremental): python tools\asset_index.py --sync . Text index (full): python tools\asset_index.py --rebuild . Image index (incremental): python tools\asset_vision_encode.py sync --library "<library root>" . Image index (full): add --rebuild to the command above. The index_sync command also works, with kind set to materials , images or both ; rebuild only affects the image index. Verify the result After syncing, check the entry count and update time with asset_semantic_status or python tools\asset_index.py --status ; --verify checks consistency. Tips and warnings The rebuild flag of index_sync only applies to the image index; to rebuild text fully use python tools\asset_index.py --rebuild . Never use --limit on the image sync as sampling, because it trims the index to the first N entries. With a fresh lock on the index directory, search skips syncing to avoid blocking; retry once the other side finishes.

items.title: Rebuilding and choosing models
items.summary: The embedding model defines the vector space; when the model, dimensions or text template change, the old index must be rebuilt or it can only be judged unavail
items.text: The embedding model defines the vector space; when the model, dimensions or text template change, the old index must be rebuilt or it can only be judged unavailable. When a rebuild is mandatory The embedding model changed, or the model recorded in the index differs from what is expected now. The index dimensions, primary key scheme or text template were upgraded. The index directory was copied by hand or points at another library. Index files are damaged or the consistency check fails. Steps Confirm the target model exists in Ollama: ollama list . Rebuild the asset text index: python tools\asset_index.py --rebuild --model <model name> . The default is embeddinggemma-2:740m . Rebuild the documentation index: python tools\build_semantic_index.py --model <model name> . Rebuild the image index: python tools\asset_vision_encode.py sync --library "<library root>" --rebuild --model gemma2 . Check the status back in the plug-in; reopen the plug-in window if needed so settings and environment variables apply. Verify the result asset_semantic_status shows available as true, model matching the target and count matching the number of assets; the semantic part of maya_docs(action="status") should be available as well. Tips and warnings Changing the model re-encodes the whole library and takes noticeably long with many assets; do not change it without reason. The environment variables and the models recorded in the indexes must agree: the asset index reads SQUIRREL_ASSET_EMBED_MODEL and the documentation index reads SQUIRREL_EMBED_MODEL , and they must match or only half the system works. Rebuilding the image index is heavy work, so prefer doing it while Maya is idle or unused.

items.title: Searching commands, nodes and the API
path: Searching commands, nodes and the API
items.summary: The Maya documentation knowledge base has no separate window; its entry is the maya_docs tool in the AI assistant or maya_doc_search on the command surface. Fir
items.text: The Maya documentation knowledge base has no separate window; its entry is the maya_docs tool in the AI assistant or maya_doc_search on the command surface. First find the name with a sentence, then read the details by name. The image is only a signpost: there is no separate documentation window and no documentation entry in the menu — click AI 助手 (AI assistant) first and ask it for commands, nodes or the API in the conversation. Results are returned in the chat, not in this menu. Prerequisites A local knowledge base exists or the online fallback is available; semantic retrieval also needs Ollama and the documentation index, while lexical retrieval does not. Steps Ask directly in the AI assistant, for example "how do I use polyReduce" or "how do I put objects along a curve". The assistant calls maya_docs(action="search", query="...", mode="auto") . You can limit type to command , node , api , devguide or doc , with limit up to 20. Read the name, type, plug-in, description and match field in the results and pick the exact name. Use the name for details: commands go through maya_docs(action="help") for live local parameters, nodes and the API through maya_docs(action="show") . Verify the result It returns status=ok with a count and a result list; match says whether the hit came from lexical, semantic or both. When a result's source starts with online: , the online fallback was used. Tips and warnings Command parameters should follow the live local help; the knowledge base is only a snapshot. mode="keyword" is fastest and fully offline; colloquial questions should use the default auto . Commands from installed plug-ins are usually absent from the offline library, so check the plug-in list first and then use live help.

items.title: Semantic and lexical fusion
items.summary: Documentation search runs lexical and semantic retrieval in parallel and fuses them with weighted RRF: lexical guarantees precision when you know the name, sema
items.text: Documentation search runs lexical and semantic retrieval in parallel and fuses them with weighted RRF: lexical guarantees precision when you know the name, semantics catches you when you do not. The four lexical layers Whole-string hit : the query appears verbatim in the original name or description, scoring highest. Multi-word AND : the query is split on whitespace and every word must appear in the name, description or flag / attribute summary. Synonym expansion : reads kb/aliases.json and maps "decimate" to polyReduce and "scatter" to MASH_Distribute . Ranking : by actionability tier, then score, then IDF weighting; alias hits on the name get another half tier. The semantic path The query is encoded into a vector, compared by cosine similarity against about 17,000 entry vectors and fused with the lexical results. The fusion constant RRF_K is 20, so one rank of difference weighs little, preventing an accidental single-path hit from overriding the other path. When lexical finds nothing, semantic results are returned alone; when the query is exactly a name, that name is locked so fusion cannot push it out. Fallback and diagnosis Without a semantic index, with Ollama stopped or the model not pulled, it uses lexical only without reporting an error. A failing semantic call trips a circuit breaker of about 60 seconds during which retrieval falls back to lexical. Each result's match says keyword , semantic or both , which tells you which path caused a problem.

items.title: Command details
items.summary: Once you have the exact name, use maya_docs(action="show") for structured details; for command parameters prefer the live local help, because it reflects the cu
items.text: Once you have the exact name, use maya_docs(action="show") for structured details; for command parameters prefer the live local help, because it reflects the current Maya version and installed plug-ins. The image is only a signpost: command details and node attributes are fetched with the maya_docs tool inside AI 助手 (AI assistant) , not from this menu. Prerequisites The exact name has been found by search; note that Maya commands are case-sensitive. Steps In the AI assistant say "show me the details of polyReduce", or call maya_docs(action="show", name="polyReduce") directly. It returns a compact summary by default: the synopsis, long and short flag names with types and related notes. When a long list exceeds the limit it names the remaining items. To focus on one parameter add flag="percentage" to get that flag's full description. For the complete body add full=true ; guide bodies can run to tens of thousands of characters, so use it sparingly. For a command's live parameters use maya_docs(action="help", name="polyReduce") , which goes through Maya's cmds.help . Verify the result It returns status=ok with the name, type and detail fields; a flag query returns only the target parameter's full description. An unknown name returns nearby candidates to retry with. Tips and warnings Node types cannot be looked up with cmds.help ; use show , because help only knows commands. The online fallback only has page bodies and no flag tables; parameter help requires a local Maya or the local knowledge base. Commands from installed plug-ins follow the live help, and the offline library may not include them.

items.title: Online fallback
items.summary: When this machine has no local knowledge base, or local retrieval finds nothing, the plug-in falls back to Autodesk's official help; that guarantees "you can lo
items.text: When this machine has no local knowledge base, or local retrieval finds nothing, the plug-in falls back to Autodesk's official help; that guarantees "you can look it up", but only page bodies, no command parameter tables. Why it exists Autodesk documentation may not be redistributed with the plug-in, so a local knowledge base can only be built on each machine. Users without one still need a way out, and the online fallback is that way. How it works The official help site exposes no public server-side search API, so the plug-in uses two stable public data sets instead: the site-wide table of contents and individual pages. Retrieval scores the table of contents by title and path, then fetches the matching page on demand and converts it to text. Result fields match the local library, and source is written as online:<product>/<version>/<language> so it is obvious the data is not local. Cache and network The table of contents is cached for 7 days and pages for 30 days under ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\help_cache . A single request times out after 30 seconds with up to 3 retries; offline, a cached answer is still returned and marked as cached. It queries Maya's official help by default; developer help is English only. The switch Off by default : once enabled, query keywords are sent to Autodesk (an overseas server), so you must turn it on yourself and agree separately. UI switch : Settings → AI → 本地文档没有时，在线查询 Maya 官方帮助 (query the official Maya help online when local docs are missing) . The first check opens a separate consent dialog; unchecking it at any time turns it off without a restart. Environment variables (they take precedence): MAYA_KB_ONLINE=1 ( true / yes / on ) forces it on; MAYA_KB_ONLINE=0 ( false / off / no ) forces it off. An explicitly set environment variable is never overridden by the UI switch. With it off and no local library, the only answer is a missing-data notice. Limits Online results have no flag tables; use the live local help for command parameters. For stable offline lookups, build a knowledge base on this machine.

items.title: Knowledge base status
synonyms: how big is the knowledge base
items.summary: The status page answers four questions: what the library holds, how large it is, how long since it was rebuilt and whether semantic retrieval works right now; i
items.text: The status page answers four questions: what the library holds, how large it is, how long since it was rebuilt and whether semantic retrieval works right now; it also says which source to trust for which query. The image is only a signpost: the status comes from having the assistant run maya_docs(action="status") ; the menu has no separate knowledge base status item. Prerequisites maya_docs can be called in the AI assistant, or the same command can be run on the command surface. Steps Have the assistant run maya_docs(action="status") . Read the entry count and its distribution by type (command / node / api / devguide / doc), each file's size and the alias count. Read the rebuild time and sources under rebuilt to judge whether the knowledge base is stale. Read semantic : model, dimensions, count, availability and reason; for an end-to-end check add probe=true , which sends one real embedding request. To see which plug-ins are installed, run maya_docs(action="plugins") , optionally filtered by plug-in name. Verify the result It returns status=ok with entries , by_type , semantic and authority ; with probe=true it adds the result of one real embedding call. Tips and warnings When the local library is missing it clearly states the current mode is online; do not assume local data exists. authority states the authoritative source: live help for command parameters, details for node attributes and retrieval for body text. When the knowledge base is stale or incomplete rebuild it with tools\rebuild_maya_doc_kb.py ; avoid heavy Maya work while it builds.

items.title: The MCP channel
items.summary: MCP is the standard channel through which external AI tools call the plug-in's capabilities; installing the skills alone is not enough — the tools the skill tex
items.text: MCP is the standard channel through which external AI tools call the plug-in's capabilities; installing the skills alone is not enough — the tools the skill text refers to must really exist. Two servers Name Purpose Depends on Maya squirrel-assets Search assets and drive Maya / Blender scenes, imports and exports Needs a live instance maya-kb Search the offline Maya knowledge base No, works without Maya running Both start over stdio: in source form python mcp\squirrel_mcp_server.py , and packaged builds are launched by the main program with sentinel arguments. squirrel-assets also writes --broker-url and --instance-id , with the backend at http://127.0.0.1:39002 by default. Which tools are exposed Not every command is exposed, only a high-frequency allowlist covering scene, assets, rendering and execution; the command list is always fetched live from the backend's /commands and never hard-coded. High-risk commands (such as running Python) are in the allowlist too, and callers should preview before running. How to attach it In Settings → AI 设置 (AI settings) → 外部 AI 工具 (External AI tools) group → 外部 AI 工具… (External AI tools…) check MCP for the target tool and the plug-in writes the entry into that tool's configuration file; when there is no configuration it can safely write, copy the snippet and paste it by hand. Boundaries The MCP entry never connects to Maya directly and never imports maya; it only talks to the local backend. Before writing another tool's configuration it backs it up, refuses to write when parsing fails and only adds or removes its own entries.

items.title: The dsh skill bundle
synonyms: how to teach AI to use the plug-in
items.summary: A skill bundle is a manual written for the AI: one directory and one SKILL.md per skill, stating when to use it, how to do the work and which pitfalls exist. So
items.text: A skill bundle is a manual written for the AI: one directory and one SKILL.md per skill, stating when to use it, how to do the work and which pitfalls exist. Source and destination The source directory is <plug-in directory>\dsh_plugins\skills , currently 13 bundled skills covering the asset library, asset conversion, Maya help, headless modeling, Bifrost, plug-in internals, script assets and more. Bundled dsh : before launching the web client each time, the plug-in idempotently lands the skills in <dshHome>\skills and writes user-level rules to <dshHome>\AGENTS.md ; the user does nothing. External tools : the same source lands in the other tool's skill root; outside dsh both the directory name and the frontmatter name carry a squirrel- prefix so they cannot clash with the user's existing skills. Why standing rules are also needed Skills load on demand and a model may act without reading them; the managed section of AGENTS.md is injected every session and enforces baselines such as "consult the help first, change the scene afterwards". Landing only touches its own section and keeps whatever the user wrote. Self-checks while landing Hosts usually ignore problems in skill files silently, so landing fixes fence lines, checks that name matches the directory name, verifies there is no UTF-8 BOM and that another tool's same-named directory is not overwritten. Updating and uninstalling Reinstalling first confirms the overwrite list; uninstalling uses the ledger to delete only our skills and leaves other skills in the same directory alone.

items.title: External AI tools panel
items.summary: The panel shows "skill landing" and "MCP channel" separately: the first teaches the other model how to proceed, the second makes the tools actually callable. Pr
items.text: The panel shows "skill landing" and "MCP channel" separately: the first teaches the other model how to proceed, the second makes the tools actually callable. Prerequisites The plug-in main window is open and the target tool is installed. The skill directory of some tools has not been verified on this machine and is marked "to be verified". Steps Open Settings → AI 设置 (AI settings) and click 「外部 AI 工具…」 (External AI tools…) in the 「外部 AI 工具」 (External AI tools) group. Find the target tool in the list and check the skill root it shows. When auto-detection is wrong click 「选择路径…」 (Choose path…) to set it by hand. Click 「安装技能」 (Install skills) . If that tool already has skills installed, the list of skills to be overwritten is shown first and installation continues only after confirmation. After installing read the status line and self-check results: they should show the skills in place with a count, and list any problems item by item. When MCP is needed check the matching 「MCP 通道」 (MCP channel) . For tools without a writable configuration click 「复制配置片段」 (Copy the configuration snippet) or 「手工配置说明」 (Manual configuration instructions) and paste it yourself. When it is no longer needed click 「移除技能」 (Remove skills) ; removal only deletes the batch recorded in the ledger. Verify the result The status shows 「技能已就位（N 个）」 (skills in place, N) , MCP shows as attached with the configuration file path, and after the other tool restarts you can see squirrel-* skills and the matching tools. Tips and warnings Operations in this panel write to disk directly and are not controlled by the Settings dialog's OK / Cancel. Another tool's configuration is backed up before writing; when it cannot be parsed the panel refuses to write. The path of a tool marked "to be verified" may be wrong, so confirm it before installing. Some clients only read their configuration at startup, so restart that tool after changing it.

items.title: Ports and instance binding
synonyms: which Maya does it connect to
items.summary: The plug-in finds Maya through two layers of ports: the backend port routes commands and Maya's commandPort provides the direct fallback; every Maya process is
items.text: The plug-in finds Maya through two layers of ports: the backend port routes commands and Maya's commandPort provides the direct fallback; every Maya process is a separate instance. Backend and instances The backend listens on http://127.0.0.1:39002 by default; when that port is taken it switches automatically and writes the actual address into the endpoint file ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\broker_endpoint.json . Each Maya registers as an instance named maya-<version>-<process id> . Tools act only on the instance bound to this conversation by default; cross-instance work must be allowed explicitly so multiple sessions are not confused. The AI assistant and external MCP clients connect to the same backend but can each choose which instance to bind; AI search reads the current library's index directly and does not go through the backend. Maya fallback ports When the backend is unavailable the plug-in can talk to Maya's commandPort directly. Ports are assigned by version: 7001 for 2026, 7002 for 2025 and so on; with several sessions of the same version the later one falls back to the 7110–7129 range and records it in bridge_port.log . Security boundaries All ports bind 127.0.0.1 only and are never exposed to the LAN. But a commandPort is equivalent to an arbitrary-code-execution entry: do not forward it to the internet and do not leave it open on untrusted networks. Confirming with several sessions First list the instances to see which are online and then decide what to operate on; never rely on "whichever responds first", which is the usual cause of cross-session mix-ups.

items.title: AI unavailable
synonyms: how to go back to ordinary search
items.summary: First work out which layer is broken: semantic search, visual analysis and the AI assistant are three independent paths, so one being unavailable does not mean
items.text: First work out which layer is broken: semantic search, visual analysis and the AI assistant are three independent paths, so one being unavailable does not mean the other two are broken. Symptoms and causes Symptom Common cause 「AI 服务不可用，已用关键词直接搜索」 (AI service unavailable; searched by keyword instead) Ollama is not running, the embedding model is not pulled, or the index is unavailable AI analysis says the model does not support images, or fails outright The current model is text-only, or no vision model exists The AI assistant will not open or prompts to install dsh is missing locally, or the Node version does not qualify Cloud model errors Missing API key, wrong endpoint or a network problem Steps First run Settings → AI 设置 (AI settings) → AI 功能与依赖 (AI features and dependencies) → AI 依赖检查 (AI dependency check) and use the report to locate the exact layer. Ollama: confirm ollama list works and run ollama serve when needed. Missing model: use 「一键安装」 (One-click install) to add the embedding or vision model. Index problems: follow the rebuild command in the report, or see the "Missing model or index" page. dsh problems: reinstall as described in "Install guide when dsh is missing". Cloud problems: check the provider, API key, API endpoint and model name. What still works after a fallback Search falls back to keywords and tags, and asset browsing, import and export are unaffected. Without AI analysis you can fill in the name, category and tags by hand. Without the AI assistant you can still use the main interface's AI search and the documentation command surface. If it still fails Report the dependency report, the end of the relevant logs and reproduction steps together; do not reinstall the whole dependency set repeatedly.

items.title: Missing model or index
items.summary: These problems usually come with an explicit error: model not found, index not built yet, index model differing from what is expected, or an index belonging to
items.text: These problems usually come with an explicit error: model not found, index not built yet, index model differing from what is expected, or an index belonging to another library. Symptoms, causes and fixes Model not found : the needed model was never pulled, or settings keep a deleted model name. Check with ollama list , pull the model, or choose an available model in the configuration. No asset library semantic index yet : that library never had one. Open the library and wait for the background warm-up, or run python tools\asset_index.py --sync . Index model differs from the expected one : the embedding model changed, or the index came from another configuration. Rebuild as prompted: python tools\asset_index.py --rebuild --model <model name> . Index belongs to another library : the index directory was copied by hand or points at the wrong place. Remove the override variable so the index returns to the in-library directory, or rebuild to take it over once the original library no longer needs it. Image retrieval unavailable : the sidecar venv is missing, numpy / Pillow are absent, or the image index was never built. Rerun the image part of the one-click install and then python tools\asset_vision_encode.py sync --library "<library root>" . Documentation semantics unavailable : the documentation index is missing or the model differs. Run python tools\build_semantic_index.py --model <model name> ; lexical retrieval still works without it. Verify the result asset_semantic_status reports available with a matching model, and the semantic part of maya_docs(action="status") is available too. If it still fails First check whether the index points at the wrong directory and then read the logs; never bypass the ownership check by copying an index directory by hand.

items.title: Irrelevant search results
items.summary: First decide whether "nothing was found" or "the ranking is wrong": the former is usually an index or metadata problem, the latter usually a description that is
items.text: First decide whether "nothing was found" or "the ranking is wrong": the former is usually an index or metadata problem, the latter usually a description that is too broad or a wrong scope. Symptoms and causes A freshly added asset is not found : the index lags. The next search syncs incrementally, or run python tools\asset_index.py --sync . Similar assets do not rank first : the name, tags and notes are too sparse, or there is no appearance description. The index text comes mainly from those fields. Several concepts blur together : one sentence mixes material, purpose and color and the semantics average out. Split it into two or three sentences, or use keyword mode. Wrong scope : a category is selected although you think you are searching the whole library; clear the category selection and retry. Everything is scrambled after changing models : the index and the current model differ, so it was judged unavailable and fell back to lexical. HDR assets are hard to tell apart : their thumbnails are all light-probe previews, which any retrieval struggles with; add scene or light-source tags manually. Steps Check asset_semantic_status and confirm it is available with index_lag.stale false. Add names, tags and notes to key assets; for assets with sparse metadata, generate an appearance description with a description tool first. Shorten the query and keep only the most important material or appearance words. Search within the right category, or switch to "search by image". When it is still inaccurate use mode="keyword" to verify whether the semantic path introduced the bias. If it still fails Record the original query, the expected asset name and the actual top results; that is the key evidence for telling index quality from metadata quality.

items.title: Connection timeouts
items.summary: For a timeout first decide whether the model is slow, the backend is not running, the network is blocked or the Maya main thread is busy; each layer is handled
items.text: For a timeout first decide whether the model is slow, the backend is not running, the network is blocked or the Maya main thread is busy; each layer is handled quite differently. Common symptoms and fixes The first semantic search or AI analysis is slow : a model needs time to load the first time; wait or retry once, and it should become clearly faster. Ollama request timed out : confirm http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags opens; if the system or environment sets a proxy ( HTTP_PROXY / HTTPS_PROXY ) without 127.0.0.1 in NO_PROXY , even loopback requests are intercepted. Raise SQUIRREL_EMBED_TIMEOUT when needed. Cloud endpoint timed out : check the API endpoint, key, network and proxy; try another available model. AI assistant reports the web client failed to start with an empty log and exit code 0 : almost always the Node version is too old and must be ^22.19 || >=24 . Use the one-click install for portable Node, or point SQUIRREL_NODE at a qualifying interpreter. The backend is unreachable : confirm it is running and read the actual port from ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\broker_endpoint.json ; it switches ports automatically when one is taken. A Maya command never returned : the main thread may be busy. Check late results and job state first, and never rerun a destructive command just because of one timeout. Verify the result The timing-out item returns normally, squirrel_list_instances shows the current Maya, and another dependency check reports no new gaps. If it still fails Use the crash / disconnect diagnostic tooling to check whether the port is really answering or merely listening ; listening does not mean healthy.

items.title: The quick tools menu
items.summary: All quick tools live behind the 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) button in the main window toolbar, and the menu lists the scripts in the plug-in's quicktools/ directory. P
items.text: All quick tools live behind the 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) button in the main window toolbar, and the menu lists the scripts in the plug-in's quicktools/ directory. Purpose The menu gathers HDR, model and PBR texture to asset conversion plus image conversion, batch processing, material tools and the script browser in one place, so you do not have to remember each script path. Tool list Script file Purpose Details hdr_to_zasset.py HDR/EXR environment texture → .zasset 9.2.1 model_to_zasset.py Model file → .zasset 9.2.2 pbr_to_zasset.py PBR textures → .zasset 9.2.3 图像格式转换工具.py (image format conversion tool) Batch image format conversion 9.3.1 批量处理maya文件.py (batch process Maya files) Run one script against several .ma / .mb files 9.4.1 批量镜像复制.py (batch mirror copy) Mirror a directory filtered by extension 9.4.2 材质导入导出工具(材质管理).py (material import/export tool) Material import and export ( .zmetal , MA+JSON) 9.5.1 材质转换工具.py (material conversion tool) Batch material type conversion 9.5.2 材质节点属性映射工具.py (material attribute mapping tool) Edit .mmap attribute mappings 9.5.3 脚本浏览器.py (script browser) Browse, search and run scripts 9.6.1 Steps Click 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) in the main window toolbar (tooltip 「快捷工具：运行 quicktools 目录里的脚本」 (quick tools: run scripts in the quicktools directory) ). The menu rescans quicktools/ every time it opens and lists the .py files inside. Click an entry to open the tool window, then choose inputs, set parameters and run it there. For conversion tools, check the configured output directory afterwards for the .zasset or converted files. Verify the result The menu lists tool entries instead of 「暂无快捷工具」 (no quick tools yet) . Clicking an entry opens its window normally. Conversion tools report success / failure counts in the status bar or a dialog, and the output directory contains the products. Notes The menu loads only .py files in the root of quicktools/ and never scans sub-directories; an entry name is the file name without .py and with underscores turned into spaces. New scripts need no registration and appear the next time the menu opens (see 9.7.1). A tool needs a main() , run() or if __name__ == "__main__" entry, otherwise clicking it does nothing (see 9.7.2). In the standalone edition, tools that need Maya are dispatched to an online Maya; 图像格式转换工具.py and 批量镜像复制.py are pure file tools that run locally.

items.title: How to run them (UI, command, script browser)
path: How to run them (UI, command, script browser)
synonyms: how to start a quick tool
items.summary: Quick tools have three run paths: the toolbar menu, the AI command quicktool_run , and the script browser or Script Editor; all three run the same script in qui
items.text: Quick tools have three run paths: the toolbar menu, the AI command quicktool_run , and the script browser or Script Editor; all three run the same script in quicktools/ . Prerequisites Tools that read or write the Maya scene must run inside Maya; the standalone edition dispatches them to an online Maya automatically. 图像格式转换工具.py and 批量镜像复制.py are pure file tools and can run locally. Path 1: the UI menu Click 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) in the main window toolbar. Choose a tool entry and follow the page instructions once its window opens. Path 2: the command channel Call quicktool_run ; without name it only returns the script list (including entry points and whether a first-class command already covers it). Pass name (with or without .py ) to run it, and optionally params as arguments. Add dry_run=true first to see which script and entry would be called without running it. name only accepts a bare file name inside quicktools/ ; path separators and .. are rejected. When a dedicated command exists, prefer it: hdr_to_zasset , model_to_zasset , pbr_to_zasset , convert_image_format , mirror_copy , convert_material , convert_import , material_conversion_info . Path 3: script browser / Script Editor The script browser scans script_assets/ and extra script roots by default; adding the quicktools/ directory as an extra script root lets you run them there (a general capability, not specially registered for quick tools). You can also run a .py directly in the Maya Script Editor, which is equivalent to running it as __main__ . Entry resolution order The menu and the command channel behave the same: main() → run() → run once as __main__ when the source contains if __name__ == "__main__" . When only main / run exists the module body is not executed again, so top-level side effects never run twice. Verify the result Menu path: the tool window appears. Command path: it returns status: ok , entry and opened: true ; for GUI tools this only means the window opened, not that the work finished. Script browser: the status bar shows success / failure and the elapsed time. Notes The menu calls main() / run() without arguments; scripts that need arguments must go through the command channel or "run with parameters". After the command channel returns, a GUI tool is still waiting for user interaction; do not treat that as a finished task.

items.title: Results and logs
items.summary: Quick tools write no central log file: results stay in each tool window, and progress output plus errors go to the Maya Script Editor history. Where to look Too
items.text: Quick tools write no central log file: results stay in each tool window, and progress output plus errors go to the Maya Script Editor history. Where to look Tool Where products and results appear HDR / model / PBR texture to asset .zasset in the configured output directory; a result tree, status bar and completion dialog in the window Image format conversion tool Converted images in the output directory; the conversion log, progress bar and completion dialog in the window Batch mirror copy Files copied with the same structure in the target folder; operation log, progress bar and a completion summary Batch process Maya files The .ma / .mb files themselves (when saving is checked); an execution log area and a closing summary Material import/export tool .zmetal / .ma / .mcm / .ameta and so on in the export directory; progress details printed to the Script Editor Material conversion tool New materials in the current scene; status bar, completion summary and a failed-material list Material attribute mapping tool .mmap files in Assets/material_mapper_presets ; a save prompt and Script Editor logs Script browser Success / failure and elapsed time in the status bar; the script's print , traceback and RESULT in the Script Editor Verify the result After a conversion tool finishes, open the configured output directory and confirm the new .zasset or target-format files. Open a .zasset and you should see meta.json , the source files (for example under textures/ ) and an optional thumb.sicon . Refresh or rescan the asset library and confirm the new assets are listed. Search the Maya Script Editor for the tool prefix (such as [HDR Tool] , [材质导出] or [QuickTool] ) to read progress output. Notes A single failed file usually does not abort the batch; trust the success / failure counts and the failure list. The script browser has no separate output panel: script output and tracebacks only appear in the Script Editor history, and failures open a copyable error dialog. The batch Maya file tool can 「保存日志」 (Save log) as .txt or 「复制日志」 (Copy log) to the clipboard. Each tool writes logs only into its own log area in the window (the Script Editor gets output as well); there are no extra log files on disk.

items.title: HDR to asset
items.summary: Package .hdr / .exr environment textures into .zasset files one per file, optionally generating tone-mapped thumbnails as well. Purpose Turn scattered environme
items.text: Package .hdr / .exr environment textures into .zasset files one per file, optionally generating tone-mapped thumbnails as well. Purpose Turn scattered environment textures into assets the library can recognize and preview, either one file at a time or a whole folder. The menu shows the script name : the quick tools menu scans the scripts in quicktools/ directly, and an entry name is the file name without .py with underscores replaced by spaces, so the menu shows hdr to zasset rather than a Chinese title. The three conversion tools map as follows: hdr to zasset = HDR to asset, model to zasset = model to asset, pbr to zasset = PBR texture to asset. Input and output Input: one or more .hdr / .exr files, or a folder (recursive, filterable by format). Output: one <file name>.zasset per source file, written to 「输出位置」 (Output location) ; in folder mode with 「保持层级结构」 (Keep hierarchy) checked it follows the source directory structure. Inside the asset: meta.json and textures/<original file name> , plus thumb.sicon when a thumbnail is generated. meta.json records asset_type: hdr , node_type: environmentMap , the resolution and tags ( hdr , environment , the extension). Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → hdr to zasset . Choose 「选择文件」 (Choose files) or 「选择文件夹」 (Choose folder) and click 「浏览...」 (Browse...) to set the input. In folder mode click 「扫描HDR文件」 (Scan HDR files) ; with 「递归扫描子文件夹」 (Scan sub-folders recursively) checked it searches recursively. Set 「输出位置」 (Output location) ; empty means the directory of the input files. Adjust the options under 「转换选项」 (Conversion options) as needed. Click 「转换」 (Convert) and wait for the progress to finish. Verify the result The status bar shows 「完成: x 成功, y 失败」 (finished: x succeeded, y failed) and a 「转换完成」 (conversion finished) dialog appears. The matching .zasset files appear in the output directory. After refreshing the library the assets show thumbnails and resolution information. Options and notes Option Default Notes Generate thumbnail preview On Generates a tone-mapped PNG thumbnail from the HDR/EXR Prefer an existing thumbnail On Searches for a same-named PNG/JPG next to the source file, with the search formats png, jpg by default Scan sub-folders recursively On Folder mode only; when off only the current directory is scanned Keep hierarchy On Folder mode only; when off all assets go into one directory Import into the current category after conversion Off Copies the .zasset into the current library category afterwards (without the directory structure) Format filter Empty Empty converts .hdr and .exr ; may be set to hdr or exr Thumbnails need cv2 / numpy and Pillow, and imageio improves EXR compatibility; when dependencies are missing it asks whether to skip thumbnails and keep converting. The thumbnail edge length follows 「默认缩略图大小」 (Default thumbnail size) in settings (512 by default) and only shrinks, never enlarges. Conversion needs a valid convert license. Older help recorded that Chinese file names could break conversion and recommended letters, digits and underscores (whether this still applies is to be confirmed).

items.title: Model to asset
items.summary: Group the model files in a folder by asset and package each one into a .zasset ; files with the same name but different formats merge into one asset. Purpose Tu
items.text: Group the model files in a folder by asset and package each one into a .zasset ; files with the same name but different formats merge into one asset. Purpose Turn .ma , .mb , .fbx , .obj , USD, Alembic and similar models, together with their textures and proxy caches, into uniform assets that are easy to add to the library and import later. The menu shows the script name : the quick tools menu scans the scripts in quicktools/ directly, and an entry name is the file name without .py with underscores replaced by spaces, so the menu shows model to zasset rather than a Chinese title. The three conversion tools map as follows: hdr to zasset = HDR to asset, model to zasset = model to asset, pbr to zasset = PBR texture to asset. Supported formats .ma , .mb , .usd , .usda , .usdc , .abc , .fbx , .obj , .ass . Default priority: ma > mb > usd > usda > usdc > abc > fbx > obj > ass . The asset name comes from the file name without extension, and source file names are left untouched. Input and output Input: a model folder. Files with the same name in several formats count as one asset, with all formats packaged into the same .zasset . Output: one <asset name>.zasset per asset. When 「输出位置」 (Output location) is empty the current library category directory is preferred, and a directory picker appears if it cannot be resolved. Inside the asset: the model files, meta.json , an optional thumb.sicon , and sub-directories such as textures/ and ass/ ; texture references are written into texture_map . Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → model to zasset . Click 「浏览...」 (Browse...) and choose the 「模型文件夹」 (Model folder) . Set 「目标格式」 (Target formats) as needed (comma separated; empty packages every format found). Adjust the conversion options and click 「扫描模型」 (Scan models) to check asset counts and formats. Set the output location (may be empty) and click 「转换」 (Convert) . Verify the result After scanning, the right side shows 「发现 N 个模型资产」 (found N model assets) with each asset's formats and size. When conversion finishes the status bar shows 「转换完成！成功: x, 失败: y」 (conversion finished! succeeded: x, failed: y) . Inside the .zasset you can see the model files, meta.json and, when a thumbnail exists, thumb.sicon . Options and notes Option Default Notes Include sub-folders On Packages the contents of ass/ , textures/ , sourceimages/ and similar Search sub-folders recursively Off Scans deeper directories for model files Include dependencies (textures, materials and so on) On Parses texture references from .ma and collects same-named .mtl / .mcm / .zmetal Use existing metadata and thumbnails On Reads thumbnail paths and JSON/TXT metadata sources from the configuration Import into the current category after conversion Off Copies the asset into the current library category afterwards Configuration comes from Assets/preset/model_mapping.json , with expression overrides in Assets/preset/model_expression.json ; file routing, metadata sources and thumbnail search paths are editable in the interface. Metadata field mapping follows the configuration: none keeps the value, split_comma splits on commas into an array and first_line takes the first line; a wrong handler means no metadata is read.

items.title: PBR textures to asset
items.summary: Group a set of channel-named PBR textures by material, package each material into a .zasset and detect channel types and resolutions automatically. Purpose Skip
items.text: Group a set of channel-named PBR textures by material, package each material into a .zasset and detect channel types and resolutions automatically. Purpose Skip the manual sorting of BaseColor, Normal, Roughness and other textures, and turn Megascans, Zoo Tools or your own texture folders straight into assets. The menu shows the script name : the quick tools menu scans the scripts in quicktools/ directly, and an entry name is the file name without .py with underscores replaced by spaces, so the menu shows pbr to zasset rather than a Chinese title. The three conversion tools map as follows: hdr to zasset = HDR to asset, model to zasset = model to asset, pbr to zasset = PBR texture to asset. Input and output Input: a folder containing PBR textures; with 「批量模式」 (Batch mode) checked pick a parent folder so each sub-folder becomes a separate asset. Output: one <material name>.zasset per material, written to the input folder by default (or a separate 「输出位置」 (Output location) ). Inside the asset: textures stored by channel under textures/ , and for several resolutions in tiers such as textures/2k/ and textures/4k/ . meta.json records the properties channel mapping plus optional resolutions and default_resolution , and thumb.sicon when a thumbnail exists. Texture naming rules The tool recognizes textures by "underscore + channel alias", case-insensitively: Channel Accepted aliases baseColor basecolor , base_color , albedo , diffuse , col , color , base , diff normal normal , norm , nor , nrm , n , normalmap , nor_dx , nor_gl roughness roughness , rough , rgh , roughnessmap , rough_map metallic metal , mtl , metalness , metal_map , metallic_map ao ao , ambient , occlusion , ambient_occlusion , ao_map , occ emissive emissive , emit , emission , illumination , emissive_map , glow height height , heightmap , height_map , bump , bump_map , disp , displacement , disp_map An alias must be separated from the preceding name by _ , for example wood_albedo.png ; woodcolor.png is not recognized. The packed maps arm / orm are treated as R=AO, G=Roughness, B=Metallic. Resolution markers ( _2K_ , _4K_ , _8K_ and so on) are stripped from the file name, and can also be expressed with sub-directories such as 2k/ or 4k/ . The material name is the text before the channel alias, for example brick_2K_Albedo → brick . Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → pbr to zasset . Click 「浏览」 (Browse) and choose the texture folder, or the parent folder in batch mode. Click 「扫描贴图」 (Scan textures) and check the material count, channels and resolutions on the right. Set the output location and adjust options as needed. Click 「转换」 (Convert) . Verify the result After scanning the status bar shows the number of materials and textures found. Conversion shows a summary and each material's .zasset appears in the output directory. Opening an asset shows the channel paths in meta.json and the contents of textures/ ; the library can display the thumbnail. Options and notes Option Default Notes Export .zasset asset files On When off only scanning / preview happens Batch mode (sub-folders as separate assets) Off Suits a parent directory holding several asset folders Import into the current category after conversion Off Copies the .zasset into the current library category afterwards Package all resolutions On When on each resolution goes into textures/<resolution>/ ; when off only the default resolution is packaged Scan sub-folders recursively Off Turn on when textures live in sub-directories such as tex/ ; choose automatic recursion or specify folder names manually Exclude Empty Folder names skipped during recursion, comma separated, for example Thumbs, previews When no valid textures are found the status bar reports no PBR textures and suggests checking the underscores and aliases in the names. Thumbnail and metadata sources are configured in Assets/preset/pbr_mapping.json , which supports {materialName} / {folderName} placeholders and JSON/TXT metadata sources. Conversion needs a valid

items.title: Image format conversion tool
items.summary: Batch converts HDR, EXR, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, WebP and TGA images with OpenCV, supporting resizing and preserving the directory structure. Purpose Turn high dy
items.text: Batch converts HDR, EXR, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, BMP, WebP and TGA images with OpenCV, supporting resizing and preserving the directory structure. Purpose Turn high dynamic range textures into previews, or unify image formats between projects without opening an image editor for every file. Input and output Input: 「选择文件」 (Choose files) accepts several files; 「选择文件夹」 (Choose folder) scans the images inside recursively. Output: images in the target format keeping the source base name; an empty 「输出位置」 (Output location) means the input file's directory (or the input folder in folder mode). Output structure: 「保持层级结构」 (Keep hierarchy) is on by default and rebuilds the source relative paths under the output directory; when off everything is flattened into the output directory. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 图像格式转换工具 (Image format conversion tool) . Choose the input mode and click 「浏览...」 (Browse...) to pick files or a folder. To limit the input types fill 「输入格式过滤」 (Input format filter) such as exr or png, jpg (empty converts every supported format). Set 「输出位置」 (Output location) and 「输出格式」 (Output format) . Fill the output width / height as needed and adjust aspect ratio and format options. Click 「开始转换」 (Start conversion) . Verify the result The 「转换日志」 (Conversion log) on the left lists each processed path and any renames. The progress bar completes and a summary appears (successes / failures). The output directory contains files in the target format with the source structure preserved (when keeping hierarchy). Options and notes Option Default Notes Target format .exr The dropdown switches to .hdr , .png , .jpg , .tif , .bmp , .webp , .tga and more JPEG quality 95% Range 10%–100% PNG compression 5 Range 0–9 TIFF compression LZW NONE and DEFLATE are also available Output width / height Empty Empty keeps the original size; filling one side computes the other proportionally Keep aspect ratio On When off the image is stretched to the given size Keep hierarchy On When off all files go into one directory Converting HDR/EXR to an 8-bit format applies Reinhard tone mapping and Gamma 2.2 correction, so colors differ from the original float image; it suits previews and thumbnails. File names are cleaned to letters, digits, underscores and dots only, starting with a letter; when a name does not comply the tool renames the source file and logs 源文件已重命名 (source file renamed) . EXR reading prefers OpenCV and falls back to imageio ; missing dependencies produce an install hint. The output directory is created when it does not exist.

items.title: Batch process Maya files
synonyms: run a script on many files
items.summary: Open several .ma / .mb files in turn and run the same MEL or Python script on each, optionally saving afterwards. Purpose Suits repetitive work such as batch re
items.text: Open several .ma / .mb files in turn and run the same MEL or Python script on each, optionally saving afterwards. Purpose Suits repetitive work such as batch renaming, node cleanup or unifying render settings, without opening each scene by hand. Input and output Input: a file list ( .ma / .mb ) plus a MEL or Python script. Output: the modified and saved .ma / .mb files (when 「执行后保存文件」 (Save files after running) is checked); progress is written into the 「执行日志」 (Execution log) at the bottom of the window. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 批量处理maya文件 (Batch process Maya files) . Under 「文件选择」 (File selection) click 「添加文件」 (Add files) to add .ma / .mb files, several at a time; remove unwanted entries with 「移除选中」 (Remove selected) or 「清空列表」 (Clear list) . Under 「脚本输入」 (Script input) choose MEL or Python and paste the script; 「MEL示例」 (MEL sample) and 「Python示例」 (Python sample) are quick starting points. Validate the script with 「测试执行（当前场景）」 (Test run on the current scene) first. Confirm 「执行选项」 (Execution options) and click 「批量执行」 (Run batch) . Read the success / failure summary at the end of the log. Verify the result The log shows 「批量处理完成！」 (batch processing finished!) with the number of succeeded and failed files. With saving checked, the target files' modification times on disk are updated. Afterwards the tool tries to reopen the scene that was saved before running. Options and notes Option Default Notes Save files after running On Each file is saved with force after a successful run Show detailed information On The log lists each file being processed and its save result Advanced options Off Expands backup before running, force save and ignore errors and continue Source check: the current batch logic only reads "save files after running" and "show detailed information"; the three advanced options are not used by the execution logic yet, so checking them changes nothing (whether they are reserved for later is to be confirmed). A failing file is recorded as a failure and processing continues with the next one; the batch is never aborted. Batch runs open files one by one, so an unsaved current scene may be replaced ; save the current scene before running. It is only reopened afterwards when it already had a file path. The log supports 「清空日志」 (Clear log) , 「保存日志」 (Save log) as .txt and 「复制日志」 (Copy log) .

items.title: Batch mirror copy
items.summary: Filter the files in a source folder by extension and mirror them into a target folder with the full directory hierarchy preserved. Purpose Good for archiving as
items.text: Filter the files in a source folder by extension and mirror them into a target folder with the full directory hierarchy preserved. Purpose Good for archiving assets, distributing textures and backing up a directory structure: pick only the formats you need while keeping the original hierarchy. Input and output Input: a source folder, a target folder and the list of extensions to copy. Output: files rebuilt under the target folder with the source relative paths; with 「复制层级结构」 (Copy hierarchy) off they are flattened and name clashes get the parent folder name or a number. Files already present at the target are skipped and never overwritten. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 批量镜像复制 (Batch mirror copy) . Click 「浏览」 (Browse) next to the source folder and choose the source. Click 「浏览」 (Browse) next to the target folder and choose the destination. Fill the extensions under 「文件格式」 (File formats) , comma separated; the default is .exr, .hdr, .png, .jpg , and a leading dot is optional. Optionally check 「仅预览（不实际复制）」 (Preview only, do not copy) and click 「开始复制」 (Start copy) to check the matches. Uncheck preview and click 「开始复制」 (Start copy) again. Verify the result Preview mode: the log ends with 「预览完成，共匹配 N 个文件」 (preview finished, N files matched) and nothing is written to disk. Real copy: the progress bar completes and a summary appears (total / copied / skipped / failed). The target directory shows the same relative paths as the source (when keeping hierarchy). Options and notes Option Default Notes File formats .exr, .hdr, .png, .jpg Comma separated, case-insensitive, leading dots are added automatically Preview only (do not copy) Off Only counts and lists the files that would be copied Copy hierarchy On When off everything is flattened into the target root, with automatic name disambiguation The source and target folders cannot be the same, otherwise the tool refuses to run. Copying uses shutil.copy2 to preserve metadata such as modification times where possible. A single failing file never aborts the whole run; failures with reasons are listed in the summary dialog afterwards. Copying runs on a background thread so the interface stays responsive; with many files the "scanning files…" stage can take a while.

items.title: Material import/export tool
items.summary: Export and import material networks from one window, in either the "full radar" or the "MA+JSON" flavor. Purpose Export the material networks of a scene togethe
items.text: Export and import material networks from one window, in either the "full radar" or the "MA+JSON" flavor. Purpose Export the material networks of a scene together with textures and metadata, then restore them in another scene or on another machine and reassign them to models. The two flavors Tab Export products Best for Full radar .zmetal (material network JSON), optionally .ameta metadata, .mcm object mapping and textures/ Keeping the complete material network parameters, imported straight in this tool MA+JSON .ma (material network) + .mcm (object mapping JSON), optionally .ameta and textures/ When a Maya MA file is wanted, for manual review or further processing Input and output Export input: the selected models or materials in Maya, or 「导出所有」 (Export all) . Export output: the chosen 「工作目录」 (Working directory) ; when unset it prefers the current scene's directory and asks for one when the scene is unsaved. With 「创建文件夹」 (Create folders) checked each material gets its own folder. Import input: for the radar flavor a .zmetal / .json ; for MA+JSON a .mcm (JSON) named like the material, from which the tool finds the matching .ma ; 「从文件夹导入...」 (Import from folder...) collects recursively. Import output: material nodes in the current scene, assigned to the matching models according to the options. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 材质导入导出工具(材质管理) (Material import/export tool) . On the full radar or MA+JSON tab set 「工作目录」 (Working directory) and 「文件名」 (File name) (when empty the selected object name, then the scene name, then MaterialData is used). Under 「导出 - 选项」 (Export options) choose export selected or export all, and check separate material files, export object mapping, export metadata, create folders and package textures as needed. Expand 「导出 - 元数据设置」 (Export metadata settings) to fill in the color space (auto-detected by default, falling back to ACEScg ), category, tags and Chinese name. Click 「执行导出」 (Run export) . To import, pick a file or 「从文件夹导入...」 (Import from folder...) , set the import mode and options and click 「执行导入」 (Run import) . Verify the result The working directory gains .zmetal or .ma / .mcm files, plus .ameta when metadata is checked and textures/ when packaging textures is checked. After importing the materials appear in Maya, and with 「自动指定物体」 (Auto-assign objects) checked the models already carry them. Progress details are printed in the Maya Script Editor (such as 「[材质导出] 成功」 ([material export] succeeded) and 「导入完成」 (import finished) ). Options and notes Import options include 「自动指定物体」 (Auto-assign objects) (on by default), 「模糊匹配」 (Fuzzy matching) and 「拷贝纹理」 (Copy textures) (on by default); the basic settings accept a namespace, material prefix / suffix and model path prefix / suffix replacement. The MA+JSON tab reminds you to make sure the scene already contains the models to assign to; prepare the target models before importing. Save the scene before exporting or importing; export-selected depends on the current selection and does nothing when it is empty. This tool produces material network files rather than .zasset assets; to add them to the library use the asset import flow.

items.title: Material conversion tool
items.summary: Convert materials in Maya in bulk following "source material type → target material type" mappings, with attribute transfer controlled by .mmap mapping files. P
items.text: Convert materials in Maya in bulk following "source material type → target material type" mappings, with attribute transfer controlled by .mmap mapping files. Purpose Replace legacy materials ( lambert , phong , blinn and so on) in bulk with the current renderer's materials ( aiStandardSurface , redshiftStandardMaterial , VRayMtl and so on); useful when taking over an old scene or unifying material standards. Input and output Input: materials in the current scene, the material type mapping table and the .mmap files in the mapping folder. Output: newly created target-type materials in the scene, with the originals deleted or kept and reassigned to objects according to the options. Presets: the material type mapping can be saved as an .mlist in Assets/material_mapper_presets/mapping_type_presets/ . Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 材质转换工具 (Material conversion tool) . In the 「映射文件」 (Mapping files) area at the top click 「浏览...」 (Browse...) and choose the folder containing .mmap files (default Assets/material_mapper_presets ). Fill the source / target material types in the 「材质类型映射配置」 (Material type mapping configuration) table; pick from the dropdowns or type them by hand. When needed use 「加载源」 (Load source) / 「加载目标」 (Load target) to read types from the current Maya selection, or maintain the table with 「添加行」 (Add row) , 「删除选中」 (Remove selected) and 「清空全部」 (Clear all) . Under 「转换选项」 (Conversion options) confirm copying textures, keeping the original material and applying to the selected objects automatically. Click 「转换选择」 (Convert selection) to process only the selected materials, or 「转换全部」 (Convert all) to process every matching material in the scene. Read the success / failure summary afterwards; on failures use 「在Maya中选中失败材质」 (Select failed materials in Maya) to locate them. Verify the result The status bar shows progress and completion information. A dialog afterwards reports the converted material count and attribute copy statistics. With 「自动应用到选择对象」 (Apply to selected objects automatically) checked the objects in the viewport already use the new materials. Failed materials go into 「转换失败材质列表」 (Failed material list) and can be selected in one click to fix one by one. Options and notes Option Default Notes Copy texture connections On Copies the source material's texture connections to the target Keep the original material Off When on the source material is not deleted, which makes rollback easy Apply to selected objects automatically On Assigns the new material to the objects using the original No mapping → default material Off Creates a basic material of the target type when no mapping exists; when off it counts as a failure Without a direct mapping file it tries an openPBR detour (A → openPBR → B), and the intermediate materials are cleaned up automatically. Save the scene before converting; the target renderer plug-in must be loaded and material type names are case-sensitive. Conversion needs a valid convert license. With 「源」 (Source) left empty and only one row, every material is converted to that target type.

items.title: Material node attribute mapping tool
items.summary: Build an attribute-by-attribute mapping between two material node types and save it as an .mmap for the material conversion tool. Purpose It decides "which sour
items.text: Build an attribute-by-attribute mapping between two material node types and save it as an .mmap for the material conversion tool. Purpose It decides "which source material attribute goes to which target attribute" and can add transform functions and default values; it is the key configuration behind material conversion quality. Input and output Input: source / target material nodes (loaded from the current Maya selection), or node types and attributes typed by hand. Output: .mmap presets (JSON) saved in Assets/material_mapper_presets/ by default, named source node type_target node type.mmap . The mapping table has five columns: select, source material attribute, target attribute, transform function, default value. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 材质节点属性映射工具 (Material node attribute mapping tool) . Select the source material node in Maya and click 「加载」 (Load) next to the source node; then select the target material node and click 「加载」 (Load) next to it. Click 「添加行」 (Add row) and pick the source and target attributes from the dropdowns; 「属性浏览器」 (Attribute browser) also lets you pick attributes from the current selection. Fill the transform function and default value as needed; 「载入默认值」 (Load defaults) reads the target node's current values into the whole column. For automatic inference choose the AI service and model and click 「AI 智能映射」 (AI smart mapping) ; right-clicking a single row also infers locally. Click 「保存预设」 (Save preset) to save the .mmap ; reload it later with 「加载预设」 (Load preset) . Verify the result Saving reports 「预设已保存到: <path>」 (preset saved to: <path>) and the .mmap appears in the preset directory. Closing the window saves _last_preset.mmap automatically and restores the previous configuration next time. After loading the same mapping folder in the material conversion tool the table shows the source / target types and attribute counts. Options and notes Transform functions cover RGB channel splitting, transparency to transmission, glossiness to roughness, metalness estimation, emission, color math and more; function arguments are JSON (such as {"scalar": 2.0} ) and switching a function fills in default arguments automatically. AI services include Ollama (local, no API key), DeepSeek and Qwen (API key required); the local default model is qwen3-vl:8b , so when it is missing pick a pulled model in the dropdown or run ollama pull . An empty attribute dropdown usually means no node was loaded; use the attribute browser to add attributes one by one instead. When AI returns nothing useful, first confirm the service is reachable and the model available; with many attributes run it in batches on selected rows. The preset directory opens directly with 「打开文件夹」 (Open folder) ; a duplicate source attribute is cleared automatically.

items.title: Browsing and searching
items.summary: The script browser uses "categories on the left, script list on the right", with a search box at the top that filters live. Purpose It gathers scripts scattered
items.text: The script browser uses "categories on the left, script list on the right", with a search box at the top that filters live. Purpose It gathers scripts scattered across the script asset library, project folders and personal folders in one place, so you can double-click to run them instead of remembering paths or pasting into the Script Editor. Interface Left column: script asset categories plus 「全部」 (All) , 「★ 收藏」 (Favorites) , 「🕘 最近运行」 (Recently run) and 「未登记」 (Unregistered) ; extra script roots are grouped by their first-level sub-directories. Empty categories are shown too. Right column: the script list showing the Chinese name, risk level and whether it has been verified live; hovering shows its purpose and trigger scenario. Top: the search box, 「▶ 运行」 (Run) , 「添加目录」 (Add directory) and 「刷新」 (Refresh) . Bottom: a status bar with success / failure and the elapsed time. Steps Open 快捷工具 (Quick tools) → 脚本浏览器 (Script browser) . Choose a category on the left; on first use click 「添加目录」 (Add directory) or drop a folder into the window to add an extra script root. Type a keyword in the search box and the list filters as you type. Select a script to read its list information; double-click, press Enter or click 「▶ 运行」 (Run) to execute it. Verify the result The number of list entries changes with the category and search terms. After running, the status bar shows 「已运行 <name>（用时 x.xxs）」 (ran <name>, x.xx s) or 「运行失败」 (run failed) . The script's print output and tracebacks appear in the Maya Script Editor history. Notes The scan covers script_assets/ and extra script roots; files starting with . or _ are not listed. F5 refreshes, Ctrl+F focuses the search and Ctrl+C copies the selected script path. The script browser has no separate output panel; all output goes to the Script Editor. The search and filter syntax is described in 9.6.4.

items.title: Categories, favorites and recent runs
items.summary: Categories decide where a script sits in the left column, while favorites and recently run are two cross-category shortcuts. Purpose Once scripts multiply, use
items.text: Categories decide where a script sits in the left column, while favorites and recently run are two cross-category shortcuts. Purpose Once scripts multiply, use categories to organize them, favorites to pin the ones used often and recently run to return to what you just used. The three entries Entry Contents Source Categories The script asset category directories; first-level sub-directories of extra script roots also count as categories The category table in script_assets/scripts.json plus disk directories ★ Favorites Scripts favorited by hand, with the count in parentheses The favorites path list in plug-in settings 🕘 Recently run Scripts run recently, newest first, at most 15 Recorded automatically after each run Unregistered Scripts whose file exists but whose metadata is missing from the registry Scan results Steps Right-click a script in the right column and choose 「★ 收藏」 (Favorite) or 「取消收藏」 (Remove favorite) . Click 「★ 收藏」 (Favorites) or 「🕘 最近运行」 (Recently run) in the left column to see those lists. Right-click a category node on the left for 「新建分类…」 (New category…) , 「新建脚本…」 (New script…) , 「重命名分类…」 (Rename category…) , 「删除分类（含内容）…」 (Delete category with contents…) and 「打开该分类文件夹」 (Open that category folder) . Drag a script from the right column onto a category on the left to move it and update its category. Verify the result The counts in parentheses for favorites and recently run change with your actions. After a move, the paths in favorites and recently run update instead of disappearing. After a drag the script appears in the target category and no longer in the original one. Notes Dropping onto the virtual nodes 「全部」 (All) , 「★ 收藏」 (Favorites) , 「🕘 最近运行」 (Recently run) and 「未登记」 (Unregistered) is refused and the status bar explains why. Dragging across script roots, or onto a category that already has a same-named script, does not move anything. 「删除分类（含内容）…」 (Delete category with contents…) permanently deletes the scripts inside the directory, and the confirmation defaults to 「否」 (No) . Recently run keeps at most 15 entries; older ones drop out.

items.title: Running and importing
synonyms: put a script in the editor
items.summary: Scripts can be run directly, run with parameters, imported as a module, or loaded into the Maya Script Editor. Purpose Use the same script for different purpose
items.text: Scripts can be run directly, run with parameters, imported as a module, or loaded into the Maya Script Editor. Purpose Use the same script for different purposes: run it directly to see the effect, run it with parameters to pass values, or load it into the editor for further editing. Running Select the script and double-click, press Enter or click 「▶ 运行」 (Run) . Scripts registered as high risk ask for confirmation first, with 「否」 (No) as the default; you can suppress the prompt for this session. Python scripts are syntax-compiled first, so syntax errors are never executed; MEL runs through mel.eval . For parameters, right-click and choose 「带参数运行…」 (Run with parameters…) and fill a JSON object that is preset as PARAMS for the script (Python only). A script may put its result into RESULT , whose summary the window prints in the Script Editor. Importing and loading 「导入（加载为模块）」 (Import, load as a module) only supports Python: it adds the script's directory to sys.path , registers the module under the file's base name in sys.modules and lists the available names. MEL is not a module and is refused. 「加载到脚本编辑器」 (Load into the Script Editor) writes into the Python or MEL tab by extension; when the target tab already has content it asks before overwriting. 「生成执行命令（放工具架）…」 (Generate an execution command for the shelf…) generates a Python / MEL shelf button command. Verify the result The status bar shows 「已运行 <name>（用时 x.xxs）」 (ran <name>, x.xx s) ; failures open a copyable error dialog. The script's print output and traceback appear in the Maya Script Editor history. After importing you can use import <module name> in the Script Editor; after loading, the editor tab shows the script source. Notes Running with parameters does not apply to MEL; MEL has no PARAMS / RESULT convention, so print the important results. The standalone edition dispatches the script to an online Maya; when Maya is offline it reports 「投送 Maya 失败」 (dispatch to Maya failed) . Suppressing the prompt for high-risk scripts only lasts for the current session.

items.title: Filter syntax
items.summary: The script browser's search box splits on spaces and requires every term to match (AND), and supports four prefix filters: tag: , risk: , cat: and unverified .
items.text: The script browser's search box splits on spaces and requires every term to match (AND), and supports four prefix filters: tag: , risk: , cat: and unverified . Purpose Narrow down quickly when there are many scripts, for example to see one category, one tag or only unverified scripts. Syntax Form Meaning keyword Case-insensitive substring match across the name, file base name, purpose, category, script root name, path, tags and trigger scenario tag:texture The tag must equal that value (case-insensitive) risk:high The risk level must be exactly high cat:qa The category or script root name contains that value unverified Shows only scripts without a live-verification record Examples tag:texture risk:high : scripts tagged texture with risk high. cat:qa unverified : unverified scripts in the qa category. brick : scripts whose name, purpose, tags or path contain brick . Steps Open the script browser. Type one or more terms in the search box, separated by spaces. Keep appending prefix conditions to narrow the results; clearing the box restores every script in the current category. Verify the result The list shrinks or grows live as you type. The status bar reports no error; mutually exclusive conditions simply yield an empty list.
