Notes Multiple terms are ANDed; OR and negation are not supported. risk: is an exact match, while cat: and tag: match different scopes, since cat: also looks at the script root name. Chinese keywords work directly without quotes. Search only filters the current scan result and never triggers a rescan; press F5 to refresh after files change.

items.title: Directory and naming conventions
items.summary: A custom quick tool is simply a .py file placed in quicktools/ , and the menu lists it automatically by file name. Directory conventions Location What goes ther
items.text: A custom quick tool is simply a .py file placed in quicktools/ , and the menu lists it automatically by file name. Directory conventions Location What goes there <plug-in root>/quicktools/ Quick tool scripts; the menu scans only .py files at this level and never recurses into sub-directories <plug-in root>/Assets/help/<tool name>/help.html The tool's own help page; for an English page also place a same-named _en.html next to help.html <plug-in root>/Assets/preset/ Tool configuration such as model_mapping.json , pbr_mapping.json , *_expression.json <plug-in root>/Assets/material_mapper_presets/ Material mapping .mmap and .mlist presets Naming conventions The file must end in .py and its name must be unique in that directory. The menu entry name is the file name without .py with underscores replaced by spaces; a Chinese file name is shown as is. The menu sorts by file name and applies no hidden filter, so do not keep temporary or backup scripts in quicktools/ or they appear in the menu too. Tools called from the script browser or the command channel should keep a stable file name, since frequent renames break favorites and mappings. Code conventions Use main() or run() as the entry, or keep an if __name__ == "__main__": block for a plain script (see 9.7.2). Match the rest of the plug-in: prefer package-absolute imports and fall back to top-level ui.* / utils.* , so the script runs both inside the plug-in and in the Script Editor. Do not put a tool's own configuration and presets in the root of quicktools/ ; place them in the matching directory under Assets/ so they are not scanned as scripts. Verify the result The 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) menu shows the new file name (with underscores displayed as spaces). Clicking it starts the window or script normally and the Script Editor shows no ImportError . The help button opens Assets/help/<tool name>/help.html . Notes New files need no menu code or registry change; the menu rescans the directory every time it opens. The standalone edition dispatches quick tools to Maya by default; whether a pure file tool runs locally depends on the host allowlist (see 9.7.3).

items.title: Parameters and return values
items.summary: The menu only calls main() / run() without arguments; when parameters or structured results are needed, use the PARAMS / RESULT convention of the command channe
items.text: The menu only calls main() / run() without arguments; when parameters or structured results are needed, use the PARAMS / RESULT convention of the command channel or the script browser. Entries and parameters The menu and the command channel resolve entries the same way: main() → run() → run once as __main__ when the source contains if __name__ == "__main__" . The menu calls main() / run() without arguments. The quicktool_run command tries fn(params) when params is given; when the entry does not accept arguments (raising TypeError ) it falls back to fn() . When only main / run exists the module body is not executed again, so top-level side effects never run twice. The PARAMS / RESULT convention A script-style entry can read and write two conventional variables: PARAMS = globals().get("PARAMS") or {} DRY_RUN = bool(PARAMS.get("dry_run", False)) def main(): # do the work here; for writes prefer dry_run first and return before / after values return {"status": "ok", "updated": 0} RESULT = main() if not globals().get("SKIP_RUN") else None PARAMS : the JSON object passed by the script browser's "run with parameters…" or by the command channel. RESULT : the script result; the script browser prints a summary and the command channel puts it into its return value. MEL has no PARAMS / RESULT convention, so print the important results. Return value shape The command channel can safely return None , booleans, numbers, strings, lists and dictionaries. Nested dictionaries / lists keep only the first 30 items; other objects are turned into repr and truncated to 300 characters, so never return unserializable objects such as Qt widgets. GUI tools normally have no meaningful return value; the command channel only reports opened: true , meaning the window opened and the work is not finished. Verify the result Call quicktool_run with dry_run=true first to confirm the entry is resolved correctly. After a real run check status , entry and result in the return value. Run the same script in the script browser; the status bar should show the elapsed time and the Script Editor should show the RESULT summary. Notes The menu path never injects PARAMS , so logic that depends on parameters must also run safely with defaults. For long-running or cancellable work, provide your own progress and cancel mechanism inside the script.

items.title: Quick registration
synonyms: the new script does not appear
items.summary: Quick tools have no registry: dropping a .py into quicktools/ completes the UI registration; only the command channel or a special run location needs an extra e
items.text: Quick tools have no registry: dropping a .py into quicktools/ completes the UI registration; only the command channel or a special run location needs an extra edit. The fastest path Create a .py file in <plug-in root>/quicktools/ . Provide a main() , run() or if __name__ == "__main__": entry. Open the 「快捷工具」 (Quick tools) menu, confirm the file name appears and click to run it. The menu rescans the directory every time it opens, so no Maya restart is needed . Calling quicktool_run without name also lists the new file and its entry . When extra registration is needed Need What to change Have the command channel suggest "prefer this first-class command" The _QUICKTOOL_COVERAGE map in squirrel_asset_manager/ai/runtime_commands.py Have a dedicated command (parameter schema, dry_run, structured result) squirrel_asset_manager/ai/quicktools_commands.py , registering a CommandDescriptor like the existing three commands A pure file tool that should run locally in the standalone edition instead of being dispatched to Maya The local_only set in _run_quick_tool in squirrel_asset_manager/ui/main_window.py A dedicated help page inside the tool Place help.html in Assets/help/<tool name>/ After registering a command, call refresh_commands if the plug-in is running to rebuild the executor and reconnect; commands in flight at that moment fail, so never call it during a long job. Verify the result The menu shows the new entry instead of 「暂无快捷工具」 (no quick tools yet) . Clicking it opens the window or runs the script without ImportError / SyntaxError in the Script Editor. Calling the command channel without name lists the file and its entry ; passing name returns status: ok . For a pure file tool that should run locally, confirm in the standalone edition that it is not dispatched to Maya. Notes If it does not appear, first confirm the file is in the root of quicktools/ , ends in .py and is not in a sub-directory. Clicking with no effect usually means no recognizable entry; the menu prints 「没有可执行的入口」 (no executable entry) . After adding a command or changing a parameter schema, refresh the command list so external AI tools do not keep seeing the old schema. Registration changes are plug-in source changes; verify them in a test environment before distributing.

items.title: Connection method and ports
items.summary: The plug-in drives a running Maya through Maya's native commandPort , and the connection only uses the loopback address 127.0.0.1 , so Maya is never exposed to
items.text: The plug-in drives a running Maya through Maya's native commandPort , and the connection only uses the loopback address 127.0.0.1 , so Maya is never exposed to the LAN. Prerequisites Maya is running and its version is supported by the plug-in. 「允许外部工具连接 Maya（独立版 / 命令行）」 (allow external tools to connect to Maya, standalone / command line) is checked in settings. The matching option is bridge_auto_port , on by default, written into each version's userSetup.py startup block at install time. Port rules Default ports count down by year: port = 7001 + (2026 - version year) . Maya 2026 2025 2024 2023 2022 Port 7001 7002 7003 7004 7005 When a second instance of the same version starts, the default port is taken by the first one, so the later instance uses the backup range 7110~7129 ; see "Backup ports and auto-discovery". Steps Start the target Maya and confirm the option above is enabled in settings. In the project root run python maya_bridge.py --ping and confirm a reply arrives. To see which versions are online run python maya_bridge.py --scan . To open the port manually, run this in Maya's Script Editor (Python tab): import maya.cmds as cmds cmds.commandPort(name="127.0.0.1:7001", sourceType="python") Verify the result --ping returns a string like 2026 | <untitled> , the first part being the Maya version and the second the current scene; --scan lists the online state of every port. Tips and warnings The channel is eval mode : it evaluates a single-line expression and returns its value; print output only goes to the Maya Script Editor and never back to the caller. Never call the bridge client from inside the Maya process: it would connect to itself and block the main thread, and the code has an explicit deadlock guard for that. To pin a target, set the SQUIRREL_MAYA_PORT environment variable, or use --maya 2025 / --port 7002 .

items.title: Choosing among several Maya sessions
items.summary: In the standalone edition the Maya target button in the toolbar specifies which Maya to drive when several are open, preventing automatic selection from importi
items.text: In the standalone edition the Maya target button in the toolbar specifies which Maya to drive when several are open, preventing automatic selection from importing assets into the wrong scene. In the current implementation the button is created only in the standalone edition while it is not attached by Maya : Form Has the Maya target button Why Standalone edition / EXE (started on its own, not attached) Yes You need to choose which online Maya to drive In-Maya version (the plug-in runs inside Maya) No It is already inside Maya, so the target is itself Standalone attached by Maya (opened embedded from a Maya menu) No The target is locked to the host; offering a switch would mislead and could import into another scene Prerequisites You are using the standalone edition (not inside Maya) and it is not attached by Maya ; the in-Maya and attached forms do not have this button. The target Maya is running; if its bridge port is closed it is still listed but cannot be connected directly. Steps Click the Maya target button in the standalone top toolbar; the tooltip reads "choose the Maya to drive (for several sessions; each has a window thumbnail in the menu)". (The in-Maya version has no such button.) The first menu item is 「自动选择（优先最新版本）」 (Automatic, preferring the newest version) , which returns to picking a Maya by port. Every other row is one Maya: the title shows the version, the subtitle the scene name, PID and port, and a window thumbnail sits on the left. Clicking a row applies immediately, restores that Maya and brings it to the front; the choice is also written into settings ( maya_target ) and restored the next time the standalone edition starts. When a row reads 「Maya（未开桥接端口）」 (Maya, bridge port closed) , clicking it copies the repair command to the clipboard and brings that Maya forward; paste it into its Script Editor and press Enter to open the port. Verify the result The currently selected instance row carries a check mark, the button tooltip appends the chosen target's version, scene, PID and port, and a read-only operation (such as the scene overview) returns the expected scene. Tips and warnings Automatic selection picks in port order, and with several sessions of the same version the first one holds the default port, so specify manually when working with several. If the button is missing from the toolbar, first check which form you are in: the in-Maya version and the attached standalone edition never show it (see the table above); this is not a missing feature. A minimized Maya yields no window thumbnail and the menu says why; Windows does not render minimized windows. Restoring the last choice at startup does not bring Maya to the front; when that instance is offline it falls back to automatic selection and logs an explanation.

items.title: Backup ports and auto-discovery
items.summary: When several sessions of the same version run, or Maya restarts quickly after a crash, Maya falls back from the default port to the backup range 7110~7129 , and
items.text: When several sessions of the same version run, or Maya restarts quickly after a crash, Maya falls back from the default port to the backup range 7110~7129 , and clients probe that range as well. Why the port changes The startup block tries this version's default port first. When that port is already taken by another instance of the same version (Maya reports 10048), it tries 7110~7129 in turn and writes the result into ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/bridge_port.log . The client's candidate order is: the preferred year (2026) → older years → newer years → the backup range. So instances on the backup range are discovered automatically too. Steps Run python maya_bridge.py --scan to see which candidate ports are online. To connect by version use python maya_bridge.py --maya 2025 , which probes the default port and the backup range one by one and confirms identity from the year in the ping reply. When the exact port is known use python maya_bridge.py --port 7110 --ping . To pin the client to one port set SQUIRREL_MAYA_PORT=7110 . To investigate past port changes read ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/bridge_port.log . Verify the result --ping returns version | scene ; --doctor lists listening, answering, PID and verdict per port. Tips and warnings A netstat LISTENING state does not prove Maya is alive: a hung instance or a crash reporter process can hold the port. The verdict must come from actually sending a command and seeing whether it answers. The probe must be a normal expression (such as ping ), never print ; commandPort returns the value of the expression, so print gives the caller None and misjudges a healthy instance as hung.

items.title: Disconnect and reconnect
items.summary: A disconnect usually is not a broken plug-in: Maya has exited, the bridge port is closed, the port moved to the backup range, or the main thread is held by a mo
items.text: A disconnect usually is not a broken plug-in: Maya has exited, the bridge port is closed, the port moved to the backup range, or the main thread is held by a modal dialog or a long command. Symptoms The standalone edition reports no online Maya, or a call returns maya_offline / port_closed . --ping cannot connect, or connects but never gets a reply. An asset cannot be imported although Maya is online, or it lands in another Maya. Causes and fixes Look at the Maya window first : with a crash-recovery, unsaved-changes or error dialog present, dismiss it and retry the read-only query. A modal dialog holds the main thread and looks exactly like a hang. Run python maya_bridge.py --doctor to see who is online, who listens without answering and whether render leftovers exist. If only the port changed, use --scan to find the actual port and then connect with --maya version or --port port ; setting SQUIRREL_MAYA_PORT also works. If the port is closed, check 「允许外部工具连接 Maya（独立版 / 命令行）」 (allow external tools to connect to Maya) in settings, or run cmds.commandPort(...) inside Maya. Once it is confirmed to be a hang (not a dialog), use python maya_bridge.py --doctor --kill-hung to clear only instances that listen but do not answer. With no usable instance use python maya_bridge.py --doctor --launch , which starts Maya and waits until it really answers. Idempotent tasks can add --retry-if-crashed to clean up, launch and resubmit once; a task file containing SQ_DESTRUCTIVE = True is refused. Verify the result --ping returns version | scene again, --doctor marks the target port healthy, and the standalone toolbar's target tooltip shows the expected scene. Tips and warnings Self-healing only suits idempotent or read-only tasks. A crash loses the unsaved scene, and a resubmit only reruns the task itself, never restoring the original session state. There is no resident supervisor process, so Maya is not started automatically when nobody is running a task. Every self-healing attempt appends a record to ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/bridge_recover.log .

items.title: Apply materials
path: Materials and lights into the scene
synonyms: assign a material to the selection
items.summary: There are two commands for applying materials: apply_material only creates the material network, while apply_material_to_selection builds it and assigns it stra
items.text: There are two commands for applying materials: apply_material only creates the material network, while apply_material_to_selection builds it and assigns it straight to the current selection. Prerequisites Maya is online and the target objects exist in the scene. The asset is a material asset; a texture asset without .zmetal falls back to "create a new material from the textures". Steps Select one or more objects in Maya. Right-click the material asset in the library and choose 「为当前选择指定材质」 (Assign material to the current selection) . The standalone edition dispatches this step to Maya through the command channel. The AI assistant can also call apply_material_to_selection with the asset's zasset_path . To only create the material without assigning it, call apply_material and take the material name from the returned nodes . Verify the result It returns status=ok with material and objects counts; the new material appears in the Maya Hypershade and the selected objects' shading network points at it. Tips and warnings Using apply_material alone looks like "nothing happened" because it only creates and never assigns; use the composite command to put a material on the selection. With nothing selected the command reports an error instead of guessing a target. Cross-renderer materials are converted for the current renderer; check the conversion result and attribute mapping in the returned nodes . To only overwrite an existing material's parameters with the asset's values without rebuilding the network, use apply_material_params .

items.title: Assign textures
path: Materials and lights into the scene
synonyms: connect a texture to a material
connect an HDR to a light
items.summary: Assigning textures connects a texture or HDR asset to an existing node: a texture to a material, or an HDR to the selected dome light. Prerequisites The target
items.text: Assigning textures connects a texture or HDR asset to an existing node: a texture to a material, or an HDR to the selected dome light. Prerequisites The target material node or dome light exists in the scene and is selected in Maya. The asset type matches the action: a texture asset uses 「指定贴图到材质」 (Assign texture to material) , an HDR asset uses 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . Steps Select the target material or light node. Right-click the texture asset in the library and choose 「指定贴图到材质」 (Assign texture to material) ; for an HDR asset choose 「指定贴图」 (Assign texture) . You can also call assign_texture : kind=auto decides from the asset's meta.asset_type , texture forces a material connection and hdr forces a dome-light connection. To import the asset's textures into the scene first, call import_texture ; without a texture name it imports every image texture and shares one place2dTexture . Verify the result It returns status=ok with an assigned list; a texture asset reports kind as texture and an HDR asset as hdr . For textures a newly connected file node appears in the Hypershade, while the HDR branch updates the dome light's texture path. Tips and warnings The HDR branch needs an existing selected dome light; without a target it returns an error instead of creating one. Use "create a dome light" for that. auto relies on asset metadata, so pass kind explicitly when type detection is unreliable. A failed assignment returns reason ; confirm the target node type matches the current renderer and retry.

items.title: Apply lights
path: Materials and lights into the scene
items.summary: Applying a light writes the parameters of a light asset onto an existing light shape in the scene, mapping them for the current renderer. Prerequisites A light
items.text: Applying a light writes the parameters of a light asset onto an existing light shape in the scene, mapping them for the current renderer. Prerequisites A light exists in the scene and its shape is usable. The current renderer is decided; cross-renderer application converts parameters through the mapping. Steps Select the light to modify in Maya (either the transform or the shape). Right-click the light asset in the library and choose 「应用灯光参数到选中灯光」 (Apply light parameters to the selected light) . You can also call apply_light with explicit targets ; without them it uses the current selection. To preview first, pass dry_run=true , which lists the target and source renderers in the return value. Verify the result It returns status=ok with the number of applied entries, the source renderer and a shapes list; compare intensity, color, decay and similar parameters in the Attribute Editor. Tips and warnings Light attributes live on the shape , not the transform; expand the shape when checking by hand. With no light selected the command returns the error 「未选中任何灯光节点」 (no light node selected) instead of guessing a target. When the source asset differs from the current renderer it converts; some parameters may not map one to one, so trust the returned shapes and the interface. With .zlight present it builds a temporary light from that data and converts; without it, it falls back to the asset's .ma / .mb light network as the parameter source.

items.title: Create a dome light
path: Materials and lights into the scene
items.summary: Creating a dome light builds the matching dome light node for the current renderer and connects the HDR texture to it as environment lighting. Prerequisites May
items.text: Creating a dome light builds the matching dome light node for the current renderer and connects the HDR texture to it as environment lighting. Prerequisites Maya is online and the current renderer is decided. When using presets, the matching .ma preset exists under the plug-in's Assets/HDR_ligt . Steps Right-click the HDR asset in the library and expand the 「创建环境光」 (Create environment light) submenu. The submenu lists the presets under Assets/HDR_ligt ; running inside Maya imports that preset and replaces the HDR path, while the standalone edition builds the light from a built-in template through the command channel and connects the chosen HDR. You can also call create_dome_light ; pass hdr_path for the texture, or leave it empty for the built-in default IBL. After the light exists, to swap the HDR or connect another HDR to an existing dome light use the HDR branch of "assign texture". Verify the result It returns status=ok with node ; the Outliner shows the renderer's dome light node (Arnold aiSkyDomeLight , Redshift RedshiftDomeLight , V-Ray VRayLightDomeShape ) and the light's texture path points at the chosen HDR. Tips and warnings The dome light node type varies by renderer, so after switching renderers re-check the light's attributes and texture wiring. When the current renderer has no usable template the command returns 「创建失败（渲染器不支持或 Maya 未就绪）」 (creation failed; renderer unsupported or Maya not ready) . Light attributes normally live on the shape; expand it in the Attribute Editor when checking. Without hdr_path the built-in default IBL is used; to change the texture afterwards use the HDR branch of "assign texture".

items.title: Viewport screenshot
items.summary: A viewport screenshot grabs one PNG frame of the current viewport with Maya's playblast and returns the file path within seconds; it is good for checking shape,
items.text: A viewport screenshot grabs one PNG frame of the current viewport with Maya's playblast and returns the file path within seconds; it is good for checking shape, proportions and seams. Prerequisites Maya is in a GUI session; mayapy or -batch has no viewport and cannot capture. The target panel is open and the viewport has refreshed. Steps Call capture_viewport ; without image_path the output goes to the system temp directory. Set the size with width / height , 1280×720 by default. Choose the viewpoint by passing a camera name to camera or a modelPanel name to panel ; otherwise the current camera and first panel are used. Choose the display mode: mode is shaded (default), textured or wireframe ; add wireframe=true to overlay wireframe on shaded. Choose the frame: frame defaults to the current frame. Verify the result The return value contains image_path ; open the PNG and confirm the image is neither a flat color nor empty. When the image is suspiciously small or looks flat, the reply carries a warning. Tips and warnings Before capturing it runs dgdirty and forces a refresh; otherwise a newly created or rebuilt scene easily captures an empty image. Camera, display mode, wireframe and current frame are all restored afterwards, so your viewport is never left in a temporary state. A playblast is a single blocking call: you can cancel before it starts, but not once it runs; a large scene can take from a dozen seconds to several minutes, so prefer an async job. panel and camera must refer to the same viewport; playblast captures the active panel by default, so a mismatched camera captures something else.

items.title: Thumbnail framing
items.summary: Thumbnail framing takes a clean square PNG of the given objects: it frames automatically, turns off camera gates and mask decorations, and restores the whole sc
items.text: Thumbnail framing takes a clean square PNG of the given objects: it frames automatically, turns off camera gates and mask decorations, and restores the whole scene state afterwards. Prerequisites There is an explicit subject; the command never guesses "the only thing in the scene". To write into an asset, have the asset's material_id ready. Steps Select the objects in Maya, or pass objects when calling thumbnail_shot . Set the edge length: size is the square pixel size, defaulting to the configured thumbnail size (512 by default). Tune the composition: fill controls how much of the frame the object occupies (0.85 by default) and fit_factor controls how tight viewFit is (1.0 by default). For wireframe pass wire=true ; to pin a camera or panel pass camera / panel . To write this image straight into an asset pass material_id , which is equivalent to running "update thumbnail" at the same time. Verify the result It returns ok with path plus self-check details such as format , stats and warnings ; open the PNG and confirm the subject is centered and the image is not flat. When the format is not PNG or the image is flat, status drops to partial ; when the target covers not a single pixel it errors and the image cannot be used. Tips and warnings With no subject it errors immediately; select objects first or pass objects explicitly. The focal length is only replaced with 70mm when the camera still has Maya's default 35mm; focal_length=0 means no intervention. The capture temporarily isolates the target and hides camera gate decorations; afterwards the camera, panel, selection, current frame and isolation state are all restored, so the scene is unchanged.

items.title: Frame sequences
items.summary: A frame sequence captures a set of viewport images frame by frame (playblast per frame) for watching motion and change; use "viewport screenshot" for a single d
items.text: A frame sequence captures a set of viewport images frame by frame (playblast per frame) for watching motion and change; use "viewport screenshot" for a single detailed frame. Prerequisites Maya is in a GUI session with a usable modelPanel . The frame range and output location are decided. Steps Call capture_sequence ; frames accepts "1-10" , "1,3,5" , "1-10:2" or a plain array. Set the output: image_path may be a placeholder template (such as .../shot_{frame:04d}.png ), a prefix or a directory; without it the system temp directory is used. Set size, camera and display mode: width / height , camera , mode , wireframe , panel . Set the frame-number padding (4 by default) and the per-call max_frames limit (200 by default). To also encode a video, pass video and fps and encoding follows immediately. Verify the result It returns the list of produced frames and their file paths; the count should match the requested range, and a few frames should look right. Every frame gets a blank check and anomalies are listed in blank_frames . Tips and warnings At most 200 frames per call, a hard gate that keeps the Maya main thread from being monopolized. There is a cancel checkpoint per frame; cancelling stops immediately and keeps captured frames with status=cancelled and stopped_early=true . Capturing temporarily changes the current frame and restores it afterwards; a large sequence can leave the scene marked as modified, so use cmds.file(modified=False) when that matters. A placeholder such as {frame:04d} is expanded from the format string; a prefix or directory uses padding for zero filling, ready for the encoding command.

items.title: Encoding GIF and MP4
items.summary: The encoding command compiles a set of frame images into a GIF or a video, with the output format decided by the file extension. Prerequisites The frame files e
items.text: The encoding command compiles a set of frame images into a GIF or a video, with the output format decided by the file extension. Prerequisites The frame files exist and are named consecutively by frame number (such as frame_0001.png ). An .mp4 output needs ffmpeg; the plug-in ships bin/ffmpeg.exe . A .gif output falls back to Pillow when ffmpeg is missing. Steps Call encode_sequence with image_dir for the frame directory, or pass an explicit files list. Set the output file output : .mp4 ( .mov / .mkv / .webm also work) or .gif . Set fps (24 by default); to shrink a GIF use max_width to scale the frames. When frame names vary, set the scan pattern with pattern , frame_*.png by default. Verify the result The command succeeds and the output file exists; open it in a player and confirm the frame order and duration. On cancel the partial file is deleted, and errors state whether it was NO_ENCODER or FRAMES_NOT_SEQUENTIAL . Tips and warnings Frame names must be consistent and consecutive; with gaps ffmpeg would produce a wrong order, so the command reports FRAMES_NOT_SEQUENTIAL instead of forcing an encode. When neither ffmpeg nor Pillow is available it reports NO_ENCODER honestly and gives the frame directory, never pretending to succeed. Encoding is pure file and subprocess work that never touches Maya, so it can run on a worker thread and still supports progress and cancel. Frame rate and total frame count decide the duration; pair GIF output with max_width to keep the file size reasonable.

items.title: Rendering frames
items.summary: Rendering frames uses the current renderer for a final per-frame render; it is much slower than a viewport screenshot and suits finished images once framing and
items.text: Rendering frames uses the current renderer for a final per-frame render; it is much slower than a viewport screenshot and suits finished images once framing and materials are confirmed. Prerequisites The scene's render settings are configured and the current renderer is available. The frame range, output directory and resolution are decided; rendering cannot be undone. Steps Call render_frames ; frames accepts "1-3" , "1,5,9" , "1-10:5" or a plain array. Set the output directory image_dir ; without it the scene's own output prefix is used. To override resolution pass width / height (0 means use the scene settings). Choose the camera and the file name prefix ; in an Arnold scene samples temporarily changes AASamples. Limit this call with max_frames , 100 by default. Verify the result It returns each frame's output path and progress; open the images and confirm resolution, frame numbers and content. Images already rendered are kept after cancelling. Tips and warnings Each frame takes tens of seconds to minutes, so this is a long job: run it as an async job and watch the progress. The command temporarily bakes the frame number into the output prefix and turns animation off, restoring both afterwards; otherwise one call would render the whole range or overwrite every frame with the same file. Rendering cannot be undone; samples only applies when the scene already has a defaultArnoldRenderOptions node. Repeated in-process Redshift renders in the same Maya session risk a crash; see "Renderer crashes".

items.title: Headless mayapy
items.summary: mayapy.exe is Maya's Python interpreter; it starts the complete Maya core without an interface, and the plug-in uses it for thumbnails and format conversion, wi
items.text: mayapy.exe is Maya's Python interpreter; it starts the complete Maya core without an interface, and the plug-in uses it for thumbnails and format conversion, without touching your open Maya or scene . How it runs The parent process first looks for a mayapy.exe of the same version as the current Maya. When it cannot find one, set SQUIRREL_MAYAPY to <Maya install directory>\bin\mayapy.exe . Every job creates a working directory in the system temp folder, writes job.json and has mayapy run tools/asset_headless_worker.py . The worker never imports the plug-in package, so it can be reproduced with mayapy alone. Jobs produce output outside the library and only write into the asset package after verification. Steps Right-click an asset in the library and choose 「更新缩略图」 (Update thumbnail) → 「后台渲染」 (Background render) , or choose 「格式转换」 (Format conversion) . 「后台渲染」 (Background render) first shows its options dialog; confirm renderer, model, environment light, size and quality and click 「开始生成」 (Start) . Wait for the progress window to finish; the interface stays usable meanwhile. Note: the headless render menu item is now called 「后台渲染」 (Background render) (the old "generate thumbnail" wording is gone). It appears only in the context menu of the materials / models / lights / textures / scenes / dynamics / node trees sub-libraries; HDR, images, audio and animation data do not have it. Verify the result The job returns ok / failed with per-item results; once thumbnails are written back the card images refresh. Failures carry a reason, such as no geometry, no mayapy or missing render tools. Tips and warnings mayapy opens a separate empty scene ; it cannot read the scene you have open and has no viewport. To read the current scene or grab a viewport, use the interface version or the bridge channel, never mayapy. The working directory is cleaned up only after results are written back; a mid-way failure leaves unadopted temporary output behind, which does not affect the library.

items.title: Batch thumbnail rendering
items.summary: Batch thumbnail rendering generates thumbnails for assets inside mayapy: the interface shows options first, then a separate process renders without occupying th
items.text: Batch thumbnail rendering generates thumbnails for assets inside mayapy: the interface shows options first, then a separate process renders without occupying the current viewport. Options Renderer : Arnold, Maya Software, Maya Hardware 2.0, V-Ray, Redshift. Unavailable renderers are greyed out with a reason. Preset model : material, texture and light assets have no geometry of their own, so pick a preset model from Assets/Meshes to carry them. Environment light (HDRI) : check 「使用 HDRI 环境光」 (Use HDRI environment light) and pick a preset; light assets do not show this block because a light is its own source. Size : 256, 384, 512, 768 or 1024, defaulting to the configured thumbnail size. Quality : Fast / Standard / High, mapped to the current renderer's own sampling settings. Tool requirements Arnold needs kick and oiiotool , which ship with Arnold. Maya Hardware 2.0, V-Ray and Redshift need Maya's Render.exe in a batch session. V-Ray and Redshift also need their plug-ins installed locally; Redshift additionally needs a usable GPU. Steps Select one or more assets, right-click → 「更新缩略图」 (Update thumbnail) → 「后台渲染」 (Background render) . In the dialog (also titled "background render") choose the renderer, model (when needed), environment light, size and quality. Click 「开始生成」 (Start) and wait for the progress window to finish. Verify the result Successful thumbnails are written back to the assets and refresh on the cards; failures and skipped items report reasons one by one (missing geometry, missing preset model, missing render tools and so on). Images are validated before writing, so flat or empty images never overwrite existing thumbnails. Tips and warnings An unavailable renderer is an environment problem; switch to an available one to get images first. Higher quality is slower; Arnold uses the standard level by default. The environment light only provides lighting and never enters the background, so thumbnails have a transparent background.

items.title: Batch format conversion
items.summary: Batch format conversion turns an asset's own geometry into other formats inside mayapy and appends the results to the asset package, keeping the original format
items.text: Batch format conversion turns an asset's own geometry into other formats inside mayapy and appends the results to the asset package, keeping the original formats. Supported formats Extension Name ma Maya ASCII mb Maya Binary fbx FBX obj Wavefront OBJ usd USD abc Alembic Prerequisites The asset has geometry of its own ; assets without geometry, such as materials, textures and lights, are skipped with an explanation. A mayapy of the same version as the current Maya exists locally. Steps Select one or more assets and choose 「格式转换」 (Format conversion) from the context menu. In the dialog check the target formats to write into the package; an existing format is marked 「已存在」 (already present) , and checking it replaces that format with this result. Click 「开始转换」 (Start conversion) and wait for the progress window to finish. Verify the result It returns per-item results plus success / failure / skipped counts; the asset directory gains the new format files and the original formats are not deleted. Everything converts in a temporary directory outside the library and is written back only after verification. Tips and warnings Assets without geometry cannot be converted; that is a design limit, not a failure. Same-named assets can exist in different categories, and the job uses numbering internally so outputs never overwrite each other. Cancelling or failing leaves the library unchanged, at most leaving one unadopted temporary output behind.

items.title: Division of work with the interface version
path: Division of work with the interface version
items.summary: The plug-in has three ways to drive Maya, differing only in whose scene is touched and how to iterate : headless mayapy, the bridge command channel and the in-M
items.text: The plug-in has three ways to drive Maya, differing only in whose scene is touched and how to iterate : headless mayapy, the bridge command channel and the in-Maya Script Editor. The three paths Path Form Affects the current scene Best for mayapy standalone Separate process, full Maya core, no interface Not at all Recomputing from scratch, batch thumbnails, batch conversion Bridge command channel Drives a running Maya through commandPort Yes Reading and writing the scene the user has open Maya Script Editor The user runs it manually Yes One-off scripts, handing a script to the user How to choose Recompute from scratch → mayapy. It works in its own empty scene and cannot see the user's window or viewport. Modify the user's copy → the bridge command channel. Reading the current selection, current frame or current viewport requires this route. Long jobs (rendering, exporting, large imports) → run them as async commands and watch progress instead of blocking the main thread. Boundaries and cautions The standalone edition needs an online Maya for scene operations; browsing assets, searching and file-level work can happen offline. Many functions in core/ and integration/ self-degrade through a module-level _IN_MAYA , so calling them directly in a separate process does nothing and reports no error . Any call that would hit such an early return must go through a remote channel. The two channels are separate processes that cannot see each other; seeing no interface activity while using mayapy is normal.

items.title: Job progress and cancellation
items.summary: Headless jobs report state through a progress file in the working directory; cancelling also ends the child process tree so no render leftovers survive. Progres
items.text: Headless jobs report state through a progress file in the working directory; cancelling also ends the child process tree so no render leftovers survive. Progress of a headless job The parent process polls progress.json , whose fields include: running , index / total , label : whether it runs, which item is current and the current asset name. phase : the current stage, showing "cancelling" while cancelling. ok / failed / error : finished and failed counts plus the error. seconds : elapsed time. Polling is non-blocking and the interface refreshes on a timer, so the window never freezes. Cancelling Click cancel in the progress window. The parent process sets _cancelled and runs taskkill /F /T on the child, ending the whole process tree. When results are collected, cancelled=true and the log states the reason. Verify the result The job process should exit after cancelling; use python maya_bridge.py --doctor to check for leftover mayabatch / Render / kick / oiiotool processes. Tips and warnings Arnold's kick does not exit by itself after rendering, so cancelling must kill the whole tree; killing only the parent leaves hundreds of MB of zombie processes. Long loops run through maya_run_python must call progress(...) themselves and check if cancelled(): break ; code without checkpoints cannot be stopped. On a job timeout or disconnect check late results first, and never rerun a destructive task just because of one timeout. If the worker exits abnormally without a result.json , the result says "the worker produced no result file"; read the end of the log to locate the cause.

items.title: Main thread hangs
items.summary: When the Maya main thread is held by a command that never returns, the interface shows "not responding" and the bridge waits forever for a result; this is usual
items.text: When the Maya main thread is held by a command that never returns, the interface shows "not responding" and the bridge waits forever for a result; this is usually not a connection problem. Symptoms The Maya window shows Not Responding and process CPU is near 0%, meaning it waits rather than computes. --ping connects to the port but does not reply, or commands time out. The backend health check shows in_flight.wedged = true with the current command not returned and no modal dialog present. Causes A slow operation runs synchronously on the main thread: launching a front end, cleaning sessions, a long render or repeated sleep . QApplication.processEvents() is called nested on the Maya main thread, causing event reentrancy and mutual waiting. The command itself never returns, and the bridge only replies once it does. Fixes Check the Maya window for a modal dialog first; dismiss it and retry a read-only query. Never rerun a destructive command because of one timeout; check late results first to see whether it already finished. Use python maya_bridge.py --doctor to distinguish a real hang from a dialog blocking the thread. Only after confirming a hang with no other option decide whether to force-kill Maya; unsaved scenes are lost. Prevention: run long jobs as async work, report progress(...) inside loops and check if cancelled(): break ; never write your own processEvents() loop on the main thread. If it still fails After force-killing Maya, relaunch as described in "Recovering after a crash". Auto-save only protects scenes that were already saved, and flush-to-disk has not been observed under programmatic control, so never treat it as the only safety net.

items.title: Recovering after a crash
synonyms: how to start after a crash
items.summary: After a Maya crash the port often still shows LISTENING, but that is usually a leftover process or the crash reporter; run a health check first and then decide
items.text: After a Maya crash the port often still shows LISTENING, but that is usually a leftover process or the crash reporter; run a health check first and then decide whether to clean up or relaunch. Symptoms The Maya window is gone, or clients still cannot connect after a restart. netstat shows the port listening, yet --ping is refused or times out. A freshly started Maya runs on 7110 instead of the default 7001 . A new MayaCrashLog<date>.<time>.dmp appears in %TEMP% . Steps Look at the Maya window first : for a crash-recovery or unsaved-changes dialog, dismissing it can rescue the unsaved scene, so do not rush to kill the process. Run python maya_bridge.py --doctor to see each port's listening, answering, PID and verdict. Once it is confirmed to be "listening but not answering", run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --kill-hung , which clears only hung instances and leaves healthy ones alone. With no usable instance run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --launch , which starts Maya and waits until it really answers. Finish by confirming the online versions and scenes with --scan / --ping ; to pin a client to one port set SQUIRREL_MAYA_PORT=7110 . Decide from the leftover render processes listed by --doctor ( mayabatch / Render / kick / oiiotool ) whether any must be ended. Verify the result --ping returns version | scene , --doctor marks the target port healthy, and no new crash dumps appear. Tips and warnings There is no resident supervisor process, so Maya is not started automatically when nobody is running a task. --retry-if-crashed only works for idempotent or read-only tasks; a task declaring SQ_DESTRUCTIVE = True is refused. Auto-save only protects scenes already saved to disk, and whether it flushes under programmatic control without human interaction is unverified, so save important scenes by hand first.

items.title: Renderer crashes
synonyms: crashes as soon as it renders
items.summary: Maya exiting during rendering is usually not Maya's own fault: the renderer core crashed and took Maya with it. Symptoms The Maya process disappears once render
items.text: Maya exiting during rendering is usually not Maya's own fault: the renderer core crashed and took Maya with it. Symptoms The Maya process disappears once rendering starts, with no chance for the interface to report an error. The Windows event log names the renderer's own dll as the faulty module, for example redshift-core-vc140.dll or vray_*.dll . The same error offset repeats and a matching MayaCrashLog*.dmp exists in %TEMP% . After the crash the port is often still held by the crash reporter, appearing as "online but not answering". Causes The known Redshift path: cmds.render ends up in rsRender -render , which is asynchronous without -blk ; a second render in the same Maya process collides with the cleanup of the previous one and crashes in redshift-core-vc140.dll ( 0xc0000005 , offset 0xf77c1f ). Version defects in the renderer itself or GPU driver problems can also crash inside the renderer dll. Fixes Use the plug-in's blocking channel rsRender -render -blk for Redshift thumbnails and grab the Render View, never falling back to cmds.render . For complete isolation use out-of-process Render.exe : Redshift and V-Ray must use it in mayapy standalone too, because standalone cmds.render ignores the current renderer. Never run several in-process Redshift renders in a row in one session; use headless batch rendering for bulk work. Do not hot-reload plug-in modules before rendering; doing so has reproduced the same-signature crash. After a crash, clean up leftover processes and ports as described in "Recovering after a crash", then reload the scene. Verify the result Repeated renders no longer crash, no new same-signature dumps appear in %TEMP% , and the event log stops showing the same module and offset. If it still fails Record the faulty module, exception code and offset from the event log plus the newest dump path, and report them with the renderer version; switch to out-of-process Render.exe to keep producing images meanwhile.

items.title: Modal dialogs holding the thread
items.summary: A modal dialog holds the Maya main thread and makes every remote command wait as well; it looks much like a hang, but dismissing the dialog restores everything.
items.text: A modal dialog holds the Maya main thread and makes every remote command wait as well; it looks much like a hang, but dismissing the dialog restores everything. Symptoms Commands time out for no clear reason while the Maya process is alive and the port still connects. --ping takes very long, or the next command times out right after a reply. The Maya window shows a pending dialog: save prompt, license notice, Arnold error, crash-recovery box and so on. Cause A modal dialog enters its own event loop and occupies the main thread, so remote code only runs once it closes; this is not a bridge or port failure. Fixes Call maya_modal_probe (read-only), which returns active_modal , modals and a summary you can relay directly. Switch to the Maya window based on the reply and decide by hand, then dismiss the dialog. After dismissing it, run a read-only query again to confirm the main thread recovered. When the dialog asks whether to save, decide to save or discard before continuing. Verify the result maya_modal_probe no longer reports an active modal, --ping replies normally and later commands return within the expected time. Tips and warnings The probe is read-only: it never clicks or closes anything, because whether to save is the user's decision. Never force-close dialogs with a script; read the content first so no data is lost. If it still times out after dismissing the dialog, continue with "Main thread hangs".

items.title: Opening and saving
items.summary: Settings open from the gear button in the plug-in main window toolbar, and changes reach the disk only after clicking 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) . Prerequisites
items.text: Settings open from the gear button in the plug-in main window toolbar, and changes reach the disk only after clicking 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) . Prerequisites The plug-in main window is open (either the in-Maya version or the standalone edition). Steps Click the gear button on the right of the main window toolbar; its tooltip reads 「设置（AI / 字号 / 语言 / 资产库…）」 (settings: AI / font size / language / asset library…) . Choose a page in the left navigation of the Settings window: General, AI settings, Export defaults, Context menu, Supported formats, Texture suffixes, Sub-libraries and categories, Other configuration, License activation, About. The tabs are stacked vertically on the left (long English labels would not fit across the top). Change what you need. Click 「应用」 (Apply) to save without closing, 「确定」 (OK) to save and close, or 「取消」 (Cancel) to close without saving. At any time click 「设置帮助」 (Settings help) (the orange question mark icon) at the bottom to open the built-in settings help page. Apart from General, AI settings, License activation and About, the other tabs are read-only by default; to change them check 「解锁全部配置」 (Unlock all configuration) at the bottom and confirm the warning first. Saving semantics 「应用」 (Apply) collects per tab: General and AI preferences go to ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/app_settings.json ; asset library, format and sub-library settings go to Assets/preset/config.json inside the plug-in package; export defaults, context menu, double-click commands and texture aliases each write their own preset file. Some settings apply immediately after applying: color theme, language, default library switch, drag-and-drop toggle, bridge port toggle. Font size and interface scaling rebuild the main window style after applying; the thumbnail output size takes effect from the next generation or capture. The Settings window is a non-modal singleton: clicking the gear while it is open only brings the existing window forward. Verify the result Close and reopen Settings and the values you changed are still there. The main window's font size, color theme, language or view changes as expected. To confirm writing to disk, check the modification time of app_settings.json listed on the configuration file locations page. Tips Tip : 「恢复默认设置」 (Restore default settings) at the bottom only resets some items in the current dialog; see "Restoring defaults". Tip : to back up, move to another machine or restore factory settings, use save / import / export / restore in Settings → 常规 → 设置预设 (General → Settings preset) ; see 15.9.2 . Tip : clicking Apply while unlocked opens one more confirmation; choosing No saves nothing. Tip : installing and mounting inside the 「外部 AI 工具」 (External AI tools) panel writes to the other tool's directory immediately and is unrelated to this window's Cancel.

items.title: Restoring defaults
items.summary: 「恢复默认设置」 (Restore default settings) puts most editable items in the Settings window back to factory values, but it writes nothing immediately and never deletes
items.text: 「恢复默认设置」 (Restore default settings) puts most editable items in the Settings window back to factory values, but it writes nothing immediately and never deletes library files. Prerequisites The Settings window is open and no unsaved change needs keeping. Steps Click 「恢复默认设置」 (Restore default settings) at the bottom left of the window. Click 「是」 (Yes) in the confirmation 「确定要恢复所有设置到默认值吗？（config.json 将被重置）」 (restore all settings to defaults? config.json will be reset) . Check the reset items and re-apply whatever must be kept. Click 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) to write to disk. Items that are reset Item Restored to Font size 13 Interface scaling Automatic Scaling anchor Follow system scaling Default view Icon grid Duplicate name handling Auto rename Texture suffixes Reread pbr_mapping.json Other configuration Factory geometry / image extensions and material node type list Export defaults Reread export_preset.json Context menu Reread context_menu_preset.json Items that are not reset The library list, default library and library paths. Texture import policy and dependency file import policy. The supported format list asset_file_extensions . The global model, API keys, AI chat surface, external connection and external AI tools. Interface language, appearance theme, drag-and-drop snapping and thumbnail output size. License state. Want a "factory reset"? Use "restore preset" The button above only resets some controls and writes nothing until you apply. To restore the whole set of interface preferences to a freshly installed state, use: Settings → 常规 (General) → 设置预设 (Settings preset) → 还原预设 (Restore preset) Item Behavior Scope Every interface preference in app_settings.json : font size, scaling, language, theme, default view, thumbnail size, AI model configuration, all toggles When it takes effect Writes to disk and applies immediately after confirmation; the Settings window closes itself afterwards Kept API keys, the library list / default library, license state Not reset Assets\preset\*.json (export defaults / context menu / double-click commands / texture suffixes / sub-libraries and categories) — restore those on their own tabs Preset file The local settings_preset.json is not deleted and can still be restored later with 「导入预设」 (Import preset) 警告 Importing or restoring a preset rewrites settings on disk directly and closes the Settings window . That prevents stale control values from overwriting the result when you click OK — reopen Settings to see the new values. Verify the result After clicking Apply and reopening Settings, the values in the table above are factory values. The asset library is still in place and the main window browses normally. After 「还原预设」 (Restore preset) the language, theme and font size change immediately; a few items such as the language need a plug-in restart to apply fully. Tips Warning : the confirmation says config.json will be reset, but in practice only the items collected by the current dialog are written back; preset files such as export_preset.json are not rewritten with factory values. Tip : to also bring Assets\preset\*.json back to a clean state, back them up first and then delete the matching keys, as described in "Reset"; for interface preferences themselves 「还原预设」 (Restore preset) is enough.

items.title: Configuration file locations
items.summary: The plug-in's settings are split between the user directory and the preset directory of the plug-in package; know which is which before editing. File overview F
items.text: The plug-in's settings are split between the user directory and the preset directory of the plug-in package; know which is which before editing. File overview File Location Main contents app_settings.json ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/app_settings.json Font size, scaling, theme, language, view, library list and default library, AI provider and keys, bridge toggle, chat surface location, external tool choice settings_preset.json ~/.squirrel_asset_manager/settings_preset.json A snapshot of all interface preferences saved by General → Settings preset ; used for import / export / restore (absent means no preset has been saved) config.json <plug-in package>/Assets/preset/config.json Sub-libraries and default categories, supported formats, texture suffixes, duplicate name policy, texture / dependency import policies, material presets export_preset.json <plug-in package>/Assets/preset/export_preset.json Default export formats per asset type, linked files and materials-only context_menu_preset.json Same directory Context menu item toggles per sub-library double_click_preset.json Same directory Double-click commands and import sub-options per sub-library pbr_mapping.json Same directory PBR texture type aliases library.json Each asset library root Library version, name and sub-library list FolderMetadata.fdata Each sub-library directory Sub-library or category id, name and type <plug-in package> means the squirrel_asset_manager directory and ~ the current Windows user directory. How to find them Decide which kind of setting it is: interface preferences and the library list live in app_settings.json , everything else in Assets/preset/ . Type %USERPROFILE%\.squirrel_asset_manager in the Explorer address bar to open the personal configuration directory directly. Preset files travel with the plug-in package; confirm which package is actually loaded before editing. Editing and backing up Prefer the Settings window over hand-editing JSON. Copy to a same-named .bak before manual edits; restart the plug-in afterwards to verify. When app_settings.json fails to load or its JSON is corrupt, defaults are used and the original is backed up as .bak or .corrupt_<timestamp> . bridge_port.log and bridge_recover.log also appear in the same directory, for diagnosing bridge ports and disconnect recovery. settings_preset.json is the local copy of "settings preset": to back up all interface preferences, generating a JSON with 「导出预设」 (Export preset) in the Settings window is safer. Verify the result After changing any setting and clicking Apply the matching file's modification time updates. Settings survive a plug-in restart. Tips Warning : config.json and the preset files live inside the plug-in package, so back them up before reinstalling or overwriting the plug-in. Tip : API keys in app_settings.json are stored as plain JSON, so never send that file to anyone.

items.title: Font size
items.summary: Font size is the base size of the plug-in interface, and all text and icons scale from it. Effect It adjusts the text size in plug-in windows and acts as the ba
items.text: Font size is the base size of the plug-in interface, and all text and icons scale from it. Effect It adjusts the text size in plug-in windows and acts as the base for the 「有效字号」 (effective font size) calculation. Values and default The slider ranges from 10 to 24, with 13 as the default. To the right of the slider the current base value and the effective font size are shown: effective = base × interface scaling. For example a base of 13 with 150% interface scaling gives an effective size of about 20 px. Scope Text in the main window, the Settings window and all dialogs; icons scale proportionally from the 13 px base. After a change the main window resets its style and recomputes its minimum size, and the Settings window re-fits the screen. Only the plug-in's own interface is affected, never Maya's native menus and toolbars. It applies after 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) ; no plug-in restart is needed. When to change it On a small or high-resolution screen where the default text is hard to read, raise the base font size first. To enlarge the whole interface including spacing and icons, prefer 「界面缩放」 (Interface scaling) ; the two can combine. A base of 24 plus high scaling makes windows very large; content scrolls, but adjusting the scaling step is usually better. Tips Tip : if some text still looks small after the change, first check whether 「界面缩放」 (Interface scaling) is set to 「自动」 (Automatic) . Tip : font size and appearance theme are independent and can be set separately.

items.title: Interface scaling and anchor
items.summary: Interface scaling decides how much everything is enlarged on top of the base font size; the anchor only decides which DPI basis the Automatic step uses. Effect
items.text: Interface scaling decides how much everything is enlarged on top of the base font size; the anchor only decides which DPI basis the Automatic step uses. Effect It uniformly enlarges the plug-in interface's text, icons and spacing to fit different resolutions and system scaling. Values and defaults Interface scaling: Automatic (default), 100%, 125%, 150%, 175%, 200%. Scaling anchor: Follow system scaling (default) or follow pixel density. The anchor only works in the Automatic step and is greyed out for manual steps. Automatic rules: when the system scaling is already reflected in Qt's device pixel ratio (above 1.05) no extra enlargement happens; otherwise Follow system scaling uses logical DPI ÷ 96 and Follow pixel density uses physical DPI ÷ 96, clamped to 1.0–2.0. Scope Effective font size = base font size × scale factor; icons, dialogs and toolbars follow. When the scaling step changes the main window resizes by the old and new ratios so content is not squeezed out. Only the plug-in interface is affected, never Maya's own interface or viewport display. It applies after 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) ; no restart is needed. When to change it On a high-DPI screen where the interface is too small: try Automatic first, then a fixed step if that is still not right. To match system scaling like Photoshop or a browser: choose Follow system scaling as the anchor. A high-DPI screen with 100% system scaling that should feel larger: choose Follow pixel density as the anchor. With a manual step the anchor plays no part in the calculation. Tips Tip : font size and scaling multiply, so the 「有效字号」 (effective font size) next to the slider is the clearest guide. Tip : with scaling too high a window can exceed the screen; lower the base font size before picking a step.

items.title: Default view
items.summary: The default view decides whether the asset browser presents assets as an icon grid or as a list. Effect It sets the display mode used when the library opens and
items.text: The default view decides whether the asset browser presents assets as an icon grid or as a list. Effect It sets the display mode used when the library opens and when switching categories. Values and defaults Icon grid (default): thumbnails in a grid, good for finding assets by appearance. List view: rows of asset information, good for checking fields such as name and type. Scope After clicking 「应用」 (Apply) the main window switches immediately and remembers the choice as the default. It only changes the presentation and never the filtering, sorting or selection logic. Thumbnail size in the grid is controlled by the toolbar's thumbnail slider and is unrelated to this item. It also does not affect the command run when double-clicking an asset. When to change it Use the icon grid when there are many assets and thumbnails should be browsed quickly. Use list view when checking names, categories or tags one by one. Tips Tip : switching the view never rescans the library; the current category and filters stay as they are. Tip : to change double-click behavior, see "Choosing a command per sub-library".

items.title: Drag-and-drop snapping
items.summary: When on, dragging a model, dynamics, scene or light into the Maya viewport snaps the asset to the model surface under the cursor and aligns it to the normal. Ef
items.text: When on, dragging a model, dynamics, scene or light into the Maya viewport snaps the asset to the model surface under the cursor and aligns it to the normal. Effect It makes a dropped asset land on a visible surface in the viewport instead of returning to its original coordinates. Values and default The checkbox 「拖入资产（模型 / 动态 / 场景 / 灯光）时吸附到场景表面」 (snap assets dragged into the scene onto the surface) is on by default. Scope For models, dynamics and scenes: the asset's up axis (+Y) aligns with the surface normal and its bottom edge touches the drop point. For lights: the light direction (−Z) aligns with the surface normal, shining outward from the surface with its back against it. With several assets dropped together they line up along the surface; when the rules differ they import at their original positions. It only applies to the models, dynamics, scenes and lights sub-libraries; material, texture and HDR drop semantics are unaffected. When off, assets import at their original position, restoring the previous behavior. When to change it Keep it on to place assets quickly onto an existing model surface. Turn it off for assets with complex transforms that must return to their original coordinates, or when no surface is available. The setting is read at the next drag, so applying is enough and no restart is needed. Tips Tip : snapping needs an actual model face under the cursor; dropping over empty space falls back to the original position. Tip : for more detail on drop points and rotation rules see "Snap to the surface".

items.title: Interface language
items.summary: The interface language switches the plug-in's own Chinese / English display and never affects asset names, tags or the Maya interface. Effect It chooses the lan
items.text: The interface language switches the plug-in's own Chinese / English display and never affects asset names, tags or the Maya interface. Effect It chooses the language of plug-in windows, menus and messages. Values and default Follow system (default), Chinese, English. The field is labelled Language / 语言 . Scope After 「应用」 (Apply) the i18n switches immediately and the category tree rebuilds the display names of built-in categories in the new language. The window shows 「设置已保存。请重启插件以完全生效。」 (settings saved; restart the plug-in for full effect.) Most main-window text unifies after a plug-in restart. It never translates user data such as asset names, Chinese names or tags, and never changes Maya's native interface. The setting is stored under the language key in app_settings.json . When to change it When a team uses the English interface, or to compare against English documentation. If some windows still show the old language, restart the plug-in and check again. Tips Tip : language and appearance theme are independent settings; switching language never changes colors. Tip : the category tree updates immediately, but open dialogs usually need to be reopened to change language.

items.title: Appearance theme
items.summary: The appearance theme switches the plug-in interface between dark and light colors and only affects plug-in windows. Effect It chooses the color scheme used by t
items.text: The appearance theme switches the plug-in interface between dark and light colors and only affects plug-in windows. Effect It chooses the color scheme used by the plug-in main window and dialogs. Values and default Dark (default), Light. Scope After 「应用」 (Apply) the main window immediately rebinds color tokens, rebuilds the style sheet and re-renders icons. Backgrounds, text, borders, buttons and status colors all switch together; colored icons in toolbars and menus are re-tinted for the new background. Dialogs opened afterwards use the new colors. It never affects Maya's native interface, the viewport background or render results, and never changes icon shapes or layout. It is stored under the theme key in app_settings.json . When to change it Light reads better in a bright office; keep dark for dim rooms or night work. Switch when colors should match screenshots or a presentation. Sticking with one theme is fine; frequent switching never affects asset data. Verify the result The main window's background and text colors change immediately, and newly opened dialogs match the main window. Closing and reopening Settings still shows the chosen value in the theme dropdown. Tips Tip : if a window that is already open still shows the old colors, reopen it. Tip : switching the theme never changes font size or interface scaling.

items.title: Thumbnail output size
items.summary: The thumbnail output size is the default edge length shared by generated and captured thumbnails; it decides sharpness as well as render time and file size. Eff
items.text: The thumbnail output size is the default edge length shared by generated and captured thumbnails; it decides sharpness as well as render time and file size. Effect It unifies the square edge length used by default for headless renders, AI thumbnail shots, export screenshots and the screenshot tool. Values and default 256 × 256, 384 × 384, 512 × 512 (default), 768 × 768, 1024 × 1024. When the settings file holds a value off the list, the dropdown shows an extra 「自定义」 (Custom) entry keeping that value. It is clamped to 64–4096 pixels when read. Scope Generation side: headless offscreen rendering, AI thumbnail shots, playblast and render thumbnails on export, and the thumbnail cap for ingesting external files and PBR imports. Capture side: the initial width × height of the screenshot tool and the long edge of preview-panel quick captures. Quick tools (HDR / model / PBR to .zasset ) also follow it. It never decides how large thumbnails appear in the main grid; the toolbar slider does that. It applies from the next generation or capture after 「应用」 (Apply) ; no restart is needed. When to change it Raise it for sharper asset covers, at the cost of headless render time and file size. Lower it when batch output needs speed or disk space is tight. 512 balances sharpness and cost, so the default suits most cases. Tips Tip : raising it never redoes existing thumbnails; regenerate or recapture them. Tip : headless rendering and the screenshot tool share this one value, so do not change it in only one dialog.

items.title: Permanent delete (high-risk switch)
synonyms: why is permanent delete greyed out
items.summary: In one line: a safety catch that is off by default — once enabled, 「彻底删除」 (Delete permanently) in the context menu works, and deleted files vanish immediately w
items.text: In one line: a safety catch that is off by default — once enabled, 「彻底删除」 (Delete permanently) in the context menu works, and deleted files vanish immediately without entering the recycle bin and cannot be restored. Where it is Settings window → General page → the 「彻底删除」 (Permanent delete) group (between "Appearance" and "Thumbnails (resolution)"). While it is off (default) 「彻底删除」 (Delete permanently) in the asset / category / version context menus is greyed out , and clicking it suggests enabling it in settings; Deletion only offers "move to recycle bin": files stay in the library and can be restored ; The recycle bin is limited to 100 GB, and when full you must permanently delete items inside it (see 15.8.3 ). Steps to enable it Check 「启用「彻底删除」（直接删除文件，不进回收站）」 (enable permanent delete, removing files directly without the recycle bin) ; Clicking 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) opens a second confirmation stating that files are removed directly, do not enter the recycle bin and cannot be restored; It takes effect immediately after confirming; back in the asset grid, 「彻底删除」 (Delete permanently) is no longer greyed out. Enabling and disabling both write an audit log ( setting / permanent_delete_enabled , marked irreversible) so the change can be traced later. Once it is on Action Behavior Delete → move to recycle bin As before: goes to the recycle bin and can be restored Delete → delete permanently Deletes the files on disk , skips the recycle bin; the confirmation says "cannot be restored"; there is no undo AI-side asset deletion Controlled separately by 「允许 AI 删除 / 覆盖替换资产」 (allow AI to delete or overwrite assets) in AI settings and unrelated to this switch (see 11.4.6 ) 警告 Permanent delete keeps no backup, skips the recycle bin and cannot be undone. Keep this switch off for day-to-day work; enable it temporarily only when space must really be freed and the library is backed up. See 4.12.4 for backups. Common questions Symptom Cause / fix 「彻底删除」 (Delete permanently) is greyed out This switch is off by default; enable it in settings After deleting, the recycle bin is empty You used delete permanently; only "move to recycle bin" goes to the recycle bin Want AI to delete assets too That is another switch: AI settings → AI / MCP 通道 (AI / MCP channel) → allow AI to delete or overwrite assets Related Recycle bin view and context menu → 15.8.3 Batch delete → 4.8.2 AI / MCP channel (including the AI destructive-action switch) → 11.4.6 Other settings on the General page → 11.2.1

items.title: Managing the library list
items.summary: Library list management is where asset libraries are added, created and removed, and where the default library loaded at startup is chosen. Prerequisites The 「资
items.text: Library list management is where asset libraries are added, created and removed, and where the default library loaded at startup is chosen. Prerequisites The 「资产库管理」 (Asset library management) group on Settings → 常规 (General) is open. The directory to add is accessible on this machine, and the parent directory is writable when creating a library. Steps Add an existing library: click 「添加资产库」 (Add asset library) , choose the library directory on disk and type a display name (empty uses the folder name). Create a new library: click 「创建资产库」 (Create asset library) , pick a parent directory and type a name (default SquirrelLib ). The plug-in creates the library directory, library.json and the six sub-library directories materials, models, lights, textures, scenes and HDR; the remaining built-in sub-libraries are completed automatically the next time the library loads. Set as default: select an entry and click 「设为默认」 (Set as default) ; a [默认] ([default]) marker appears and the library loads automatically at startup. Delete: select and click 「删除选中」 (Delete selected) . This only removes it from the list, never deletes files on disk, and at least one library must remain. Click 「应用」 (Apply) or 「确定」 (OK) to save. Verify the result The list shows name — path [default] . The main window's library dropdown shows the new library immediately, and it switches automatically when the default changes. Reopening Settings still shows the list and the default marker. Tips Tip : the same path (different slashes or letter case) counts as a duplicate, and adding it reports 「该资产库已在列表中」 (this asset library is already in the list) . Tip : when an empty folder is switched to for the first time, all built-in sub-library directories are completed from the configuration (11 in total: materials, models, lights, textures, scenes, HDR, dynamics, images, audio, animation data, node trees). Warning : deleting a library only changes the list; to really clean the disk, do it yourself in Explorer.

items.title: Duplicate name handling
items.summary: Duplicate name handling decides what happens when exporting an asset whose target location already holds a same-named asset. Effect When exporting or creating a
items.text: Duplicate name handling decides what happens when exporting an asset whose target location already holds a same-named asset. Effect When exporting or creating an asset meets a same-named target, the preset policy is applied so nothing is overwritten by accident. Values and defaults Policy Behavior Ask every time Opens a dialog to choose auto rename, type a new name, or cancel Auto rename Appends _001 , _002 … automatically Manual input Opens an input box for a new name The current preset file defaults to 「自动重命名」 (Auto rename) ( name_conflict_policy.mode = auto_rename ); when that key is missing the interface also falls back to auto rename ( NameConflictDialog.DEFAULT_MODE ), so there is a single default across the whole chain. A choice made under "ask every time" can be remembered with 「记住选择，不再提示」 (remember this choice, do not ask again) , and later exports follow the remembered policy. Scope It only affects the target-already-exists case when creating a new asset; existing assets are never auto-renamed or deleted. Appending a LOD or creating a new version are explicit actions in the export dialog and do not use this policy. It is stored as name_conflict_policy in Assets/preset/config.json . When to change it Use 「自动重命名」 (Auto rename) for batch exports that must not be interrupted. Use 「每次询问」 (Ask every time) when every name should be confirmed. Use 「手动输入」 (Manual input) with a fixed naming convention that needs human naming. Tips Tip : auto renaming only changes the new asset's name and never touches existing assets. Tip : the policy is written to the preset file after clicking 「应用」 (Apply) and applies from the next export.

items.title: Texture import policy
items.summary: The texture import policy decides where textures are read from and whether they are copied into the project when importing materials or textures from the librar
items.text: The texture import policy decides where textures are read from and whether they are copied into the project when importing materials or textures from the library. Effect It controls where textures under textures/ inside a .zasset end up in Maya.
