Use mode=keyword when you need a purely literal match, and mode=semantic when investigating semantic recall. Verify the result The target asset enters the top three, match shows semantic or both , and newly added tags and Chinese names can be found. If it still fails Record the query, the target asset name and the actual top five results to see whether recall or ranking is the problem. If results are still off right after a rebuild, confirm the model matches the index and no old index directory is mixed in. For ambiguous queries, add qualifiers such as material, color or purpose and compare the results again. Continue with 4.5.9.3 "Irrelevant search results" and 4.5.6.4 "Incremental and full sync".

items.title: Slow startup
items.summary: The plug-in shows the window first and loads the asset library in the background, so slow startup is usually slow library scanning, index cache or disk reads, n
items.text: The plug-in shows the window first and loads the asset library in the background, so slow startup is usually slow library scanning, index cache or disk reads, not UI construction. Symptoms The window appears quickly, but a loading indicator stays in the middle while the category tree and thumbnails take a long time. The first launch is clearly slower than the second. One particular library is very slow while the others are fine. The asset count in the status bar does not update for a long time, but Maya itself is not frozen. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action The asset library is very large Thousands of assets; scan time grows with the count Split into several libraries, or reduce the asset count per library No index cache on the first launch .squirrel_index_cache.json does not exist under the library root yet Wait for the first scan; the second launch hits the cache The library is on a network or sync drive The directory is on a NAS, cloud drive or auto-sync folder Move the library to a local disk Index cache incompatible with the current version The log says "index cache incompatible, falling back to a full scan" Clear the cache and let it rebuild once The first read of many asset descriptions The first sync after a restart reads many meta.json files Wait for it to finish in the background; the description cache is used afterwards Many thumbnails loading at once The first screen decodes many images simultaneously Wait for async loading, or reduce the number on the first screen The AI index warms up in the background The status shows warming up Warm-up does not block search; just wait for it Steps Check whether the window has appeared, then decide whether the UI or the data loading is slow. Look at the [MaterialManager] log in the Script Editor to see whether it hit the cache or is doing a full scan. Move the asset library to a local disk; avoid network drives and real-time sync folders. On the first launch wait for the scan to finish, confirm .squirrel_index_cache.json was created, then restart and compare the second run. For a broken cache, clear it with library_health op=clear_cache and let it rebuild once. When there are too many assets, split by sub-library or project to reduce the scale of each load. Verify the result The second launch is clearly faster than the first, the category tree and first-screen thumbnails appear shortly after the window opens, and the status bar count is correct. If it still fails Record the library's asset count, disk type (local/network), and cold and warm startup times. Compare with an empty library; if an empty library is also slow, the bottleneck is not asset scanning. Check whether several Maya instances load the same library at once, or sync software is scanning the library directory. Continue with 6.6.2 "Stuttering and memory" and 4.1.12.2 "Index rebuild".

items.title: Stuttering and memory
items.summary: When Maya shows "not responding" with CPU near 0%, it is usually waiting for a main-thread task to return rather than lacking compute; first decide whether it i
items.text: When Maya shows "not responding" with CPU near 0%, it is usually waiting for a main-thread task to return rather than lacking compute; first decide whether it is frozen or waiting. Symptoms The UI shows "not responding" while Maya's CPU usage in Task Manager is near 0%. Opening the AI panel or switching libraries takes tens of seconds. Consecutive thumbnail renders get slower and slower, eventually crashing. Memory keeps climbing and does not drop noticeably after closing the plug-in window. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action A long task runs synchronously on the main thread CPU low, UI frozen, recovers when the task finishes Wait for it, or switch to an async/batch interface A nested event loop on the main thread The UI never returns while CPU stays near 0% Stop such scripts and restart Maya Consecutive renders in the same process The second render starts hanging or crashes See 6.7.3 "Renderer crash" Many thumbnails decoded at once Stuttering while scrolling, disk and memory rising Wait for async loading and reduce the first-screen count The semantic embedding model stays resident Ollama uses hundreds of MB in Task Manager (about 639 MB measured for the 0.6B tier; varies by model) Stop Ollama when semantic search is not needed Index/cache files are large Cache files in the library directory reach several MB Split the library, or rebuild the index Several Maya instances at once Multiple processes load libraries and thumbnails simultaneously Reduce parallel instances Steps Check Task Manager first: CPU near 0% and frozen for a long time means the main thread is waiting; do not keep clicking. Confirm whether a render, batch import/export or AI panel is in progress; do not trigger it again before it finishes. Use async interfaces for batch tasks, provide progress and cancellation checkpoints in long loops, and never spin on the main thread. Scripts and tools must not poll with sleep on the Maya main thread, nor nest processEvents() loops. Load thumbnails and previews in batches; close preview panels you do not need and extra split-instance panels first. If it hangs or crashes after consecutive renders, fully restart Maya instead of hot-reloading the plug-in. Verify the result The UI responds again, tasks complete normally, memory drops after a task ends, and the permanent "not responding" state is gone. If it still fails Record what was running before the hang, how long it lasted, and the CPU/memory usage at the time. Repeat the same operation in an empty scene to rule out scene size or third-party plug-ins. If the bridge or AI panel hangs, use 6.7.1 "Port listens but does not answer" to check whether Maya is really alive. For recovery after a crash, follow 6.7.2 "Three steps to recover after a crash" and keep the crash dump.

items.title: Large batch operations
items.summary: Large batch operations should use batch interfaces or async jobs, and after a timeout you should check the result first instead of rerunning immediately. Sympto
items.text: Large batch operations should use batch interfaces or async jobs, and after a timeout you should check the result first instead of rerunning immediately. Symptoms Progress does not move for a long time during batch import, export or thumbnail generation. The operation timed out, and you are not sure whether the background work is still running. The same batch ran twice, producing duplicate assets or files. One failing asset stalls the whole batch, or the batch results are incomplete. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action Items processed one by one instead of in batch The log handles one item at a time and time grows linearly Use batch commands or multi-select operations Thumbnails rendered sequentially in the main process The Maya UI is occupied and CPU/memory keep rising Switch to headless offscreen batch generation One bad asset blocks the batch The log stops at the same asset Isolate the problem asset, then rerun the rest Resubmitted after a timeout Duplicate results appear for the same batch Check the result of the submitted job before rerunning The output directory is on a network drive Writes are slow or fail on permissions Write to a local disk first, then copy The batch is too large Memory and handles keep growing Split into smaller batches and verify each one Steps Test with 5 to 10 assets first to confirm the workflow, naming and output directory. For thumbnail generation use Update thumbnail → Background render (headless), which runs in a separate mayapy process and does not occupy the current scene. Split export and import by sub-library or category; avoid processing an entire library at once. After submitting an async task, record its job_id and check progress and cancellation interfaces instead of waiting with sleep . After a timeout, check late results and job history first and retry only once you confirm nothing completed. Never rerun a destructive operation just because of one timeout; work through the failure list item by item instead of starting the batch over. Verify the result Batch progress advances normally to completion, the failure list is clear, the asset count matches expectations and no duplicate files exist. If it still fails Record the batch size, start and end times, failing entries and their logs. Run the failing assets separately to see whether it is one asset or the batch scale. Check the output directory's free space, permissions and network connection. Confirm job status per 5.2.4 "Async, progress and cancellation" before deciding to rerun.

items.title: Port listens but does not answer
path: Port listens but does not answer
synonyms: Maya is open but cannot connect
port is taken with no response
items.summary: A port showing LISTENING in netstat does not mean Maya is alive; liveness must be proven by actually dispatching a command and seeing whether it answers. Sympto
items.text: A port showing LISTENING in netstat does not mean Maya is alive; liveness must be proven by actually dispatching a command and seeing whether it answers. Symptoms The tool reports a failed connection or timeout, yet netstat still shows the port listening. --ping returns no version or scene, or the connection is refused ( WinError 10061 ). The Maya window appears open but the UI does not respond, or a dialog is in front of it. A newly started Maya did not take the default port, and the client keeps reporting that it cannot connect. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action The Maya main thread is hung The process exists and the port listens, but commands time out or are refused Confirm, then clean the hung instance A modal dialog blocks the main thread The Maya window shows crash recovery, an error or an unsaved-changes prompt Dismiss the dialog, then retry The crash reporter still holds the port After a crash the port still listens but never answers Follow the crash recovery flow The port moved to the fallback range The default port is taken by an instance of the same version Scan the fallback range 7110–7129 The client only knows a fixed port The actual instance is on a fallback port Use auto-discovery, or set the port environment variable Another process owns the port The port owner is not Maya Change ports, or end the owning process Steps Look at the Maya window first; if a modal dialog is present, dismiss it and probe again. Run python maya_bridge.py --doctor and check listening , responsive and verdict for each port. Run python maya_bridge.py --ping to confirm which Maya and which scene answer. Run python maya_bridge.py --scan to see whether the instance landed in the fallback range 7110–7129. Once you confirm it is hung and not a modal dialog, run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --kill-hung ; it only cleans instances that listen but do not answer. When no instance is available, run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --launch and wait until it really answers. If the client must use a fixed port, set SQUIRREL_MAYA_PORT to the actual port. Verify the result --ping returns "Maya version | current scene", --doctor shows verdict=healthy for that port, and commands round-trip normally. If it still fails Check the latest port assignments in ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\bridge_port.log to see whether it keeps falling back. Look in %TEMP% for a new MayaCrashLog*.dmp to tell a hang from an actual crash. Never kill a process based on netstat alone; healthy instances and the user's work must stay untouched. Continue with 6.7.2 "Three steps to recover after a crash", or collect information per 6.8.2 "Diagnostic workflow".

items.title: Three steps to recover after a crash
path: Three steps to recover after a crash
items.summary: After a crash, follow three steps — diagnose, then clean hung instances or dismiss modal dialogs, then launch and prove it answers. Do not reopen repeatedly or
items.text: After a crash, follow three steps — diagnose, then clean hung instances or dismiss modal dialogs, then launch and prove it answers. Do not reopen repeatedly or kill processes outright. Symptoms Maya suddenly disappears, goes white, or stops responding for a long time. The tool reports a disconnect, and reopening Maya still cannot connect. After a new Maya starts, the client reports a port already in use or a refused connection. The unsaved scene from before the crash cannot be found. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action The Maya process already crashed The process is gone and %TEMP% has a new crash dump Recover with the three steps The main thread is hung The process exists and the port listens, but nothing answers Confirm, then clean the hung instance A modal dialog blocks it The Maya window shows a recovery, error or unsaved prompt Dismiss the dialog first An old instance holds the default port The new instance fell back to 7110–7129 Scan the fallback range and connect to the actual port The renderer or a plug-in took Maya down The event log points at a renderer DLL See 6.7.3 "Renderer crash" The unsaved scene is lost The autosave directory is empty or autosave was off See 6.7.4 "Autosave and recovery" Steps Diagnose: run python maya_bridge.py --doctor . It only reports who is online, who is hung and what should be cleaned. Look at the Maya window first; dismiss any modal dialog and run --doctor again. Once you confirm it is hung rather than a dialog, run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --kill-hung . Launch: run python maya_bridge.py --doctor --launch , which waits until Maya really answers instead of just checking that the process started. Confirm at the end: run python maya_bridge.py --ping or --scan to confirm the version, scene and actual port. If a task must be resubmitted, only use --retry-if-crashed for idempotent or read-only tasks; when the task file declares SQ_DESTRUCTIVE = True , the tool refuses to resubmit automatically. To recover unsaved content, check the autosave directory and %TEMP%\squirrel_pre_render\ ; copy the files out before opening them. Verify the result --doctor reports a usable healthy_port , --ping returns the Maya version and current scene, and new tasks run normally. If it still fails Do not keep launching more Maya instances; first check whether the old instance still holds the port. Check ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\bridge_port.log and bridge_recover.log for port changes and self-heal records. For crash forensics, check the Windows event log (module name + offset) and %TEMP%\MayaCrashLog*.dmp . Never rerun destructive tasks just because of one disconnect; check late results and job history first.

items.title: Renderer crash
items.summary: A crash inside renderer modules such as redshift-core-*.dll or vray_*.dll means the renderer itself crashed and took Maya with it; switch to out-of-process rend
items.text: A crash inside renderer modules such as redshift-core-*.dll or vray_*.dll means the renderer itself crashed and took Maya with it; switch to out-of-process rendering and confirm the fix is actually in effect. Symptoms Maya disappears as soon as you render or use Update thumbnail → Render image . The second render in the same process always crashes while the first one works. The Windows event log shows the same DLL at the same fault offset. A new MayaCrashLog*.dmp appears in %TEMP% , and after the crash the port may still be held by the crash reporter. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action Redshift's second in-process render The first works, the second always crashes Upgrade to a build with the blocking-render fix and restart Maya The deployed copy was not updated Source changed but Maya still runs old code Redeploy and fully restart Maya Redshift version or license problem The log shows a license error Check the license; roll back or reinstall the renderer if needed Another renderer's own DLL crashes The event log points at vray_*.dll and similar Switch to out-of-process Render.exe The crash reporter holds the port The port still listens but commands do not answer Handle it per 6.7.1 "Port listens but does not answer" Retrying in-process over and over Every retry produces a new crash Stop retrying and use the out-of-process channel Steps Confirm the plug-in is upgraded to a build containing the Redshift blocking-render fix, then fully quit and restart Maya; a hot reload does not count. Do 2 to 4 thumbnail renders in a row and confirm it no longer crashes on the second. If it still crashes, set the environment variable SQUIRREL_MAYA_RENDER_VIA_EXE=1 to use out-of-process Render.exe . It is slower, but a renderer crash no longer takes Maya down. Check the Redshift version and license status; if the log shows a license error, fix the license first. Record the crash module name and offset with Event Viewer and keep the matching crash dump. Do not retry the same render path repeatedly inside one Maya process, which only produces more crash dumps. Verify the result Four thumbnail renders in a row all produce images, Maya stays open, and %TEMP% gains no new crash dump with the same signature. If it still fails Reproduce in a clean Maya instance or a minimal scene to see whether scene content is involved. Collect the event log, crash dump, Redshift version and license status before reporting. Temporarily switch to playblast or imported images for thumbnails so asset organization is not blocked. Whether the AI per-frame render command also uses the blocking path is still unconfirmed; validate with a small batch before rendering at scale.

items.title: Autosave and recovery
synonyms: cannot find the file after a crash
items.summary: Maya's autosave is off by default; you must enable it and write it into the preferences. It only protects scenes that have been saved to disk at least once. Sym
items.text: Maya's autosave is off by default; you must enable it and write it into the preferences. It only protects scenes that have been saved to disk at least once. Symptoms After a crash there is no autosave file and the autosave directory is empty. Restarting Maya shows no crash recovery prompt. A crashed new scene cannot be recovered at all. Autosave was enabled, but the setting is off again after a crash. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action Autosave is not enabled autoSaveEnable is 0 Enable it and save preferences It was only enabled for the session The setting is lost after a crash Write it into prefs\userPrefs.mel The new scene was never saved The scene has no file name, so no autosave name can be derived Press Ctrl+S first to give it a location The interval is too long About 10 minutes by default Shorten the interval and save manually before important operations The backup count hit its limit autoSaveMaxBackups is about 10 and old files rotate out Save important versions explicitly in time Program-driven with no human interaction No autosave files were observed on disk (unverified) Verify the directory when the scene is used interactively Steps Enable autosave in the Maya preferences, set the interval to 10 minutes or less, and save the preferences. Confirm the setting is written to prefs\userPrefs.mel rather than only the current session; back up the file before editing it. After creating a new scene, press Ctrl+S once so autosave has a file name to work with. After a crash, look in Documents\maya\projects\default\autosave for autosave files. Once found, copy the file to another directory first and open the copy, so recovery does not overwrite the original. Backups taken before thumbnail rendering live in %TEMP%\squirrel_pre_render\ and keep 3 copies by default; set SQUIRREL_PRE_RENDER_BACKUP=0 to turn them off. Verify the result The autosave directory gains a timestamped file whose content matches the pre-crash scene, and the autosave settings are visible in userPrefs.mel . If it still fails Temporarily set the autosave interval to 1 minute, work normally for a while, then check whether files land in the directory. Confirm the scene really was saved to disk; an untitled new scene never produces an autosave. Autosave files can also be overwritten or rotated out, so save versions manually before important steps. Investigate the crash itself per 6.7.2 "Three steps to recover after a crash" or 6.7.3 "Renderer crash".

items.title: Log locations
items.summary: The plug-in has no central log hub; most diagnostic output goes to the Maya Script Editor, and you then look in the matching directory by problem type. Symptoms
items.text: The plug-in has no central log hub; most diagnostic output goes to the Maya Script Editor, and you then look in the matching directory by problem type. Symptoms You want to report a problem but do not know which file to attach. The Script Editor only shows part of the output, and the record disappears after a restart. Crashes, bridging and AI installation each leave a pile of logs and you cannot tell which is relevant. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action Only the UI message was read The UI shows one line while the full error is in the Script Editor Open the Script Editor and reproduce once Logs are split by feature Bridging, AI installation and headless jobs each have their own files Find the matching file in the table below Logs were rotated or cleaned The directory only holds the last few runs Copy them immediately after reproducing The crash left no time to write logs The process exited outright Check the crash dump and the Windows event log Common log locations Location Content Maya Script Editor Main output and tracebacks for plug-in runtime, import/export, rendering and material conversion ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\bridge_port.log commandPort port assignment, conflicts and fallback ports ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\bridge_recover.log Disconnect self-healing, cleanup, launch and re-dispatch records ~\.squirrel_asset_manager\broker_boot.log Why registering with the AI broker failed at Maya startup <package>\dsh_home\dsh_install.log dsh installation process <package>\dsh_home\broker_daemon.log AI broker process output <package>\dsh_home\squirrel_web_<instance>.log dsh front-end startup output %TEMP%\squirrel_asset_manager\ai_install.log AI dependency installation log %TEMP%\squirrel_standalone_host.log Standalone host startup log worker.log in the headless job working directory Job logs for headless thumbnail generation, format conversion and similar %TEMP%\MayaCrashLog<date>.<time>.dmp Maya crash dump Windows Event Viewer → Application Crash module name, fault offset and exception code %TEMP%\squirrel_pre_render\ Scene backups taken before rendering, not logs dsh_home is the dsh_home directory inside the plug-in package by default; if SQUIRREL_DSH_HOME or DSH_HOME is set, the environment variable wins. Steps Open the Maya Script Editor, clear it, reproduce the problem and copy the full traceback. Locate logs by problem type: bridge_* for bridging, dsh_home for AI, ai_install.log for installation. For crashes, also record the module name and offset from the event log and keep the matching dump. Copy the key snippets into your report instead of just saying "it errored". For long logs keep the beginning, the end and the area around the timestamp, and state when you reproduced it. Verify the result You can state clearly which layer failed and point at the log or dump from the matching time. If it still fails Copy logs right after reproducing so the next launch does not overwrite them. If a directory does not exist, that feature never reached the logging step; go back to the troubleshooting page for that feature. If you are unsure which file to read, work through 6.8.2 "Diagnostic workflow" layer by layer. When submitting feedback, use 6.8.3 "Feedback template" and include log paths and key snippets.

items.title: Diagnostic workflow
items.summary: Work through "symptom → Script Editor → feature status → bridge health → crash forensics" in that order: first decide which layer the problem is in, then dig de
items.text: Work through "symptom → Script Editor → feature status → bridge health → crash forensics" in that order: first decide which layer the problem is in, then dig deeper. Symptoms The symptom is vague and you cannot tell whether it is the UI, asset library, AI, bridging or the renderer. The same symptom can have several causes, and trial and error is expensive. You need to give the maintainer information but do not know what to collect first. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action The full error was never read Only the UI message was seen Reproduce and capture the traceback first The order jumps around Reinstalling now, rebuilding the index next Work layer by layer, one decision per layer Status endpoints were not used No idea of the current library/index/AI state Check feature status first Bridge and Maya state are confused Cannot tell a hung Maya from a client problem Use --doctor and --ping to prove liveness Crash evidence was not preserved Logs and dumps were overwritten Copy them right after reproducing Steps Record the symptom: when it happened, what you were doing, whether it reproduces reliably, and the scope. Open the Script Editor, clear it, reproduce once and copy the start and end of the full traceback. Check feature status by problem type: library_health with op=status for the asset library; asset_semantic_status for search and AI; the dependency check in settings for AI dependencies. For Maya connection, hang or disconnect problems, run python maya_bridge.py --doctor , then use --ping and --scan to confirm instances and ports. For crashes, record the module name and offset from the Windows event log and keep %TEMP%\MayaCrashLog*.dmp . For rendering problems, confirm whether the crash is inside a renderer DLL; use 6.7.3 "Renderer crash" to decide whether out-of-process rendering is needed. If you still cannot locate it, organize the information per 6.8.3 "Feedback template" and submit it. Verify the result You can state clearly which layer failed (UI, asset library, index, bridge, renderer or licensing) and have the matching log or status return in hand. If it still fails Build a minimal reproduction: empty scene, single asset, single operation, to rule out scene and batch factors. Keep copies of logs from before and after the reproduction, not just the last launch. If you are unsure where logs live, look them up item by item per 6.8.1 "Log locations". Include the steps you already tried so the maintainer does not repeat them.

items.title: Feedback template
synonyms: what to write in a bug report
items.summary: A useful report contains the version, reproduction steps, the full error and the relevant logs, ideally with a minimal reproduction asset attached. Symptoms Aft
items.text: A useful report contains the version, reproduction steps, the full error and the relevant logs, ideally with a minimal reproduction asset attached. Symptoms After reporting, you keep having to add information and the problem stays unlocated. The report only says "does not work" or "it errored", with no version, steps or logs. A screenshot was attached, but without the full error text or a timestamp. Possible causes Cause How to tell Action Environment information is missing No Maya version, OS or plug-in version Fill in the template Reproduction steps are incomplete The maintainer cannot reproduce from the description Write numbered steps starting from opening the plug-in The error was truncated Only the last line or a blurry screenshot Attach the full traceback text No logs The failing layer cannot be determined Attach key snippets per 6.8.1 "Log locations" No minimal reproduction Only the whole project is available Provide a minimal scene or a single asset Sensitive information leaked A full license or key was attached Provide only the status and error code Steps Fill in the template below as completely as you can. [Environment] Plug-in version: Maya version: Operating system: Renderer and version: [Problem] One-line description: When it first appeared: Scope (single asset / whole library / all scenes): [Reproduction steps] 1. 2. 3. [Expected result] [Actual result] [Full error] (Paste the Script Editor traceback, keeping the first and last few lines) [Logs] Log path: Key snippets: [Attachments] Screenshots / screen recording: Minimal scene or asset: What you already tried: [Other] Does it reproduce reliably: Does it only happen in one Maya version: Error text takes priority over screenshots; use screenshots to show the UI state. Attach only the relevant log snippets and state their paths and timestamps. You may desensitize assets or scenes, but keep the structure and node types that can trigger the problem. Verify the result The maintainer can reproduce the problem from the report alone, or can tell exactly which layer's logs are needed. If it still fails If unsure what to attach, at least provide the version, reproduction steps, the full error and the --doctor output. For crashes, attach the event log module name and offset and keep the crash dump. Never publish full license files, private keys or credentials containing personal information. Use 6.8.2 "Diagnostic workflow" to locate the failing layer first, then add the matching material.

prefer out-of-process Render.exe for batch rendering docs/2026-10-15-Redshift缩略图崩溃-移交文档.md Synchronous commands have a hard 30-second cap After a timeout the command may still be running on the Maya main thread Run long commands as async jobs; after a timeout check /late_results first and do not rerun destructive commands ai_base/broker.py , ai_base/jobs.py Commands touching host state are strictly serialized on the main thread One long command blocks other commands and status snapshots; only pure query or pure file commands with affinity=any can run in parallel Merge batch operations into one call; use async with checkpoints for long tasks dsh_plugins/skills/squirrel-assets/SKILL.md , ai_base/command_registry.py Semantic search depends on local Ollama and the embedding model Only lexical search is available when the model or index is missing Run the AI dependency check; it degrades to lexical automatically when unavailable docs/2026-10-02-资产库语义检索P0落地.md The English help center is not finished yet Users of the English UI still see Chinese bodies This release ships Chinese first; English pages are reserved with the same id structure docs/2026-10-19-帮助系统重构规划.md Installer v1 is unsigned Windows SmartScreen warns about an unknown publisher SHA256SUMS ships with the package; choose Run anyway AGENTS.md The cp313 artifacts for Maya 2027 were not tested on this machine 2027 compatibility is only a compile target, not machine-verified Compile with build_all_pyd.py --extra-python "py -3.13" and verify yourself AGENTS.md Note : "not observed", "to be confirmed" and "not tested" are kept as written; items.text: 2025 and 2026 share the same Python, so it is compiled only once; Maya loads the matching build automatically.
